leader). `GameWorld::squadTooSmall` (the soldier's `equip` refuses such a
weapon) and `takeSquadSizeRefused`, which main.cpp hands the help
manager. Without a key, c_PIToggleWeapon (input 45) or a press of the
seat's specialToggleWeaponInput (PCO template `+0x46c`, `0x40` none; the
edge of `+0x14c`, `0x005c7f80`) moves each group with an active weapon to
the next of its weapons sorted by item index (`0x004d2010` with
`LAB_004cc640`: the item interface's slot `0x30`), round from the last,
with no selectable test: as_ag's and us_ag's gunners (cannon itemIndex 1,
GuidedMissileWeapon 2, both isSelectable 0) and the hover bike's gunner
switch to their TV missiles on PIAltFire. While the special toggle input
is held it fires nothing (`0x005c69a0` in `0x005c50e0`). toggleWeapon
(template `+0x420`) has its executor and save only: no reader. Each
entry starts every group at its first weapon in the tree's order: the
enter methods (interface `0xc4c5` slot 7, `0x005cdd60`, "<player> enters",
and slot 8, `0x005ce600`) end by setting, for each of the three lists
(`+0x7c`, 16 bytes apart) that has any, its first one active (slot
`0x7c`, which changes nothing for the one already active), so a gunner
who left on the TV missile comes back to the gun (the ghosts' group
indices, `0x00605b00`, take a server's). Rewritten: `SeatLayout::weapons` (`SeatWeapon`: group,
item index, selectable, the per-weapon start, barrels, recoil, toggle
camera, deviation, active defence), `Body::Gun`'s `arms` and `active`,
`GameWorld::selectSeatWeapons`, `activateSeatWeapon`, `fireSeatWeapon`;
`vehicleSeats` gives each seat's selected PIFire weapon as its
`SeatWeapon` part (the HUD's GuiIndex, icons and crosshair, the seat
camera's startCameraId, the camera recoil follow it). The shipped
TV-guided launchers so start the projectile camera. Drivers fire all
three groups (see the drivers' and pilots' guns above). Each entry sets
the groups' first weapons again (`seatPlayer`); a key's pick sets the
player's `seatItemSelect` (`takeSeatItemSelect`), which the HUD turns
into the popup with the seat's PIFire group (`ItemSelection::flash`, a
local round's player; a joined client runs the same pick for its own
control object: its weapon key goes to the server as PIWeaponSelect and,
for a selectable PIFire weapon of that index that our own state's group 0
doesn't already hold, opens the popup there too)
(`Vehicles_SeatItemSelectionAndFirstWeapons`). **Bots** (AIDLL): the seat's armament is its
weapons with a weaponTemplate (the Armament list `0x10075170`); the
targets' loop and the weapon choice (`0x10074ef0`) score them as a kit's,
and the trigger statement presses the chosen one's fire input (the AI
weapon's slot `0x60`, BF2142.exe `0x008927c0`: the fire component's
fireInput; BAPATrigger's button), so a PIAltFire weapon gets PIAltFire.
A PIFire weapon that isn't active is taken first by its key when
selectable, else by c_PIToggleWeapon (a rewrite stand-in: no shipped
gunner seat has two weapons with a weaponTemplate, and the TV missiles
and the ads have none, so bots never use them). `BotManager::seatArmament`.
A driving bot works the root's guns the same way (`BotManager::drivesGun`):
the Tank, FloatingTank, Mech and ArmedCar sets' Fire is BBFireInfantery
(BBPFireInfantery, AIBehaviours.ai, with MouseTurretAimAt and Trigger
among their interpreter entries), and the drivers' ControlInfo aims with
PIMouseLookX / PIMouseLookY (eu_tank_Ctrl −12 / −1, the APCs' −7 / −1,
the mechs' −3 / −3) or, on the hover tank, PIRoll / PIPitch
(as_tank_Ctrl −1.5 / −20 / 0: its aim turns the hull). The sensing view
follows the turret (the Tank set's `addSensingAgentPattern Turret`).

**The vehicle's fire plan** (`0x100795a0` for a bot object with a Mobile
part, from `LAB_10079dde`; soldiers have one too). Its statements name
themselves in their debug printers: If (`0x100d29f0`, vtable
`0x1011a378`: condition, then, else, a forced update `+0x30` and "freeze
false-statement" `+0x31`), the Serial (`0x100ce370`) and Parallell
(`0x100cddb0`) combiners, OR / AND / NOT (`0x100cf1b0`, `0x100d49a0`,
`0x100d2f80`), a shared memo (`0x100d8e40` / `0x100d8f90`),
MoveToObjectFinding (`0x100cff90`, vtable `0x10119e28`), MoveToFinding
(`0x100d11c0`), ObjectDistance (`0x100d44c0`, evaluated by `0x100d4620`),
ForgetObject (`0x100da5f0`: the memory item dropped, `0x100ec400`) and a
failing statement (`0x100da480` with mode 0). In a Parallell combiner:
- the moves: If (forced, frozen) the target isn't in view (NOT the memo
  of the target conditions `0x100dc400` / `0x100dad60`): Serial of
  MoveToObjectFinding at the target with no distance kept, ForgetObject,
  the failing statement (the plan ends); else If (not forced) NOT
  ObjectDistance [minRange, 1.1 D]: MoveToObjectFinding keeping D (the
  plan's distance, below) with its near limit ec = min(1.1 minRange, D),
  at the Mobile maxSpeed and half of it (MoveToFinding to the spot beside
  a target without a Mobile part, at 0.75 of it). The move is done when
  ec ≤ d ≤ D (`0x100cfe20` over the squared distance `0x100f9970`).
  Beyond ec it paths at the target; nearer it backs off (`0x100d00e0`) to
  the first clear of three spots ec + min(10, 0.2 (D − ec)) from the
  target: along its forward (a mover that isn't ITSoldier), then to its
  right and its left (rays from the target, `0x101394d4` slot `0x84`), and
  chooses again each second (`+0x100`);
- the trigger: If (forced) the target lies within [0.9 minRange, 1.1
  reach] (ObjectDistance; nothing in the explosive plan): the fire
  statements (`0x100777a0`), else only the aim (`0x100d9740`).
The distance D: minRange + (reach − minRange) f, reach = maxRange + 1.25
dh over 5 m up (not melee or thrown), + 0.25 dh above only in the
explosive plan (`local_60`) and not thrown; minRange is 5 m for a thrown
weapon at a target over 3 m up in that plan. `BotManager::driveFirePlan`,
`backOffSpot`, `fireReach`, `fireMinRange`
(`Bots_DriverAimsAndFiresTheTurret`, `Bots_DriverBacksOffInsideMinRange`,
`Bots_PreferredRangeFollowsTheWeapon`). Stand-ins: the rewrite drives
with the vehicles' MoveTo (`drive`) at the Mobile maxSpeed (no
half-speed approach); the spots are tested on the vehicle mesh; "in view"
is the rewrite's sight. Soldiers keep the walk of the foot branch (to
1.1 D, back from minRange). Measured (15 bots, 300 s, `BF2142_BOT_SEED`
1–16, against the same tree without the change): see coverage-5's A1
status.

### Seat behaviours: entering, cameras, rolling loops, shield cells

**Entering a vehicle.** The use key (`0x004bb570`) and the spawn points'
enterOnSpawn (`0x005b24f0`) both ask the entry search `0x005a98e0` with
the soldier's team (player slot `0xf8`): the EntryPoint objects (class
`0x9477`) within the radius (3 m on foot, 5 m on spawn, 15 m for a bot's
spawn, or each entry's entryRadius `+0x23c`), the nearest first. A
vehicle (its root's PlayerControlObject, interface `0xc4c5`) is passed
when its team (slot `0x9c`: the first seated player's, else its own) is
neither the soldier's nor 0, its template is a PlayerControlObject
(`0xc4c2`), and either somebody sits in it (`0x005c8b40`: a seat with a
player; a Titan always counts) or its template is `lockToTeam`
(`+0x350`; only the heavy IFV eu_ifv ships it). So an enemy's empty APC
may be taken, the heavy IFV not, and nobody gets into an enemy Titan's
guns. `GameWorld::mayEnter`. The search finds the EntryPoint objects
wherever they hang in the vehicle's tree (their root is the vehicle,
`0x006f1d70`): us_heavy_mech's two hang under its pelvis bundle and its
turret, which the rewrite's layout used to skip, so nobody could get in
but within 4 m of the origin (the fallback for a vehicle without entry
points), 3.4 m up the mech.

**crewKitIndex** (PlayerControlObject `+0x47c`, -1 by default; the
gunships' pilot and gunner 12): the enter (`0x005cdd60`) sets the
entering soldier's kit's geometry index (kit `+0x1d0` through
`0x0056cf50`; `0x0056cc50` shows that sub-geometry of the kit's mesh,
slot `0x6c`, or the default `+0x2b4` when past the mesh's count); the
soldier's exit (`0x00587540`) puts the default back (-1 → `+0x1d4`).
`GameWorld::kitGeometry`, drawn through the renderer's `geometryFor`.

**boundingRadiusModifierWhenOccupied** (`+0x48c`): an object's radius
(slot `0x90`, `0x006f6b90`) is its mesh's plus its slot `0x94`, which is 0
(`0x005b6b80`) except for a PlayerControlObject (`0x005c6be0`): the
template's value, whatever the occupancy, despite the name (the bipods'
2). `objectRadiusOf`. The bipods and the static guns are now bodies
(below, "Stationary seats"), so theirs has the 2 in it.

**toggleMouseLook** (Camera `+0x38c`; the tanks', the AT walkers' and the
gunships' pilots' cameras): the camera's input handler (`0x00611c80`)
runs the usual one (`0x00565180`) only while the player holds PIMouseLook
(input 11, the input's bit `0x800` and its value over 0.5; left Ctrl in
the default maps); otherwise the camera's speeds (`+0x194..+0x1a8`) are
zeroed and its angles (`+0x188..+0x190`) taken × 0.75 each tick, so the
view springs back ahead. `stepSeatCamera`, `SoldierInput::mouseLook`
(carried in a move as trigger 11).

**automaticYawStabilization** (RotationalBundle `+0x308`: the tanks'
cupolas, the walkers' AA cannons and the as_heavy_mech's second gun):
the bundle's matrix update (`0x00564eb0`) poses its yaw less its
parent's heading against the root's (the asin of the root's right on the
parent's forward, 180 less it when the forwards point apart). The gun
keeps the hull's heading while the turret (or the torso) under it turns.
The rewrite keeps the posed angle in the seat's gun and takes off, each
tick, what the seat's gun mount turned (`stabilizeGunYaws`).

**The rolling-surface loop** (groundContactVolume, PlayerControlObject
`+0x474`: the APCs, tanks, FAVs, the heavy IFV and the hover tank, all
1). The PCO's creation (`0x005cd4f0`) makes, for a root with the value
over FLT_EPSILON (not on a dedicated server), a contact sound object
(`0x005c64a0`, 0x34 bytes, kept at `+0x30c`; the value itself is kept at
its `+0x14` and read by nothing found) and finds the tree's first two
WheelEffectBundles (`0x006bf940` → `+0x318` / `+0x31c`). Each update
(`0x005c8e70`): the first bundle's ground material (`+0x188`, -1 off the
ground), or the second's when that is under 1 (`0x006bf900`, -2 without
one); on the ground (-1 or more) a new ground or bundle material marks it
changed; the volume wanted is the root's speed `(|v| − 0.1) / 30` within
0..1 (`+0x304`, the interior loops' input too) on the ground, else 0, and
the played one eases to it by 0.08 a tick ("pco-gcm-factor", `0x006aff70`).
`0x005c65d0`: after each choice it waits 20 ticks (`*0x00a6c9a4`); then,
changed and audible, it picks the sound again (`0x005c6510`: the material
manager's slot `0x70`, `0x0060a670`: the cell (bundle material, ground)
sound 0, else (bundle material, 0)'s; a new one replaces the old, its
volume and pitch envelopes on the eased value, placed at the vehicle) and
plays it; silent, it pauses; audible and stopped, it plays. The tracks'
web_tracked (material 61) on dirt is S_GroundContact_Dirt. (The contact
sounds skip materials 61 and 67 for this reason.)
`GameWorld::rollingSounds`, GameAudio's loops.

**The heavy IFV's shield cells.** eu_ifv carries seven
ifv_shield_the_generator children with armour (110 hit points,
`armor.mirrorParentDamageLevel 1`, `hudRepairCellNo 1`,
`damagePointOnDestroy 1`, Python onDestroyEvent 56). The armour's update
(`0x00654d80`, server, while the cell stands): every 0.1 s (`+0x288` from
`+0x28c`) a mirroring cell compares its percent (slot `0x40`,
`0x00651f90`: hit points over maxHitPoints, or over wreckHitPoints below
0, × 100) with its root's: above it, it loses the difference of its
maximum (slot `0x44`, `0x00656320`); below, it heals the difference (slot
`0x48`, `0x00655a00`, canBeRepaired). Down to 0 it is a wreck and
VehicleShieldDestroyed goes (scoringCommon.py scores it to an enemy
attacker; the mirror's loss has none). The vehicle HUD (`0x007a1e50`,
from `0x007a2e60`) shows each cell of the root's armour list with a
hudRepairCellNo other than -1 (armour slot `0x168`) at `+0x336 + n`: up
while its armour state is 0. damagePointOnDestroy (armour slot `0x16c`)
gates the game logic's team damage (`0x004c0e40`: event 0xb,
given only on the hit that wrecks it; see **Team damage**). `GameWorld::repairCells`,
SeatBehaviours.cpp. Since rewritten: each cell is a child with its own
collision mesh (ifv_shield_the_generator, mapMaterial 5101), whose
projectile LOD now goes into the vehicle's (`buildShieldCells`, at the
child's place, owned by the cell's id `kShieldCellIds + vehicle x 16 +
index`), so a round strikes the cell and its armour takes the damage
(`shieldCellDamage` from `loseHitPoints`, through the material table;
the friendly-fire rule by the vehicle's team). The cell's armour keeps
each attacker's damage; the hit that destroys it raises the
onDestroyEvent with the attacker and, damagePointOnDestroy, a teammate's
team damage (see **Team damage**). Rifle rounds (material 38) do nothing to 5101; the AV rifle's
round wrecks a cell in one hit (`Vehicles_HeavyIfvShieldCellsTakeRounds`).
**The cells' armour effects** (since 2026-11-09): each cell's armour runs
the armour effects of any armour (`0x006549a0` through `0x00654730` after
its hit points change; see **Armour effects**) on its own list:
addArmorEffect 99 e_healing_node (attached to the cell, turned 90°),
0 e_titan_consol (left in the world at the cell) and −1
e_bluespark_loop (attached). Its percent below 0 is of its
wreckHitPoints, the template's default 10 (`0x00630040`, `+0xc0`; the
cell sets none), and the hit points' setter (`0x00655460`) keeps them
within −10. So a cell under 100 % (the mirror of the hull's damage)
shows the healing node until it is full again; one brought to exactly 0
(the mirror's loss) gives the consol burst once; one under 0 (a round's
killing blow always leaves it below, `0x00656320`) takes the −1 group.
e_healing_node is an EffectBundle whose only child is the SimpleObject
ifv_shield_the_generatoreffect (an additive, UV-scrolling glow mesh,
simpleUVTranslation 0.6/0): `0x006549a0` creates the bundle (template
slot `0x50`) with its children and hangs it on the cell (slot `0xf0`),
so the glow is that mesh at the cell. No archive ships e_bluespark_loop
(Effects_bp1 has e_bluesparks_loop): the wreck's group starts nothing.
Rewritten: `GameWorld::armorEffectsAfter` (the core of
`armorEffectsAfterDamage`, now for any armour: its state, its anchor id,
its frame), called per cell at the end of `stepShieldCells` with the
cell's id as the anchor (`armorAnchorFrame` places it on the vehicle);
an attached group's SimpleObject children with a geometry are kept
(`m_armorMeshes`) and drawn as placed templates
(`GameWorld::armorEffectMeshes`, main.cpp's `placedTemplates`)
(`Vehicles_HeavyIfvShieldCellsShowArmourEffects`). Left: a joined
client's cells (the host writes them standing or wrecked only, 8 or 0
eighths), so their effects are the host's. **The HUD's cells**: the HUD registers
`RepairCell%iActive` 0..9 as bools at `+0x335` on (the HUD manager's
constructor loop beside OccupyingPlayerName%i), and 0x007a1e50 writes cell
n at `+0x336 + n`, so cell n is RepairCell(n+1)Active, which
HudElementsBP1.con's seven pictures (and their NotActive pairs) show under
GuiIndex 40 / 46..48; RepairCell0Active is never set and cells not listed
keep their values (`VehicleHudInput::repairCells`, `HudWorld::repairCells`).
**On a joined client** the cells come with the root's state: mask
0x800000 carries the root's armored list (0x0060ec00: every descendant
with armour, networkable or not; the generators have no networkableInfo,
which the rewrite's list had wrongly required) in eighths of hit points
with armor.fullChildSync (the generators set it). The rewrite's host
writes each cell 8 standing and 0 a wreck (`GameWorld::repairCells` in
order over `NetworkableHints::armoredRepairCells`), and the client keeps
them per ghost (`RemoteObject::childDamage`, `repairCells`).

### Parachutes, stationary seats and the seated soldiers (2026-11-05)

**Parachutes** (`src/Game/Parachutes.cpp`). Every kit's ParachuteLauncher
(itemIndex 9, SpawnObjectFireComp, component vtable `0x00973f20`) puts
the Parachute `parachute` (class `0xc5a8`, vtables `0x0096e518` /
`0x0096e818`) over a falling soldier:
- The choice (`0x004d2a50`): key 9 (input 22), or the jump key (input 9,
  over 0.5) while the soldier falls (his slot `0x78`, `0x007f9bc0`: the
  soldier's `+0x328`, which his update `0x0058d350` sets while his
  velocity's y is under −10, `*0x00a68e8c`, static init `0x008dfee0`),
  asks for item 9; both are read held (`0x004bba40`: over 0.5 with the
  input's mask bit, no edge), so a held key opens it once the test passes.
  Item 9 can be taken only while the fire test passes
  (`0x005c1150` → the fire component's slot 7, `0x005e4750`): a soldier,
  2 m or more over the terrain and the water with nothing 2 m below
  (`0x005e4330`, the scene's ray; unless `*0x00a6ef84`, 0 shipped),
  falling at 10 m/s or more, and room for the parachute (`0x005e45e0`:
  the round template's collision mesh, the collision manager's
  `DAT_00a82510` slot `0x28`, placed in the fire comp's frame (slot
  `0xd4`, `0x005e4460`: his heading at his feet plus the start position)
  against the objects within 15 m but projectiles: `0x006f2e90` /
  `0x006f2760`, a segment from that point to any vertex of the mesh's
  vehicle LOD crossing an object's soldier LOD leaves no room;
  `GameWorld::parachuteRoom`, `canopyClear`; parachute.collisionmesh's
  24 vertices span −3.21..1.10 m about the start). Taken, it opens at his frame
  plus fire.projectileStartPosition (`0x005e4460`, slot 53: 0/2/0), the
  round taking his velocity, and enterOnSpawn seats him (the press that
  lets the round go after the choice isn't traced; AIDLL's bots press
  only input 22, so the choice opens it). The launcher is never held in
  hand. `GameWorld::openParachute`, `mayOpenParachute`, `soldierFalling`.
- **The bots** (AIDLL `0x10099b70`, the weapon handling after each
  execution's plan, before its test of a plan holding the weapon): for a
  soldier (the object's flag bit 9) whose physics node (`+0x3c` slot
  `0x18`) moves down at 1 m/s or more (y ≤ −1) and input 22 in the bot's
  mask (`+0x100` bit `0x400000`), input 22 is held at 1 (`+0x58`); the
  game's choice opens the parachute as soon as its fire test passes. The
  whole soldier block (the parachute and the reload below) is skipped for
  a bot whose `+0x264` is set: the auto controller flag (vt+0x278 /
  vt+0x27c, `0x1009b3e0` / `0x1009b3f0`), the constructor's last argument
  (`0x1009ac30`): 1 from the auto controller maker (`0x100c8d20`,
  "Activating autoController"), 0 from the bot makers (`0x100c84b0`,
  `0x100c8950`), set again by IAIAutoControllersManager (vtbl
  `0x10114630`: `0x1004d140`, `0x1004d8e0`) when it takes over an object
  with an autoControllerTemplateName (the drones, the silos). Those run in
  GameWorld and Titans here, so no rewritten bot is one
  (`Bot::autoController`). A lower select
  input pressed the same execution (the primary's, 16) wins the choice.
  `BotManager::handleWeapon`, `Titan_FallingBotOpensItsParachute`.
- Entering (`0x005cfaf0` after `0x005cdd60`) sets a non-pod parachute
  upright about its heading. He hangs at its seatInformation (named
  "Parachute", the parachute itself, so shown) posed by
  3p_parachute_animSys; dontAllowExit keeps the use key from letting him
  out. His A/D and W/S steer it (`driverInput` to the canopy: the
  RotateForceObject's PIYaw, the wing's PIThrottle).
- The body: Mesh, mass 200, parachute_WingMiddle (lift 120), ForceDown
  (constantForce 12, useAbsoluteDirection, 20 m down), RotateForceObject
  (0.5/0/0 on PIYaw): `Body::canopy`, ticked in `stepBody`. It comes down
  at about 10.6 m/s (`Vehicles_SoldierParachuteOpensFallsAndLands`). The
  supply crate's supply_parachute Bundle the same way (lift 200, force 5):
  about 7 m/s (`Vehicles_SupplyCrateComesDownUnderItsParachute`).
- Landing (`0x005cf750`, server, once): the ground, or an object along a
  normal at least 0.3 up (`*0x00a0200c`; any when the other is under a
  quarter of its radius; not an object moving over 5 m/s), starts the
  timer `+0x45c` at 0.05 s (`*0x00a02004` / `*0x00a02008`, the
  static initialisers `0x008e42f0` / `0x008e4300`). The update
  (`0x005d01c0`) runs it down; at 0 (`0x005cff20`) the rider is out at
  setSoldierExitLocation with the parachute's velocity (`0x005cff90`)
  and 0.1 s later (event 0x21) the parachute is gone. A floor between the
  canopy and the exit place (a deck it came down on) holds him on it (the
  rewrite's soldier doesn't climb out of a floor he is put under).
- **Inside a Titan.** The mobile mesh physics meets each candidate at the
  LOD the mover asks for (otherCollisionLod: the vehicles 1; the
  parachute, the supply crate, the spawn beacon, the drones, the sentry
  gun, the hubs and the portable shield 2, the soldier LOD with the
  decks; the shotgun's round, C4 and the sonar 0). The Titan's parts were
  candidates at their vehicle LOD only, which has no interior decks, so a
  parachute opened inside fell through them (and the rewrite landed it by
  its rider's feet instead). Now each live Titan mesh is a candidate at
  each LOD it has (`Titan::VehiclePart::lod`: projectile, vehicle,
  soldier, with its collisionGroups), and a mover meets the parts at its
  otherCollisionLod; the rider's-feet stand-in is gone
  (`Titan_ParachuteComesDownOnTheDecks`: opened 14 m over the hangar's
  deck, it lands there and its rider steps out alive). Each mesh's LOD
  parts are built once (`TitanMesh::lodParts`, `titanLodParts`) and only
  picked again as parts go down or come back; the Titan's merged soldier,
  team and projectile worlds append those parts' faces
  (`physics::CollisionWorld::append`, the same faces in the same order as
  the addMesh calls made them) instead of placing every mesh again. That
  made rebuilding cheap (Titan_SilosWearTheShieldThenTheHull 30.6 → 22 s
  under the sanitizers, the round's output unchanged); the per-tick cost
  was never the per-LOD candidates (collideMover skips another LOD's part
  at once).
- The animation state (event 0x20, `0x005cfbb0`): 4 while the landing
  timer runs, else 1 at 8 m or more (`*0x00a02000`) over the terrain, 2
  below: the rider's seat messages (`Player::seatMessages`: still,
  landing, landed) and the canopy's.
- **The HUD's parachute help** (`0x00646cb0` case 0x0d, with the help
  manager's `+0x205`): the HUD manager's slot `0xb0` (`0x0074e8c0`: the
  player's controlled object, slot `0xb4`, as a soldier, `0xc4d7`) and
  that soldier's slot `0x78`: shown while he falls (under −10 m/s) on
  foot, not while he rides the parachute. main.cpp sets
  `help.parachute` from `GameWorld::soldierFalling`.
- **The state's timer**: the creation (`0x005cf6d0`) queues the timer
  event 0x20 1/3 s on (`0x3eaaaaab`) and each event queues the next
  (`0x005d0220`), so the state (`+0x460`, set through `+0x188`'s slot
  `0x10`, `0x005d0110`, which keeps the last at `+0x464`) is 0 for the
  first third of a second and changes only every 1/3 s. 4 is set while
  the landing timer `+0x45c` runs, which `0x005cf750` starts (0.05 s) and
  `0x005cff20` ends (−1): a landing between two events is seldom seen as
  4. The occupant's death (the PlayerControlObject interface's slot 10,
  the Parachute's `0x005cfe40`, after the died exit `0x005cea00`) starts
  the landing timer unless it runs, sets 4 and runs `0x005cfbb0` at once,
  so the canopy collapses and the parachute goes 0.15 s later
  (`0x005cff20`, then event 0x21) instead of coming down empty.
  `Parachute::stateTimer`, `stepParachutes`.
- **The canopy** (parachute.tweak's child animatedparachute: an
  AnimatedBundle, class `0x949c`, its SkinnedMesh on parachute.ske). The
  object's constructor (`0x005c06a0`, vtable `0x0096c048`) makes a
  skeleton instance of the template's skeleton (`+0x29c`, `0x005bfc50` →
  `+0x198`) and an instance of each of its systems (animationSystem1P
  `+0x2a0` → `+0x18c`, animationSystem3P `+0x2a4` → `+0x190`); its
  interface `0xc49e` (`+0x184`, vtable `0x0096c010`) sets a message on
  both (slot `0x10`, `0x005c0150` → the systems' slot `0x2c`) or clears
  one (slot `0x14`, `0x005c0180` → `0x34`); its update (slot `0xa0`,
  `0x005c00e0`) runs the 1P system only (slot `0xc`), poses the skeleton
  with it (slot `0x10`), takes the node matrices (`0x008b8880`) and hands
  them to its skinned mesh (the render object's slot `0x54`).
  `0x005cfbb0` clears messages 1, 2 and 4 on each `0xc49e` child and sets
  the state. parachute/AnimationSystem.inc: "startup" plays
  parachute_deploy once (not looping), "root" loops parachute_idle and,
  on message 4, parachute_collapse. Rewritten: `GameWorld::loadCanopy` /
  `stepCanopy` (the parachute's AnimationState, skeleton and pose), drawn
  through `skeletonPose` for the parachute's id; the renderer takes an
  AnimatedBundle's `skeleton` where a soldier's `skeleton3P` would be
  (`LevelRenderer::addTemplate`). `Vehicles_ParachuteCanopyDeploysIdlesAndCollapses`
  (deploy, idle, and the collapse on the rider's death, gone 4 ticks
  later). `--actions "up:150 wait:45 item:9 wait:3"` shows it unfolding.

**Stationary seats** (`Body::fixed`). The bipods (eu_bipod, as_bipod,
hmg_bipod) and static_aa / ap / av end their scripts with hasMobilePhysics
0: no mobile node, their collision the static world's. They are still
control objects to sit in (`0x005cdd60`). Before, the rewrite had no
body for them, so nobody could use them. Now a root PlayerControlObject
with seatInformation and no mobile physics is a fixed body: its seats,
guns, cameras and radius (boundingRadiusModifierWhenOccupied's 2) work,
it never moves or meets the mobile bodies, and its rounds leave its own
static mesh. The bipods' barrel rests 40° up under eu_down
(eu_bipod_toprotation setRotation 0/-40/0 under 20..60 down):
`SeatLayout::restPitch`, so the look holds the bundle at look − rest
and the round goes along the bundle plus rest. Only the three bipods
have one. eu_down takes both the yaw and the pitch input, and its pose
(`GameWorld::partPose`, which the drawing and the seat camera's walk,
`PlayerCamera::findSeatCamera`, put on it) now holds both (it held the
yaw only, so the camera under eu_bipod_toprotation looked 40° up): the
bundle's 40 down and toprotation's setRotation 0/−40/0 give the camera
and barrel the look. `Vehicles_BipodIsAStationarySeat`.

**The seated soldiers.** The PCO's creation (`0x005cd4f0`) looks up the
template that seatInformation names (template `+0x2a0`) in its own tree
(`0x005c6670`) and keeps it (`+0x280`). The enter (`0x005cdd60`) hangs the
soldier under it at the seat's place (slot `0xf0`, then the soldier's
`0xe8` with `+0x2bc`); with none it disables him (updateFlags (1, 0)).
So a seat shows its soldier only when its seatInformation names an
object of the tree. Every shipped seat with seatInformation also has a
seatAnimationSystem and names its own PCO, except the static guns, whose
gunner sits on the cockpit (Static_AV_Cockpit...), which the gun's yaw
turns. The rewrite showed a sitter whenever the seat had an animation
system. Now it shows him when `SeatLayout::seatShown` is set (and his
pose is loaded), and places him on the named node, turning with it when
it is a seat's yaw bundle (`Vehicles_StaticGunnerSitsOnTheCockpit`). The
crew kits' geometry (crewKitIndex) was already done (`kitGeometry`). No
renderer change.

### Team damage (2026-11-05)

The armour's event 0xb was taken for a damage-assist award; it is the
game logic's **ECGameLogicGLTeamDamage** (category 0, id 0xb: the name the
game logic's constructor `0x004d69d0` registers with the event manager,
slot `0x34`, beside GLKilledBy 3, GLAssistKill 9, GLTinnitus 0xd).
`src/Game/TeamDamage.cpp`.

- **The lists** (`0x006557a0`, the end of the armour's loss `0x00656320`;
  the attacker not man down, his slot `0x6c`): every hit's {attacker,
  time, amount} goes into `+0x220` (slot `0x120`). A soldier's (class
  `0x9493`) attacker not yet in `+0x238` (slot `0x128`) whose sum reaches
  the soldier's maximum (slot `0x8c`) × teamDamageScoreLimit % joins it.
  Anything else under a PlayerControlObject (`0x0042b2f0`) also puts it in
  `+0x22c` (slot `0x124`) while the root's control object has a player in
  a seat or a team (slot `0x98`); unmanned and teamless, `+0x22c` empties.
- **The limits** are the score manager's (`DAT_00a209d8`, class `0xc4b8`,
  vtable `0x009625a0`, constructor `0x00560e00`): teamDamageScoreLimit
  `+0x54` (setter slot `0x40`, getter `0x44`; 50) and
  teamVehicleDamageScoreLimit `+0x58` (`0x48` / `0x4c`; 25), set by
  sgl_setParam (`0x00567xxx`: scoringCommon.py's setTeamDamagePointLimit
  50). `GameWorld::setTeamDamageLimits` from `GameLogic::limits`.
- **The test** (`0x004c0e40` after the hit, server): a soldier not down
  (armour slot `0x58`) with the attacker in `+0x238` and on his team
  (slot `0xf8`): the attacker leaves `+0x238` and his entries `+0x220`;
  kind 0, the victim his player. A vehicle with `+0x22c`: the team of its
  first occupant (else the vehicle's, slot `0x98`) the attacker's, his
  `+0x22c` sum at least its maximum × the vehicle limit, and either no
  damagePointOnDestroy and the armour standing, or the flag and this hit
  the one that destroyed it: his `+0x22c` entries go; kind 1, the victim
  the first occupant (−1 none). Either raises PlayerTeamDamagePoint (the
  host's Python event 0x24, table `0x009fce60`: attacker, the hit object;
  scoringCommon.py's −1, teamDamages / teamVehicleDamages) and sends the
  event {kind, victim, attacker} (vtable `0x0091c9a8`, `0x005099f0`) to the
  attacker and to the victim through the game server's slot `0x88`, the
  server's own player's straight to its event manager.
  (`0x004c0e40`'s vehicle branch is skipped for a GenericProjectile,
  class `0x9539`, whose root (`0x006f1d70`) is a Titan (the Titan sync
  manager `0x005628f0`, `0x00561d90`) and whose owner (`+0x198`'s slot
  0x38, `0x005b30c0`) is that root: a Titan's own round on its deck.
  Settled without effect: the rewrite's projectiles have no armour, so
  none reaches the lists.) Each entry keeps its time (the game's clock,
  `0x00666070`; `GameWorld::DamageEntry`); the tests sum the amounts in
  list order and no reader of the times was found.
- **The heal** (`0x00655a00`) adds its hit points to `+0x264`; past 50,
  or with the armour full, `+0x220` empties (`armourHealed` from
  `healHitPoints` and the cells' mirror heal).
- **The HUD** (the HUD manager's category-0 handler `0x00759bf0`, case
  0xb): the victim's own screen has him say AUTO_MOODGP_friendlyfire to
  the attacker (the client's slot `0x50` = `0x004b2b60`, TCPlayer 0xe,
  the attacker as the value, the spam check on); else, the local player
  the attacker and the victim alive (slot `0x68`) and not down (`0x6c`),
  the victim's voice says it to him (slot `0x54` = `0x004b2dc0`); else the
  personal line (HUD slot `0x170`) HUD_HUD_TEAM_DAMAGE_PLAYER (kind 0) or
  HUD_HUD_TEAM_DAMAGE_VEHICLE (kind 1). `GameWorld::teamDamageNotice`;
  main.cpp for the host's player (`takeTeamDamage`), `HostedGame::
  sendTeamDamage` as PostRemote 0/0xb for the clients', and the joined
  client's handler (the victim's own call goes as its radio; the other
  voice, said in the victim's name, has no client message to carry it and
  is left out there).
- Tests: `GameWorld_TeamDamageOnASoldier`,
  `Vehicles_HeavyIfvShieldCellsTakeRounds`.

### Fire modes, tracers, camera recoil, armour effects and leaving a seat

**The fire component's flags.** `fire.busyUntilButtonRelease`
(SingleFireComp `+0x9c`, setter `0x004e3f33`, constructor `0x005d5790`;
the rocket, AA and AV launchers): after a round (fire, slot 36
`0x005d4d80`: state 4 until now + ticks per round) the update
(`0x005d4800`) keeps the weapon busy (`0x005c2da0`: weapon `+0x228` to now
+ wp-delay-ticks) until the release (slot 12 `0x005d3c20` sets `+0x164`,
a new press clears it, slot 13 `0x005d3b00`): no round, reload or switch
in between (`FireArm::fire`). The round's start and its wait:
- `fire.fireInCameraDof` (`+0x44`) / `fireInCameraDofLocked` (`+0x45`):
  the round's frame (fire comp slot 53 `0x005f1a20`, MultiFireComp
  `0x005d5fb0`) is a seat gun's camera's (the player's camera, slot
  `0x1b4(0)`; with Locked the seat camera's pose fixed to the gun at the
  start, `0x005f25f0`), else the gun's; on foot the soldier's control
  object's frame always (the flag isn't read); `projectileStartPosition`
  is then added in that frame. Rewritten for seat guns
  (`GameWorld::seatGunOrigin`, `fireCamera`): with the flag the round
  starts at the seat's active Camera (the one whose CameraId the weapon's
  zoom.startCameraId takes up, `0x005db260`, else the seat's first; its
  place at rest turned with the gun's aim about the yaw bundle). A camera
  under the seat's yaw or pitch bundle turns with the gun, and the round
  leaves along the gun's aim; one off them leaves it along the camera's
  own facing at rest (`SeatLayout::SeatCamera::turn`), turned by the
  seat's look when it is the mouse-look camera: as_ag's and us_ag's
  GuidedMissileWeapon (startCameraId 11, the TAD camera set 10 degrees
  down under the gunner's seat) launch the TV missile at rest along it
  (`Vehicles_GunshipMissileCamera`). Locked (`+0x45`, only
  AS_TANK_Turretfirearm): at the gun's setup (`0x005f25f0`) the pose of a
  Camera that is a direct child of the weapon's control object
  (`0x0042b2f0`, interface 0xc4c5; its children through 0xc378 slot 0xec
  and their `+0x38` siblings) relative to the weapon is kept (`+0xcc`), and
  each round takes that pose times the weapon's matrix (`0x005f1a20`)
  instead of the live camera: the camera carried by the gun, its own
  mounts' free look not steering the round. The rewrite's origin is
  already the camera's rest place turned with the gun, which is what
  Locked gives; the tank's camera sits under the barrel's mounts, not
  directly under the control object, so the scan finds none and its rounds
  leave from the gun's own frame (a nuance not followed). `projectileStartPosition` is added along the frame's right, up and
  forward (the rewrite's 1 m ahead without one).
- `fire.pullbackTime` (ThrownFireComp `+0x94`, ticks `+0x98`, 0.2 s by
  default; the grenades 1, the sonar 0.05): the throw waits that long
  (state 2), then fireLaunchDelay (state 3) before it goes (`0x005e4c80`;
  slot 36 `0x005e5a10` starts state 2, the update is slot 5). Rewritten
  (`FireArmSettings::thrown`, `FireArm::throwing`): the round is decided
  and spent on the press and leaves pull-back + launch-delay ticks later
  (a frag grenade's 30 + 12). **The underarm (soft) throw**: with
  `fire.altFireInput` (PIAltFire on seven throwables) the alternate press
  (slot 13 `0x005e4d80`) starts the throw with the soft flag (`+0x178`),
  under which the timer (`0x005e4c80`) waits; while held the power
  (`+0x168`) is min(1, ticks held × 1/30) (`0x005e4eb0`; `+0x90` is the
  constructor's 1/30, not a property), the arm's animation taking min(power,
  0.99); the release clears the flag and the round leaves after the
  pull-back and launch delay at the weapon's speed × power plus the
  thrower's velocity (`0x005e5720`; its random spin `+0xac` × power too,
  see **The rounds' own look**). A
  normal throw's power is 1 (`0x005e4b40`). `FireArmSettings::softThrow`,
  `FireArm::throwPower`, `GameWorld::fire`. fireLaunchDelaySoft (`+0x9c`)
  is read only by slot 11 (`0x005e4e70`: max(fireLaunchDelay, soft) +
  `+0xa4`, the busy time) and isn't applied; the arm's animation isn't
  either.
- `fire.addBarrelName` (`0x004e45a6` → `0x005d6ae0`, MultiFireComp
  `+0x94`): the gun's children of those names are its barrels
  (`0x005d6d20`), fired in turn (`+0x9c` set by default, `+0x1a8`) from
  each barrel's frame, or all at once. Rewritten: the seat's `barrels`
  (the gun's direct children of those names, in the tree's order), one in
  turn (`0x005d64a0`: one barrel always the first; past the last the first
  again), each turned with the gun's aim; fireInCameraDof's camera frame
  wins over them (`0x005d5fb0`).

**Fire modes.** The fire component (constructor `0x005f28a0`) starts in
the first `fire.addFireRate` (the template's list at `+0x30`; 2 without
one) and keeps it at `+0x28`: 0 single, 1 burst, 2 automatic. The
trigger (`0x005f1370`) keeps a press (`+0x6c`); the round's count
(`0x005f1820`) ends a burst at `fire.burstSize` − 1 (template `+0x4c`, 3).
c_PIToggleFireRate (input 46) is the firearm's action `0xb`
(`0x005c50e0`): the fire component's slot `0x94` (`0x005f1da0`) moves to
the next rate of the list, back to the first after the last, and returns
false with fewer than two; on true the sound component plays
`SwitchFireRate` (`0x005dc290`, first person). The assault rifles list
`0 2` (they start in single fire), the machine guns and SMGs `2`, the
APCs' gunners `1`. The weapon HUD shows `firerate_<mode>.tga`
(`0x007be640`) only with `weaponHud.hasFireRate`, which every shipped
weapon sets to 0. Rewritten in `FireArm` (`tick`, `toggleFireMode`,
`fireMode`). The drones' and sentry guns' guns keep their modes: their
auto controllers are AIDLL bots whose fire statement (`0x100777a0`; the
simple fire plan's BAPATrigger `0x100d3110`, button 8) holds the trigger
for an automatic gun and taps it otherwise, pressed on one execution and
let go on the next (`GameWorld::autoTrigger`); the recon drone's
single-fire gun so still fires at its 10 a minute.

**Tracers.** The GenericProjectile template (`0x005b3500`, saved by
`0x005b5850` at base + 8) has `tracerTemplate` (`+0x2d0`, resolved at
`+0x2ec`), `tracerInterval` (`+0x2f0`, 1), `tracerScaler` (`+0x2c0`),
`tracerSizeModifier` (`+0x2c4`, 1), `tracerConvergeDistance` (`+0x2f4`,
100), `maxTracerScaler` (`+0x2b8`, 0.1; only the object's radius slot,
`0x005b2e30`) and `minTracerScaler` (`+0x2bc`, never read). The firing
(`0x005f2bb0`): with a tracer template, the fire component's `+0x78`
counts down a round at a time and below 1 the round gets a tracer (the
first round has one) and the count restarts at the interval: a second
projectile of the same template (projectile slot `0xb8`, `0x005b32b0`:
its geometry the tracer template's), tied to the round (slot `0xbc`,
`+0x248`). Each update (`0x005b3e60`) the tracer sits on the round — or,
until the round has gone `tracerConvergeDistance` from its start and
hasn't hit anything, on the round plus its muzzle offset × (1 − distance /
converge) — pointing along the velocity. Its scale (`0x005b3cb0`) is
(s, s, min(t × L, along)) during the growth time `+0x264` = scaler /
speed × s (set at the start, `0x005b5300`, and again at a bounce), then
(s, s, L), with s = tracerSizeModifier and L = tracerScaler × s. The
`p_tracer2_*` meshes run from 0 to −0.98 along z, so the streak trails the
round. Rewritten as `tracerLook` (Weapons.h) and `GameWorld::placeTracers`,
which hands the tracers to the EffectManager's placed meshes (drawn with
the mesh particles, added: a Particle object's mesh goes to the mesh
particle drawer's own list, `+0x1d78` (cleared each frame by
`0x1009c380`), which `0x10135020` draws with MeshParticleMesh.fx's
Additive technique (`0x10167d90` with 1; the systems pick Diffuse,
Additive or DiffuseWithZWrite by their own template, `0x10134450`), its
`+0x80` / `+0x81` choosing the first-person pass and view as a system's
`+8` does; the list's filler wasn't found).

**The rounds' own look.** A round is an object like any other in the
original (a GenericProjectile): its template's `ObjectTemplate.geometry`
gives it a render object that RendDX9 draws as any bundled mesh at the
round's matrix, and its child templates are created with it (the trail's
EffectBundle, the looping Sound). The matrix is the launch frame, turned
only by the follow (a Point round's physics leaves it; `noseOf`); a stuck
round's up is the face's normal (`0x005e83d0`, `stuckFrame`), a lying one
keeps its facing. The bundles start and stop by their events
(`0x0061a4e0`): `startAtCreation` with the round; event 0 when the engine
starts (the launch `0x005b3990` calls `0x005b2c10` at once, or after
`startDelay` through the event queue, `0x005b62a0`; with
`follow.targetActivation` instead when the seek takes a target, from the
update `0x005b3e60`), which starts those whose `startOnEffects` is 0;
event 1 when it stops (`0x005b2ca0`: the target lost, or the round's end
`0x005b4cb0`), which stops those whose `stopOnEffects` is 0. `0x005b2c10`
and `0x005b2ca0` send their events (0x44 then 0; 1 then 0x45, which a
bundle ignores) to the round's own children only (slot `0xec`, siblings
`+0x38`). Of the shipped GenericProjectile templates 37 have a geometry (rockets,
missiles, grenades, mines, C4, the sonars, the decoy, the hubs, the
beacon, the shield) and 81 don't (bullets, shells, the vehicles' dumb
rockets: only their tracers and trails show). Rewritten in
`client::RoundVisuals` (src/Main/RoundVisuals.h): each living round with
bundles is an `ObjectEffects` object (anchor `kRoundAnchor | serial`,
`ObjectState::startEvent` / `stopEvent` for events 0 and 1, from
`roundEngineOn`; its end lets the bundles go where they are), and each with
a geometry is a `LevelSources::placedTemplates` entry the renderer draws
as an instance of its mesh (`LevelRenderer::syncPlaced`, its parts at rest
as the template's children place them). A joined client's round that
follows a server's projectile ghost is left out: the ghost's own object is
drawn and carries the bundles. The looping sound is the round's Sound child
(`GameAudio::loopingSound`, falling back to `S_<name>_Looping`). Tests:
`RoundVisuals_*`, `GameAudio_RoundLoopsItsSoundChild`.

*Thrown rounds tumble* (the RotationalPoints: the frag, EMP, smoke and
radar grenades, the IFV's mine, the stationary medic hub and motion
bait). Their node (`0x006c6480`, vtable `0x00993610`) keeps an angular
velocity (`+0xb8`, world axes, rad/s; set by slot `0x6c`, added to by
`0x70`, at most 1500, `*0x00a84b00`) and its step (`0x006c6860`, after
the linear one in `0x006c6b20`) turns the object's matrix about the mean
of the tick's old and new ones by |ω| × dt × 57.2958° (`0x005b1a70` →
`0x006adf40`, the 3 × 3 product `0x006ad420`: about the world's axis);
nothing damps it. The throw (`0x005e5720`'s end) sets the matrix to
projectileStartRotation's yaw / pitch / roll (`0x006adb30(−z, −y, −x)`)
× the fire frame (`0x006acfa0`; the grenades' 0/0/45 roll it 45°, the
mines' 0/−8/0 tip it), and with fire.randomRotationSpeed s above 0 the
angular velocity (0, −n1, n2) × the throw's power (`+0x168`), each n =
ceil(s × ((h | 0x80) >> 7) + 1) × 2^−24) for the next h of the engine's
generator (`0x0042b230`) seeded with the round object's id & 0x7fffffff:
whole radians a second from 1 to s. Shipped s is 4 on the smoke and
radar grenades and the motion bait (the frag grenade's line is a rem:
it flies unturning in its rolled frame). A bounce (`0x006c0d00`'s end,
slots `0x68` / `0x6c`) sets ω to −ω × min(|v′|², 1), 0 under |v′|² 0.1,
v′ the velocity after it: each bounce reverses the spin and a slow one
stops it. Rewritten: `throwFrame` (the thrower's `GameWorld::fire`; the
round's serial stands for its object id), `Projectile::turns` /
`rotation` / `spin` stepped by `physics::PointBody` (`moveProjectile`),
`bounceSpin`, and `roundFrame` drawing the round in its own frame in
flight and lying (`RoundVisuals_ThrownRoundTumbles`).

*Seen from its own camera.* A round's Camera child (`0x005b38a0`) sits
in the round's matrix, along its nose (`GameWorld::projectileCamera`),
as the mesh is drawn. AAGuided_missile_Camera lies at z 0.33 and
remote_missile's mesh reaches z 0.38: the camera is inside the nose.
BundledMesh.fx's opaque techniques (Full, Full20, t1) leave Direct3D's
default CullMode CCW (only the alpha ones set NONE), so from inside
every face of the missile turns its back and none is drawn. The
rewrite's meshes are drawn without culling, so the round whose camera
is the local view is left out (`RoundVisuals::meshes`' `viewedFrom`).

**Camera recoil.** WeaponBasedRecoilComp (the vehicle guns'; template
`0x005de1b0`, cameraRecoilSpeed `+0x24`, cameraRecoilSize `+0x28`): each
round (`0x005ddfc0`'s end) its control object's camera takes them
(`0x00610180`) when its view mode (`+0x250`) is 1 or 2 (inside, nose).
The camera's update for the local player (`0x006101c0`) moves a phase by
seconds × speed × `*0x00a739c4` (1) and stops past 1; the kick is
sin(phase × 2π) × size × `*0x00a739c0` (0.6) degrees, summed with the
shakes into one turn about the camera's `+0x330` axis (`0x00610620` →
`0x005b1a70`, degrees: `0x006ad210` scales by 0.01745). `CameraRecoil`,
`PlayerCamera::shakeDegrees`.

**Gun recoil.** The same component's own fields (template: recoilForce
`+0xc`, recoilSpeed `+0x10`, recoilSpeedGB `+0x14`, recoilSize `+0x18`;
the setters `0x005dda80` / `0x005ddac0` keep π / recoilSpeed at `+0x1c`
and (π / 2) / recoilSpeedGB at `+0x20`). Each round (`0x005ddfc0`) stamps
two tick counts: the kick ends round(`+0x1c` × 15) ticks on, the return
round(`+0x20` × 30) after it. The update (`0x005ddd80`, with recoilSpeed
above 0) slides the gun's local matrix back along its own z: during the
kick by size × 0.025 × sin((`+0x1c` / 2 + t) × recoilSpeed), t the seconds
left of it, during the return by size × 0.025 × t / `+0x20`, then back at
rest. With recoilForce above 0 the round also pushes the root's physics
by −forward × recoilForce at the gun (slot `0xa0`, `0x006c7b10`: into the
acceleration with no mass, its moment into the torque; slot `0x160` wakes
it); above 5 it also starts `0x005a6e70` at the gun (radius
min(recoilForce, 12), material 0, no damage: no shake, but a soldier on
foot within 0.6 × the radius hears the tinnitus; see **Blast shake**).
`GunRecoil`
(Weapons.h), `GameWorld::partPose` (the gun's slide), `stepGunner`.

**Armour effects.** `armor.addArmorEffect` and
`armor.addArmorEffectSpectacular` share one map of levels (the template's
save `0x00620xxx` tells them apart by a bit at `+0x3c`); each level has a
plain and a spectacular list (`0x00652190`, `0x006521b0`). After each
change of the hit points (`0x006549a0` → `0x00654730`) the percent
picks the group as for the Titans (above); a hit with a giver sets the
armour's `+0x250` by `0x006525f0`: the object's id (network id, else
`+0x20`) & 0x7fffffff through the generator `0x0042b230` (two steps,
×0x5e30 and ×0x661f), h, gives ceil((((h | 0x80) >> 7) + 1) × 1.7881393e−7)
= 3 for about a third of the objects; for them a hit taking over 0.2 ×
armor.hitPoints (template slot `0x38`, `+0xc4`), or leaving over 0.25 ×,
is spectacular, and the group started takes its spectacular list when it
has one. Levels 0 and −100 are left in the world, the others follow the
vehicle. The wreck's hit points drain to −wreckHitPoints over
timeToStayAsWreck (see the Titans), so the −1 … −99 groups (the aircraft's
burning) start on the way and the −100 group as it goes. Rewritten for
vehicles in `GameWorld::armorEffectsAfterDamage` / `followArmorEffects`,
and for any armour (the heavy IFV's cells) in `armorEffectsAfter`. A
template without armor.wreckHitPoints has the constructor's 10
(`0x00630040`, `+0xc0`; the rewrite's list took 0 before). Each effect is
a template created with its children (slot `0x50`): an EffectBundle's
SimpleObject children with a geometry (e_healing_node's glow) are drawn
at the bundle (`GameWorld::armorEffectMeshes`); the world-left groups'
(0 and −100) meshes aren't kept (none shipped found).

The wreck (`0x00652380`): timeToStayAsWreck (template `+0x158`, 20 by
default) drains the armour to −wreckHitPoints by wreckHitPoints /
(timeToStayAsWreck × 30) a tick, three times that with the AI running and
the object mobile (as for the Titans); drained or its time up, it fades
for timeToStayAfterDestroyed (`+0x15c`, 0) and goes (`0x00651db0`).
canBeDestroyed 0 or a time of −1: it never drains. A spectacular death
(the killing hit's `+0x250`): with destroyOnSpectacularDeath (`+0x165`)
`0x00654120` sets `+0x251` instead of making a wreck, and the next update
(`0x00654d80`) starts the effects of the hit points now (`0x006549a0`) and
removes the object; with hideChildrenOnSpectacularDeath (`+0x164`) the
wreck's render objects (`0x00651c60`, over the tree) give every mesh part
after the first the zero matrix (`0x006ae320`): only the hull part shows
(`GameWorld::partTransforms`). `addWreckArmorEffect` (template slot
`0x16c`, `0x00630c00`: names `+0x7c`, positions `+0x8c`, rotations `+0x9c`,
levels `+0xac`) is resolved into the armour's second level map
(`0x0062fb50`, `+0x1c`), which `0x00655630` hands to the armour's
`+0x210`; nothing in BF2142.exe reads `+0x210`, and no shipped template
calls it: kept (`armor.addWreckArmorEffect.list`), never started.

**Leaving a seat.** The PlayerControlObject template (save at base + 8):
soldierExitLocation `+0x308`, altSoldierExitPosition `+0x354`,
hasRestrictedExit `+0x353`, exitSpeedMod `+0x40c` (1),
maintainCameraOnExit `+0x480`. With hasRestrictedExit (`0x005c7840`) four
places are tried (`0x005c71a0`: the exit location, it mirrored across x,
the alternative, it mirrored; a zero one takes the parent control
object's; in the seat's frame, 0.5 m up): one is taken when nothing lies
between the vehicle and it (`0x006f2530`) and the ground lies over 0.5 m
below, then at once for an air vehicle (template `+0x3d0` 2 or 3), else
when there is ground within 5 m below a point 0.25 m further out; the
first that passed only the first tests is the fallback; with none the
soldier stays in. The test in full: the ray (`0x006f2530`, ignoring the
vehicle) runs from `0x005c6ff0`'s start: with the root's soldier
collision LOD (`+0x14` & 8, slot `0xc4(2)`), the place in the root's frame
and the line from it to the root's origin; where that first meets the
LOD's box (slot `0x54(2)`, the slab test `0x006ae680`), back in the world,
else the root's position. Then the ground over 0.5 m below, then a
standing soldier must fit (interface `0xc4d7` slot `0x14`, `0x00585d00`
with pose 0 → `physics::soldierFits`); the further test's point is 0.25 m
on along the way from the vehicle's centre (all three axes), and the
fallback is the last place that got that far. `GameWorld::exitRayStart`. The exit (`0x004bb570`) gives the soldier the vehicle's
velocity × exitSpeedMod (× 0.7 for an object that is no control object);
with maintainCameraOnExit (`0x005cea00`) it faces the way the seat's camera
looked (the camera matrix's yaw, `0x006ad2a0`). `GameWorld::restrictedExit`,
`enterOrLeaveVehicle`. The template's flags (its save at base + 8):
maintainCameraOnExit `+0x480`, maintainCameraOnEnter `+0x481`,
maintainCameraOnExitToOtherVehicle `+0x488` (getters slots `0x128`,
`0x130`, `0x148` of the interface at `+0x298`). Going straight from one
vehicle into another (GameServer `0x004b0b90`: the APCs' pod seats, the
Titans' pod arrays) the seat's maintainCameraOnExit is set to true for
that exit when it has maintainCameraOnExitToOtherVehicle and put back
after: the soldier riding the pod faces the seat camera's way
(`launchPod`). dontClearTeamOnExit (`+0x34f`): after an exit the server
(`0x005c95b0`) gives the root's control objects the team of the players
still aboard, none the default team (`+0x254`), except that with the left
seat's flag and nobody aboard the team stays (`stepVehicleTeams`).
`exitThroughPodLauncher` (`+0x490`, slots `0x158` / `0x154`; the AT
walkers' hull and seats, the pod arrays): the exit key (player input
`0x004bda00`, mask `0x400`) fires the seat's pod launcher (its weapon with
`0x94c0` whose fire is one) when a ray up the frame (3 m past it) and four
at the (±1, ±1) corners meet nothing and more than a second has passed,
then player slot `0x238(8)` and event 6; else the usual exit
(`enterOrLeaveVehicle`, without the second). `allowTogglePosition`
(`+0x491`, slots `0x160` / `0x15c`, 1 by default; the Titans' and the pod
arrays' 0): the position keys (actions `0x1a`..`0x1e`) move a soldier only
between two seats that both allow it. `seatLeftRotationLimit` /
`seatRightRotationLimit` (`+0x300` / `+0x304`, read through the seat
object's interface 0xc4c4 slots 0xd8 / 0xe0): the soldier's camera
(`0x005890a0`, the soldier's control object `+0x240` set while seated)
clamps the head's twist (`+0x278`) to ±40 (`*0x00a68eb0`) and the pitch
(`+0x270`) to ±85; the twist plus the tick's yaw offset (`+0x27c`,
zeroed each tick by `0x0058a788`) may pass ±40 only while the excess plus
the body's yaw (`+0x25c`) stays within [left, right] (the air
transports' side passengers, as_at / eu_at `Passenger2/3_Left` −15 / 40
and `_Right` −25 / 30; the FAVs' open position −90 / 90). The vehicle
hands every occupant its input (`0x005ca2e0` → the soldier's slot `0xfc`,
`0x0058a6d0`): seated (parent `+0x34`), no movement, strafe or jump; the
mouse's x goes on the twist, which takes it all within ±40; past that the
twist stays at ±40 and the body turns instead (`+0x25c`, wrapped, clamped
to [left, right]; on foot the limits are ±9999 and the body catches up
instead). `0x00587a30` sets the soldier's matrix to Ry(`+0x25c`) × the
seat's (slot `0x108`), so the whole third-person body turns about the
seat; the seat's LookAroundTrigger takes (`0x005ef250`'s seated branch)
the RotationalBundles' share above it plus `+0x25c` / 360 (wrapped,
within ±1) as its y (`3p_passenger_C`'s `lookAround` scrubs to y × 0.5 +
0.5). A seat with no camera in its subtree (the camera count `+0x2c` 0,
`0x005c7cb0`) gives the occupant's camera: the seated soldier's
SoldierCamera, at the crouch pose's eye, yaw the seat's + the body's +
the twist, pitch within ±85. Rewritten: `GameWorld::stepSeatedLook`,
`poseSeated` (the bundles' share above the seat left at 0),
`seatedSoldierView` and `PlayerCamera::view`. Not decoded: whether a
passenger's own weapon fires there (the open seats carry none).

On a joined client the seated look comes from the server: the soldier's
networkable (`0x005fc1a0` fills masks 2 and 4 from `+0x25c` and `+0x278`
whatever the soldier does; a seat without weapons carries the occupant's
soldier state in its own networkable, `0x00605b00`), and the client's
reader (`0x005fcdb0`) sets them back, so its `0x00587a30` turns the body
and the seat's LookAroundTrigger takes it as on the server. The rewrite's
server sends the seated `+0x25c` / `+0x278` (PlayerInfo `seatBodyYaw`,
`seatTwist`; no catch-up) in both, and its client poses the other
players' seated soldiers by the seat's animation system
(`GameWorld::animateRemoteSeated`, main.cpp's ghost loop: the seat
ghost's part is the seat, its occupant state's yaw the body's turn, else
the soldier's own): Ry(+0x25c) × the seat's turn on the vehicle object's,
at the ghost's place (the server's, which carries the seat's mount), the
LookAroundTrigger at +0x25c / 360, hidden in a seat without
seatAnimationSystem, the weapon put away. Not on the client: a mount's
turret turn in the rotation and the hands' IK on the grips: neither is in
the soldier's state, and the exe's client needs neither there: the
turrets are the vehicle ghost's RotationalBundle networkables (read
`0x00602070`), which turn the client's own bundles, and the seat's mount
and IK object (`0x005ee910`, `0x005efc00`) are found in that tree each
frame as on the server. The rewrite's client does the same with the
ghosts' bundle turns (`GameWorld::setRemotePartPose` from
`RemoteWorld::partPose`): a seat riding another seat's turret turns with
that seat's yaw bundle (its seatMount), and the hands take the grips
(`seatIkTargets` with the ghosts' parts) (`RagDoll_RemoteSoldierSeatedAndOnLadder`,
`RagDoll_RemoteSeatedTurretAndGrips`). A bone part's mount (the mechs'
seats on the torso): the exe's client runs every object's skeleton helper
in its own update (the object base's `0x0063d5b0` → `0x0063d2f0`, then
`0x0063d470` poses the boneIndex parts), so the walker's bundle animation
plays on the client too. The rewrite's client feeds it from the ghost
(`GameWorld::animateRemoteVehicle`, called by the client loop for every
vehicle ghost with a bundleAnimationSystem): the ghost's velocity against
its heading, its turn rate from the yaw's change, 0x800 while a player
sits in one of its seats (the client's round has no occupants of its
own, so the Body's system took "unmanned"); a ghost without a Body gets
an ObjectAnimation of its own. The bone parts are then posed (partBone):
the legs walk and the torso stands, and `animateRemoteSeated` turns the
seated soldier by the bone part's mount as well as the turret's
(`boneMount`, seatMount's bone half) (`Vehicles_RemoteMechPosesItsBoneParts`).
The legs' own messages (`0x00650530`: 0x780 cleared, then with the
state's input held, `+0x1c0`, 0x80 walking (state 1), 0x100 backing (2),
0x400 / 0x200 turning (3 / 4), the crouch flag in state 5) come from the
MechLegs networkable (`0x0060a000`: the state `+0x1bc` mask 1, the held
flag mask 2): the host writes the round's legs (`Vehicle::Legs::state`,
its messages), the client keeps them on the part (`RemotePart::legState`
/ `legHolds`) and hands `net::mechLegsMessages` to the animation
(`animateRemoteVehicle`'s `legMessages`, `RemoteDrive::legMessages`)
instead of the client legs' own, which have no input there
(`NetGame_MechLegsMessages`).

**ToggleCameraComp** (template `0x005db120`; changeCameraId `+0x14` −1,
changeCameraViewMode `+0x18` 2, startCameraId `+0x1c` −1,
startCameraViewMode `+0x20` 2, useProjectileCamera `+0x24`,
allowUntoggledFire `+0x25` 1). As its weapon is taken up (`0x005db260`)
the seat's control object takes camera startCameraId (slot `0x4c`) and the
camera the view mode (slot `0x18`): the static AV's scope and the
gunship and hover bike missile seats' camera 11 (`SeatLayout::startCameraId`,
`PlayerCamera::findSeatCamera`; a duck's camera 1 still wins). Event 7
(`0x005db2f0`) toggles to changeCameraId and back (no shipped weapon sets
one); without a changeCameraId it can always fire (`0x005daee0`), so
allowUntoggledFire 0 changes nothing for the shipped ones.

**The projectile camera** (`useProjectileCamera`, `takeOverInput`). A
round whose GenericProjectile template has `useProjectileCamera`
(`+0x32b`, executor `0x004f106a`; AAGuided_missile, TVGuided_missile,
mech_ATmissile, as_bike_TV_missile) keeps its child Camera (class
`0x9472`, interface `0xc367`) at `+0x240` when it starts (`0x005b38a0`);
fired by a weapon with ToggleCameraComp's `zoom.useProjectileCamera`
(as_ag's and us_ag's GuidedMissileWeapon, the hover bike's missile
launcher) that camera is the player's view until the round goes, when
`0x005b4b00` hands the view back (slot `0x34`). The Camera's
`takeOverInput` (`+0x42c`, executor `0x005276f0`, vtable `0x00979a50`
slot `0x88`): the PlayerControlObject's input (`0x005ca2e0`) goes to the
active camera's root, the missile, and stops there: the mouse turns the
camera as a rotational bundle (AAGuided_missile_Camera: min/maxRotation
±18°, maxSpeed 50°/s, snapToZeroOnNoInput, inputToYaw PIMouseLookX,
inputToPitch PIMouseLookY), and the seat's gun neither turns nor fires.
The wire guidance takes the player's active camera (`0x005e2e20`: player
slot `0x1b4(1)`, its `0xc378` matrix and position), so the steering point
o + f × (max(0, (m − o)·f) + look-ahead) lies ahead of the round's own
camera: the round flies where its camera looks. While the view is a
round's the renderer's TVEffect pass runs (RendDX9 `0x10048f80`,
PostProduction's `TVEffect`: `PostEffects::tv`). Rewritten in
`GameWorld::startProjectileView` / `stepProjectileView` /
`projectileCamera` (the seat's launch, `stepGunner`, the wire guidance),
`PlayerCamera::view` (the view, no cockpit) and main.cpp's postEffects.
The shipped launchers are their seats' second weapons (itemIndex 2,
`isSelectable 0` on as_ag's), taken by the seat's specialToggleWeaponInput
(PIAltFire; see a seat's weapons above): the gunner's PIAltFire, then
PIFire, launches the round and its camera (`Vehicles_GunshipMissileCamera`). `targetObjectTemplate`
(LPTargetComp `+0x88`, UniqueTarget) is the object the guidance places at
the steering point for a TTUnique seeker; the rewrite steers the round at
the point itself, which is where the object would be.

**Not read.** The Camera's bounce (bounceLength `+0x3d8`,
bounceSensitivity `+0x3dc`, bounceStrength `+0x3e0`, bounceDamping
`+0x3e4`; only the FAVs' and the hover bike's cameras set them) and sway
(cameraSwayRodLength `+0x3ac` .. cameraSwaySpringDamping `+0x3c8`, set by
no shipped template) have their property accessors (`0x005258f9` ..
`0x005268bf`) and the bounce its save (`0x006111b0`), and no other reader
in BF2142.exe: retail does nothing with them.

**Rounds and tracers in joined clients.** FireComp's fire (`0x005f31d0`)
makes each projectile (`0x005f2bb0`) on the server always, and on a
client only for a template without a networkable info (its vt+0x88's
`+0x14` empty: the bullets and shells; 176 shipped GenericProjectiles) or
for its own networked projectile when `0x005f1440` lets it predict one
(the local player's firearm, the template's interface `0x94c2` slot
`0x34` or `*0x00a71d20` == 1); game logic slot `0x144` (`+0x45`,
`0x004cc560`) is the server test. So a client makes the bullets of
everyone's firing itself, from the fire states it runs (see [joined
games' radio, tools and menus](#joined-games-radio-tools-and-menus)): the
rewrite's `GameWorld::fireRemoteRound`, each round a projectile from the
muzzle along the networked aim with its tracer at tracerInterval (the
fire comp's `+0x78` count), its impact effects and decals where it hits
(the others' soldiers by their skeletonCollisionBone capsules), and no
damage: the client game logic (vtable `0x0092a530`) has a return
(`0x008c961e`) in the four hit slots `0xf8`..`0x104`, where the server's
(`0x009294e8`) has `0x004ba440` (→ `0x005a4dd0`), `0x004ba500` (→
`0x005a39d0`), `0x004ba5c0` and `0x004ba3f0`. The firearm's deviation
isn't networked and the rewrite's client copy has none, so those rounds
fly straight along the aim. The 84 networked ones (missiles, grenades,
mines, C4, hubs, beacons: `networkableInfo BasicInfo`) are the server's
ghosts (GenericProjectile, `0x006067c0` / `0x00606f20`): the rewrite's
server ghosts its round's projectiles of such templates from their firing
until they go (`HostedGame::trackProjectiles`, the position, rotation and
speed block), and the client flies each as a visual round from the
ghost's place and velocity, corrected by each update and moving the ghost
object (`GameWorld::launchRemoteProjectile`); it shows its impact where it
hits and, if it hasn't gone off there, its detonation (the end effect)
when the ghost goes. The exe's client object is a GenericProjectile of its
own whose physics and detonation run locally (the same empty hit slots);
the rewrite's has no fuse of its own, the server's end ends it.

### Weapon, collision and part rows from the called-template list (2026-11-05)

The rows uncited.md's "called template names" pass left as gaps for
Weapons, Physics and the object parts:

- **`fire.allowZoomOnROF`** (the fire template's `+0xb4`, executor
  `0x004e44d3`; the three sniper rifles and static_av). The firearm's
  event handler (`0x005c50e0`) asks its components' busy slot 27 before
  taking any press; SingleFireComp's (`0x005d3c40`) holds while its state
  (slot `0xd8`, `+0x150`) is above 1 (the spin-up, 3; a round's cycle, 4
  until `+0x158`) unless the flag is set, and with it the component's own
  press (slot 13, `0x005d3b00`) refuses the fire press instead. So a zoom
  press between rounds is dropped (without `zoomWhenBusy`) except on those
  guns. `FireArm::cycling` / `zoomBusy`, `ZoomSettings::takesPress`,
  `SeatZoom::step`'s `cycling`, PlayerCamera's `Me::zoomBusy`
  (`Weapons_ZoomBusyBetweenRounds`, `FirstPerson_SeatZoomWhileCycling`).
- **`ammo.abilityCost`** (ReplenishingAmmoComp `+0x78`, executor
  `0x004e6efb`). A round taken (slot `0x38`, `0x005d81d0`) costs the
  holder's battery rounds × cost (the soldier component `0xc4d7` slot
  `0x98` through `0x005d7fe0`; nothing for a magazine without end), and
  the component's "a magazine can be taken" (`0x005d79a0`, in place of
  `0x005f4140`) needs an empty magazine and a battery of at least the cost:
  the ammo and medic hubs (1) come back with a full battery, after
  autoReload's 0.7 s; the repair tool's 0.3 costs nothing (its magazine has
  no end), the defibrillator's 0. The magazines still count in the fill
  (`0x005f46f0`). `FireArmSettings::replenishing` / `abilityCost`,
  `FireArm::setBattery` / `takeBatteryCost`, GameWorld's soldier tick
  (`Weapons_HubNeedsAFullBattery`).
- **`seek.directionBonus`** (the seek template's `+0x30`, executor
  `0x004f541e`; the AA missiles 0.8). The candidate query (`0x004cf290`)
  takes, of the targets within range and angle and in sight, the least
  angle × bonus × 500 + (1 − bonus) × distance below 9999 (the angle in
  radians off the heading). The round's seek (`0x005ebea0`) passes its
  bonus; the launchers' lock (`0x005e1b30`, the pushes before the call at
  `0x005e1d3c`) passes 0, so the lock is still the nearest.
  `game::seekCost`, `GameWorld::steerClosest`
  (`GameWorld_DirectionBonusPrefersTheTargetAhead`).
- **`target.notifyProjectileOnLostTarget`** (the target template's `+0x9c`;
  eu_aa, as_aa, static_aa, the heavy mechs' AA). Each shot (`0x005e1ee0`)
  clears the component's `+0x50` and, with the flag, keeps the round's id
  there; when a lock is lost (`0x005e1b30`: locked, another candidate for
  more than loseLockDelay ticks) that round's slot `0xa4(0)`
  (`0x005b2e70` → the seek's setTarget(0, 1)) frees it, its relock armed,
  and `+0x50` goes back to −1. `Player::Lock::notifyRound`,
  `GameWorld::launchLocked`, `stepWeaponLock`
  (`GameWorld_LockLossFreesTheRound`).
- **`detonation.detonateDistanceToTarget`** (`+0x50`, executor
  `0x004f381d`; eu_ifv_laserguided_mine 3) and **armingDelay**. The
  projectile's update (`0x005b3e60`) runs its seek, follow and detonation
  component only once the round is armed (armingDelay, the template's
  `+0x2fc` ticks, past its start `+0x210`), handing the seek's target to
  the detonation (slot 9, `0x005e9280`). The detonation's update
  (`0x005e9f60`), every detonationTriggerFreq (0.25 s), first sets the
  round off (event `0x1f`) when that target lies nearer than
  detonateDistanceToTarget, then runs the radius trigger. The rewrite's
  radius trigger had no arming: the anti-personnel mine (4 s) and the EMP
  mine (3 s) now wait. armingDelay is read for every round, not only
  seekers. `GameWorld::seekTargetPoint`, `stepProjectiles`
  (`GameWorld_MinesArmBeforeTheyTrigger`,
  `GameWorld_ProximityFuseOnTheTarget`).
- **`centerOfCollisionOffset`** (SimpleObject `+0xa4`, executor
  `0x0051e654`) of a RotationalPoint round: its node's ground contact
  (`0x006c0f90`, the height test at its position + slot `0x124`) and
  object contact (`0x006c1220`) test the offset point, so it rests that
  far the other way: the frag grenade (0/−0.05/0) 5 cm and the IFV's mine
  (0/−0.12/0) 12 cm higher. The decoy and the EMP mine (0/0.1/0) are Mesh
  rounds, which don't read it, nor do the ATs' Mesh templates.
  `ProjectileSettings::collisionOffset`, `stepProjectiles`.
- **`otherCollisionLod`** (SimpleObject `+0xec`, executor `0x0051ee4d`;
  the node's slot `0x1a4`, below 0 meaning 1). Slot 9 of the mesh
  response (`0x006bb050`) tests A's vehicle-LOD vertices against B's faces
  at the LOD A asks for (slot `0x54(lod)`), and none when B has no such
  LOD (slot `0xc4(lod)`); the broad phase (`0x006dc7b0`) sizes the
  candidate at that LOD (slot `0x50(lod)`). Shipped 2 on the parachute,
  the sentry gun, the portable shield, the stationary medic hub, the
  commander's supply crate, the spawn beacon and the drones: they sit on
  what soldiers stand on. 0 on C4, the sonar and the explosive shotgun
  round (projectiles in the rewrite); the parachute and the drones aren't
mesh movers in the rewrite. Not followed: with 0, a projectile A
  meeting a node whose slot `0x164` holds asks for 2. `Body::
  otherCollisionLod`, `GameWorld::lodFaces` / `atLod`, `meshPair`
  (`GameWorld_OtherCollisionLod`).
- **`blockInputOnRotBundle`** (GenericFireArm `+0x324`, executor
  `0x004e1d2b`). The firearm's enable (`0x005c47d0` → `0x005c4220(1)`)
  finds the bundle of that name in its root's tree and stores the holder's
  player at its `+0x204`, the disable (`0x005c42f0`) clears it; the
  bundle's input handler (`0x00565180`) zeroes that player's input (and so
  its regulateVector). While the TV-guided launcher is a seat's active
  weapon the named bundle holds still: us_ag's US_AG_TADbase, as_ag's
  AS_SecondPosition_Gun_Base, the hover bike's AS_Hov_light_Gunner_Turret,
  static_av's cockpit (its scope launcher). `Gun::yawBlocked` /
  `pitchBlocked`, `GameWorld::stepGunner`
  (`GameWorld_BlockInputOnRotBundle`).
- **The LookAtObject** (template class `0x948d`; `nameToLookAt` `+0x240`,
  `offsetToLookAt` `+0x25c`; the EU FAV's rear arms under the rear wheels'
  Springs). Its update (`0x0064bc00`) finds the named object in its
  root's tree once (`0x006f1f90`, the root first; without one the object
  manager's slot `0x124` takes the part away) and sets its world matrix at
  its parent's matrix × its own offset (its own rotation dropped), its z
  towards the target's matrix × offsetToLookAt, y = z × the parent's x,
  x = y × z (`0x006ac530`; the parent's matrix where that fails, a zero way
  up). The arms swing with the wheel's travel, their far ends on the hull.
  `physics::lookAtRotation`, `GameWorld::lookAtPart` through `partBone`
  (`RigidBody_LookAtRotation`, `GameWorld_LookAtObjectFacesItsTarget`).
- **ForceObject's `useAbsoluteDirection` and `rotationalForce`**
  (`+0x255`; the vector through `0x00546dc1`). The object's tick
  (`0x0062c920`) takes the force's direction from its placement relative
  to its parent (slot `0xe4`, `0x006f6dc0`) instead of its world matrix
  with useAbsoluteDirection (the parachutes' ForceDown: straight down
  whatever the canopy's tilt), and with a rotationalForce × the input
  (`+0x180`) pushes pairs at the root's radius (slot `0x90`) along the
  world axes (`0x0062ac00`): x yaws, y pitches, z rolls (the parachute's
  RotateForceObject, 0.5 on PIYaw). `Vehicle::ForcePart::absolute` /
  `rotational`, `Vehicle::updateForce`. Both parachutes are simulated
  bodies now ("Parachutes" below): their Wings and ForceObjects are
  `Body::canopy` (`Vehicle::fromTemplate` with `Accept::Flight`).
- **The hovering ForceObject** (`targetPosition` `+0x288`,
  `regulationTolerance` `+0x29c` 0.5, `relativeYCollisionGroupInverse`
  `+0x298`, `enableOnStartMessage` `+0x296`; the defaults `0x0062d4f0`)
  under a round: eu_ifv_laserguided_mine_FO. Enabled from the start
  without enableOnStartMessage, else by the round's start message (event 0,
  handler `0x0062ab40`: at the launch `0x005b3990`, or with
  follow.targetActivation at the lock `0x005b2c10`) until its stop (event
  1, `0x005b2ca0`). Its regulation (`0x0062b750`, not keepUp): the goal is
  targetPosition; with relativeY 1 over the terrain, regulated only while
  higher than tolerance + its y; with another value a ray down tolerance +
  y long (the collision manager's slot `0x68`, its group bits from the
  value) and, on a hit, the hit's height + y; nothing hit, no force. The
  y regulator (regulatePosY −0.5/1.5) changes the velocity by 30 (2a v +
  (a² + b²)(goal − y)) a second, so the mine hovers about 1.8 m up while
  it chases. `ProjectileSettings::Hover`, `projectileHover`,
  `hoverVelocity`, `GameWorld::hoverProjectile`
  (`Weapons_SeekBonusFuseOffsetAndHoverSettings`).
- **The rocket's engine** (`acceleration` +0x31c, `maxSpeed` +0x324,
  `startDelay` +0x300, `hasDirection` +0x335; the round's update
  `0x005b3e60` from `0x005b4370`). At the launch (`0x005b3990`) the round
  schedules event 0 startDelay seconds on (`0x005b62a0` → `0x005b2c10`,
  at once without a delay), which turns its engine on (`+0x25f`); with
  follow.targetActivation the lock does instead. While on and under
  maxSpeed the engine pushes it by acceleration a second: along the
  follow's new heading (its slot 0x40, `0x005ed120`) on a tick the
  follow's update (`0x005ed1a0`) answers true (it turned the round, or is
  past followTime), else along its nose with hasDirection, else not at
  all. A magnet's follow pushes it itself (`followMagnet`) and the
  beacon seeker has its own (`Titans.cpp`). The round keeps a nose
  (`Projectile::heading`): the firing's direction, which Point physics
  doesn't turn but the follow does (`0x005ecb30` turns the object's
  matrix). A round launched at rest along a seat camera's facing
  (fireInCameraDof, the gunship's TV missile) has that facing as its nose
  (see `fire.fireInCameraDof` above). The shipped AV missiles leave at 4 m/s
  and reach 50 within half a second of their 0.2 s delay; before this
  the rewrite pushed only magnets, so every other rocket crawled at its
  launch speed. `thrustProjectile`, `noseOf` (`GameWorld_RocketEngine`).
- **The reload message** (`0x005e0fd0`, the firearm's animation slot by
  the reload kind 0x005f4830 sets): a whole-magazine reload
  (ammo.reloadAmount 0, kind 3) sends message 2 once, as a pulse (the
  system's slot 0x30); only reloadAmount's round-at-a-time kinds hold it
  (kind 4, slot 0x2c) and drop it (kinds 0 and 6, slot 0x34). No shipped
  weapon sets reloadAmount. The reload bundles are abrupt one-shots, which
  a queue while playing starts over (`0x008c29d0`), so the held message
  the rewrite sent kept the reload animation at its first frame until
  the reload ended, then played it. `PlayerCamera::tick`, the soldiers'
  and remote soldiers' animation steps.

## Animation systems

Soldiers, weapons and seats name animation-system scripts
(`animationSystem3P`, `animationSystem1P`, `seatAnimationSystem`). A
script creates clips (`createAnimation`: a `.baf`, 24 frames per second
(`0x008c1c..`), with `animationManager.looping/length/fadeInTime`),
bundles of clips (`createBundle`; defaults from `0x008bf660`: looping,
fade in 0.2 s, fade out 0.1 s) and a tree of triggers (`createTrigger
<type> <name>`, `addChild`, `addBundle`). Value holders (`values min normal
max`, from `ValueHolders.inc`) give the range in which a trigger fires and
the "normal" value at which its bundles play at their own speed.

Each tick (`0x008baed0`) the object's system evaluates `startup` once, then
`root` and `postRoot`, with the object's state: pose index, message bits
(1 fire, 2 reload, 4 zoom...), the movement direction in the object's
frame, the speed, the turn rate and the vertical speed. Evaluating a
trigger (vtable slot `0x48`) tests it (by type: the pose picks a child,
Movement the speed, Forward speed times the forward part of the direction,
Side the sideways part, Turn the turn rate, Up the vertical speed,
Message the message bits), evaluates its children and queues its bundles
(slot `0x4c`) with a playback rate (value / normal). Movement bundles of
four clips blend a strafe clip and the forward or backward one by
`asin(|forward|) * 2/pi`. `addAnimation` puts each clip first, so a bundle's
clips are indexed from the end.

Queued instances are kept by priority, a trigger's place in a pre-order
walk of its tree, the top-level triggers taken by name (`0x008c0f50`).
Each tick advances them (`0x008c3360`): time wraps for looping bundles and
ends the others, and the weight is the square of a ramp over the fade
times. Looping bundles that were not queued again fade out, and finished
ones are dropped. Instances below an IdleTrigger are also dropped when the
messages change or something is queued above them.

The pose is built per bone (`0x008b8330`): the first instance that moves
the bone sets it, and each later one slerps towards its own by its weight.
A weapon's system goes after the soldier's, so its arm and weapon clips
lie over the body. Bones nothing moves keep their last pose. The held
weapon's bundled-mesh parts hang from the skeleton's nodes `mesh1`,
`mesh2` and so on, which the weapon's clips animate.

Bundles with `useNewSystem` (only the mechs' use it) work differently
(`0x008c30a0`). They fade linearly over their fade times, counted in the
bundle's own time. Once one is no longer queued it plays on to the next of
its `forceStopPoints` (fractions of its length, `"0.3;0.8;"`) before it
fades out; with no stop points it fades out at once. While a bundle with
stop points plays without fading, bundles of other priorities that are not
fading out hold still. `speedKeyPoints`, `fadeInSpeedKeyPoints` and
`fadeOutSpeedKeyPoints` are polylines over the bundle's length or its fades
(`0x008c2cd0`). Their product over the playing bundles (`0x008ba420`) is a
factor the vehicle multiplies into its movement (`0x00650e90`) and divides
out of the speed it gives the system (`0x0063ce30`).

A trigger with a `fadeInTime` fades the whole system in (`0x008b9720`).
The system's pose is slerped from what the bones were before by the
fraction of that time gone, and only a different trigger restarts it.
Movement bundles keep the soldier's step (`0x008c46d0`). The system
remembers where the last movement bundle was in its step (0..1). A new
directional bundle starts there, and side movement past ±0.5 resets it to
the start offsets (`anim_startLeftOffset` 0.2, `anim_startRightOffset`
0.7). A MovementTrigger with no value holder and two bundles picks the
standing foot by that phase. The backward clip plays half the strafe
clip's length ahead (`anim_offsetBackwardTime`). When the forward/backward
or strafe clip changes while it dominates, the bundle's pose fades in
again over its fade-in time.

CountTrigger plays its first child until the bundle on top has played
through once, then its second for good (`0x008c42b0`; the sentry gun's
"open"). LookAroundTrigger blends a two-clip bundle by one look value and
scrubs it by another (`0x008c3d00`; seats and bipods). SlopeTrigger leans a
five-clip bundle to the side by the smoothed ground slope (`0x008c4f00`;
the mechs).

**What the triggers read.** The object passes its movement to the system's
setter (`0x008b9ae0`, slot `0x38`): a time, a direction, a speed and one
more vector. The direction is `(x side, y up, z forward)` (`0x14`), the
speed `0x20`, the vector `0x38`. Given a time the direction's x and z ease
towards the new ones by `anim_smoothSet` (10 per second; at once when one
of them swaps sign past 0.9, or the new direction or speed is nil), and the
accelerations (`0x2c`) are the old speed × direction less the new, per
second. By the trigger factory (`0x008c1170`) and the types' vtables,
ForwardTrigger (`0x009dcd00`, `0x008c48d0`) tests speed × z, SideTrigger
(`0x008c4920`) speed × x, UpTrigger (`0x009dcde0`, `0x008c4980`) the
direction's y and TurnTrigger (`0x009dce50`, `0x008c49e0`) the vector's
second part (`0x3c`); with `triggerOnAcceleration` the first three test the
acceleration instead, and with `useDirection` Side and Up the absolute
value. The rates (slot `0x4c`): Forward and Side speed / normal (Side with
`useDirection` times the direction's y, as in the binary), Up |y / normal|
signed by y with `useDirection` (the ladders climb down by playing their
bundle backwards), Turn |turn| / normal, and a turn sets the step phase to
`anim_startLeftOffset`. The rewrite had Up's and Turn's tests the wrong way
round; fixed.

The soldier (`0x005ef250`) passes the horizontal velocity relative to what
it stands on (nil under 0.7 m/s when that moves), its direction in the
soldier's frame, and as y its jump state (`0x005eef80`): standing (the
