  (1 − f)² + the system's box on screen, at most 1 and at least the
  template's `+0xc8`; f = saturate((d − p·end) / ((1 − p) end)), end the
  LodDistance class's distance, p = startFadePercentageOfViewDistance),
  `+0x138` the bundle's emit scale; once the sprite pool (`+0x5f00`, the
  row's 1000) is more than `+0x8c0c` (0.75) used the frequency is scaled
  by emitPrio's `+0x8c00`.. (0.4, 0.55, 0.7); emitTime runs down by the
  interval (a looping system starts again, slot 0xc); each particle is
  born at the system's place lerped between its last two (`0x100c6b90`)
  and moved on for the rest of the step; at most (ttl + random ttl) ×
  frequency + 10 alive (`0x1013f6a0`), none when the pool is empty.
- *a birth* (`0x1013fdc0`): life ttl + u × random ttl; one random s in
  −1..1 gives the size offset s × randomSize and the speed (emitSpeed −
  s × randomSpeed) × the bundle's speed scale (`+0x13c`) × emitSpeedGraph
  over the emit time; the intensity the system's (`+0x160`, 1) and the
  random intensity randomIntensity × (−1..1) (vsParticle: `(colour × i +
  ri) / 2`, doubled by the pixel shader); its alpha factor the bundle's
  alpha intensity (`+0x164`); rotation randomRotation × (−1..1), its speed
  rotationSpeed plus |randomRotationSpeed × r| with r's sign; a world
  system's particles take the system's velocity.
- *motion* (`0x1013f0c0`): per step, w the wind at the particle
  (WindManager slot 0x3c) × windAffectionFactor (world systems,
  `affectedByWind`), r = v − w, dv = −k |r| r + y × gravity ×
  clamp(gravityGraph, 0, 1) × dt with k = airResistance ×
  clamp(airResistanceGraph, 0, 1) × dt, x += (v + dv / 2) dt, v += dv;
  speeds under 0.001 zeroed; with collisionEnable (+0xf0) the particle
  bounces off the ground (the rewrite: the terrain under it taken flat,
  the speed across it reversed times collisionSpeedAlongNormal, along it
  times collisionSpeedAlongPlane; the original's system ground planes
  aren't followed; the two speeds' defaults are 0.7 / 0.8, the mesh
  template's `0x10135f30`); forceToWaterSurface puts it
  on the water (the manager's water, `+0x8c18` slot 0x94; the rewrite
  the sea level plus waterSurfaceOffset); its rotation turns by its speed
  × clamp(rotationGraph(age), 0, 1) (`0x10131f80`).
- *the draw* (`0x10132e90` and the like): a particle's alpha times (1 −
  min((d − s) / (end − s), 1))² past s = startLodPercentageOfLodDistance
  (0.85) of its class's end, d its depth in the view; a particle whose
  alpha is below the template's alphaCull (+0xa0, the exe's slot 0x154,
  `0x00539094` → `0x00626c50`) isn't drawn (the collector `0x10130bd0`).
  pivotOffset (+0x1b0 / +0x1b4, slot 0x1c8) moves the quad's centre off
  the particle by that many half-sizes (`particle.vert`; 0/−0.5 stands
  it on it). drawOrder Back / Front is applied by its name (Back draws the
  newest particles under the older; where RendDX9 reads it wasn't
  found). selfShadowIntensity (+0xa4, slot 0x1d0) is stored by the
  template, but no reader of it in the sprite code was found: not drawn.

**Heat shimmer.** particleShaderType 1 (41 shipped systems: the fires'
and the explosions' `*_Heatshimmer`, engines) picks ParticleHeatShimmer
(`0x1012ed89`; the sprite manager's ShimmerIntensity 0.75, ShimmerPhases
20, its speed 10: `+0x1dcc`..`+0x1dd4`, `0x10131000`): the back buffer
behind the particle displaced by `cos(v × 2π phases + a), sin(u × 2π
phases + a)` × the intensity in texels, a = (FracTime + offset) × 2π,
FracTime = frac(t × speed) (`0x10132de0`), blended by the texture's alpha
× the particle's. The rewrite ends the world pass, copies the scene and
draws them over it (`shimmer.frag`, `LevelRenderer::drawShimmer`).

**The wind** (BF2142.exe's WindManager, `0x00704400`, vtable
`0x0099ad60`; `windManager.globalWindSpeed` / `globalWindDirection`,
`0x006ebec1` / `0x006ebfc8`): slot 0x3c (`0x00703b20`) is the global wind
plus the WindAffector components whose radius reaches the point (slot
0x18, `0x007040d0`: |p − pos| < falloff + the query's radius), slot 0x30
its length. A WindAffector (template component 0x127bbe7, vtable
`0x0097b1a0`; its instance `0x0064b8c0`, vtable `0x009874b8`, registered
by `0x0064b490`, counting windBlowTime down by `0x0064b4c0`) gives
direction × strength (slot 0x50 → 0x4c, `0x0064b5f0`): Directional
(0) the template's windDirection turned by the object's matrix,
strength (1 − min(d² / falloff², 1)) × windSpeed; Point (1) away from
it, the same strength; RadialDir (2) along the turned direction D,
strength (1 − min(a / falloff, 1)) × speed with a = (p − pos)·D,
nothing beyond windRadialFalloff from the axis, the direction bent out
from it by min(r² / rf² + 0.2, 1); TurbulenceField (3) none. Shipped on
the gunships' and transports' rotor Engines (RadialDir 0/0/−1, 20, 20,
10) and some explosions (Point). The rewrite collects them from the
world objects' template trees (`ObjectEffects::localWinds`, placed with
their parts each tick) into `scene::WindSettings::localWinds`;
`windAt(point)` sums them. A WindAffector's instance registers with the
WindManager as its object is made (`0x0064b490`), counts windBlowTime
(`+0x44`) down each tick and leaves at 0 (`0x0064b4c0`; −1 never) or when
the object goes (its slot 6, `0x0064b510`); windIsDynamic is read by
neither. The explosions' bundles (e_exp_micro … Xlarge and the Titan's:
Point, 20 m/s, falloff 10, 20 s) are spawned on their own, so the
rewrite keeps their winds in the EffectManager (`appendLocalWinds`) for
windBlowTime, at most as long as the bundle's particle systems last. RendDX9 steps it each
frame (`0x10028bb0`). Its readers: the particles (above), and static
meshes' leaves: RendDX9 marks a geometry whose path has "vegitation" a
tree (`0x100de6d0`, `+0x2a2`) and draws its leaves with RaShaderLeaf
(shader key `0xf0000000`, `0x100bdb00`), whose WindSpeed (per object,
`+0x208` = WindManager slot 0x30 at the object) sways them:
`pos += sin((GlobalTime / (ObjRadius + y)) × (WindSpeed + 5)) × (ObjRadius
+ y)² / 1024` (not the overgrowth's: OVERGROWTH has no sway). The rewrite
takes the alpha-tested materials of such meshes as the leaves
(`mesh.vert`, TransformUniforms `sway`), the speed at each tree's origin
(so a helicopter's downwash stirs the trees under it).

**Wheel and draft bundles.** WheelEffectBundle (`0x0061bfc0`) and
AirDraftEffectBundle (`0x0061d820`) take their effect from
MaterialManager's cell of their own `material` (67 wheeled, 61 tracked,
107/108 the smoke, 128 anti-grav, 62 the draft) against the ground's
(slot 0x68, `0x0061d510`: e.g. 62 × 1 `e_ade_genericdraft_water`). The
wheel's is on while its wheel touches (its ground material `+0x188`, set
by the vehicle), at the contact; the draft's casts a ray along its −y,
startDistance + 5 long, at the terrain, the water and the objects, and
is on while it hits closer than startDistance, at the hit, its engine
running (`engineName`'s, `+0x24c`). Each tick (`0x0061bd20`,
`0x0061ce20`) the modifiers — alpha intensity (`+0x164`), emit scale
(`+0x138`), emit speed scale (`+0x13c`), age scale (`+0x12c`), start age
(`+0xd8`) and the sound's intensity — are min + (max − min) × the
product of the mappings set (a/b: 0 at a, 1 at b): FromSpeed the
vehicle's speed at the bundle (slot 0xac), FromSpeedInDof its forward
part (at least 0; its sign turns the emit direction: the wheel's tick
hands every system of its effect (1, 1, ±1) through slot 0x70,
`0x00618c80` → RendDX9 `0x1013e8b0` / `0x10143950` / `0x1013bfe0`, which
`0x1013e930` multiplies into emitDirection axis by axis, −1 while the
point's velocity runs against the vehicle's forward. That happens
whatever emitDirectionZFromSpeedDof says: the flag, the template's
`+0x398`, 1 from `0x0061cb80`, setter / getter slots 0x100 / 0x104
`0x0061cc00` / `0x0061cc10`, is read only by its console row
`0x0053c719` and the write-back; `Emitter::directionScale`,
`ObjectEffects::updateGround`), FromAltitude the ray's length, FromEngine the throttle. The
rewrite (ObjectEffects::updateGround) probes with the game's collision
(`setGround`: the water, else `groundMaterialAlong`, the point on the
terrain under it), a wheel 1.5 m straight down from its bundle (no
contact list), takes the velocity from the object's moves, the throttle
as 1 when occupied, and skips parked, empty vehicles. With the vehicle's
wheel list (`ObjectState::wheels`, from `game::Vehicle::wheels()`: the
spring's name, its contact and the point under it) a wheel bundle under
a wheel's spring is on only while that wheel touches, at its contact
point, the material probed there; FromEngine takes |PIThrottle| of an
occupied vehicle.

*The depth gate.* An EffectBundle whose minDistanceUnderwaterSurface
(`+0x3f4`) is 0 or more runs only while the water's height over it
(`DAT_00a83e58` slot 0x94, less its own) lies within [min,
maxDistanceUnderwaterSurface] (`+0x3f8`, −1 by default, `0x0061a9b0`):
each tick (`0x0061a760`) it is started on entering that range unless it
runs (`+0x18e`, `0x0061a1c0`) and stopped on leaving it (`0x00619ee0`),
whatever started it; on a soldier only while he isn't seated (his parent
`+0x34`). Shipped: the amphibious APCs' wake, rear wake, bow spray and
their sound (started on entering, so on land the next tick stops them),
e_sinking_vehicle (2–10 m), the soldiers' e_sold_swim (0–5 m). Rewritten
in `ObjectEffects::update` (`BundleModifiers::maxUnderWater`, the sea
level from `EffectManager::waterDepthAt`; the soldier's seat as
`ObjectState::seated`). The web wheels' water spray (0–1 m) comes from a
material cell, not a tree, and isn't gated here. `addWorkOnMaterial`
(80 calls, the web wheels' smoke: the template's list `+0x438`, appended
by `0x0053f4c4`) is read only by the template's writer (`0x00619900`)
and destructor (`0x0061bac0`): inert.

**Cold breath.** `GameLogic.useColdBreath` (`0x00427d38`, the game
logic's slots 0xd8 / 0xdc; 30 levels set it) and the Soldier's
`breathEffect` (`+0x3a0`, only the booster pack's four soldiers:
`e_L_breath`), created with the soldier (`0x00588xxx`) and turned on
every few seconds (`0x00588830`: slot 0x100(0) on, (1) off) while
useColdBreath is on, the kit hasn't disableBreathEffect (`+0x384`), and
it isn't the local player's own soldier in first person. The rewrite
starts it at the head (0, 1.6, 0.15), with the kit's flag (the player's
kit template's disableBreathEffect: two shipped kits) and the soldier in
a vehicle (`+0x264`: the player's vehicle) checked.

**The quality switches** (RendDX9's settings object, vtable `0x101bfd48`,
slot 0x38 `0x10010040`, run at the renderer's start `0x10029e20` and
when the video settings are applied): `scene::QualitySettings`, set by
`VideoSettings.set*Quality` (the Video page; SettingsObjects keeps
Video.con). Applied as the original: terrain 1/2/3 — the terrain
culler's lodSwitchDistance 64/80/100 (unless a level's script set it
after: two shipped levels), undergrowth.viewDistanceScale 0.5/0.75/1;
geometry — the mesh LOD factor (renderer `+0x974`) 0.5/0.8/1; dynamic
lighting 0 — no dynamic lights (the light manager's slot 0xf4); effects
0..4 — the particle manager's row (`DAT_101f45a8` + 0x3c × level,
`0x100991b0`: view distance 500 × scale × 0/0.5/0.75/1/1 (at least 200),
pools 0/300/500/1000/1500, the fade starts 0/0.2/0.3/0.4/0.85, the
shader quality 1/1/3/3/3, the quality level 0/0/1/2/2), and below 2 no
decal sets on moving objects (DecalManager `+0x322e`, `0x100e6b70`);
dynamic shadows as before (`ShadowSettings::quality`). Also applied:
undergrowth.simpleShaderEnable (1/1/0: Undergrowth.fx's `_simple`
techniques, the terrain colour and lightmap read per vertex,
`undergrowth.vert`'s vertex samplers), maxSkip3pLods (renderer +0x910,
above), the Overgrowth's viewDistanceScale (above), the lighting level
and the texture classes (below). Stored only: renderer `+0x693`, the
road renderer's and the sky dome's levels, `+0x6a8`..`+0x6b0`,
`DAT_101fa9ac +0x40` and the filtering.

*Texture classes.* The texture manager (`DAT_101f8e5c`, constructor
`0x10017ca0`) has 15 classes at +0x5c + 8 × class: a "skips" byte (all on
but class 1's, +0x64) and the levels skipped (+0x60). A loader names its
class (`0x10017240` sets +0xd4) before loading (`0x10018650` →
`0x10017f20`), and `0x10017710` drops that many top mips of a 2D texture
while the next stays at least 4 texels (+0x1c). The switch gives every
skipping class GSSkipMipLevels (2/1/0) and classes 2, 6, 10, 11
clamp(skip − 1, 0, 1). The classes by their callers (`push n; call
0x10017240`): 1 the menu atlases (`0x10187ca0`, `0x10188330`), 3 / 5 / 9
a terrain patch's colormap / lightmap / second-name map (`0x1014be90`:
terrain +0x54, +0xa8, +0x70), 4 the low-detail texture (`0x100b0850`), 7
the detail layers (`0x100b2af0`), 8 the numbered patch maps
(`0x1014b6a0`), 10 the undergrowth (`0x101100d0`), 11 the overgrowth
atlases (`0x1008c7e0`) and trees' materials (`0x10151830` with +0x2a2),
12 static (`0x100dea90`), 13 bundled (`0x100a3b70`), 14 skinned meshes
(`0x100d4160`); 0 the rest; 2 and 6 have no caller. Rewritten as
`scene::TextureClass`, `QualitySettings::skipMipLevels(class)`,
`texture::skipTopLevels` and `LevelRenderer::texture`'s class.

*The lighting level* (renderer +0x6b4: 3/1/0 for lighting 1/2/3) is the
RaShader permutations' path: each `.mfx`'s DeprecationList drops its rows
below it (`0x10148ae0`; the static meshes' table at `0x10210924`, built
from RaShaderSTM.mfx by `0x100db190`). At medium bundled and skinned meshes
lose their normal maps (the loaders skip "_b.dds", `0x101499b0`, and
"_b.dds" / "_b_os.dds", `0x100d4160`); at low also their hemi map,
envmap, dynamic shadows and colormap gloss, and static meshes their crack,
dirt and detail normal maps (`0x10151830` skips "_cr", "_crb", "_di",
"_deb"). `QualitySettings::lightingLevel`, `meshNormalMaps`,
`meshHemiAndShadows`, `staticMeshDirtAndCrack`.

**The interior sun.** A seat camera's inside view with
`allowInsideStaticSun` (BF2142.exe `0x006104d0`..`0x00610580`,
`PlayerCamera::insideSun`) lights the first-person pass (the cockpit)
by its insideStaticSunDirection, Color (flickering to the damage colour
below insideDamageThreshold) and AmbientColor instead of the level's,
the effects' lights only with allowInsideDynamicLights
(`LevelSources::insideSun`).

## Debris, emitter types, level ambience and template behaviours

`src/Effects/Effects.cpp` (emitter types, `isStaticSystem`, the debris
emitters), `src/Game/AmbientTriggers.cpp` / `Ambience.cpp` (the levels'
triggers), `src/Game/LockFeedback.cpp`, `src/Game/TemplateBehaviours.cpp`,
the renderer's `syncDebris`.

**Where a particle is born** (RendDX9 template `+0x268`, the names
`Standard`, `RadialDirection`, `Radial`, `Box` at BF2142.exe `0x00a04264`,
setter `0x00625de0`; the sprites' `0x10140fa0` / `0x101410d0` /
`0x101412c0`, the mesh `0x10145fc0` / `0x101460f0` / `0x101462e0`, the non-screen-aligned
`0x1013d840` and the trail `0x1013acb0` systems). Standard, the scripts' usual type (1,359 systems), ignores the
emit ranges: the particle is born in the ellipsoid of `emitRadius`
(template `+0x18`, set through slot `0x28` from `0x00626e30`): theta = 2 pi
u, phi = pi u, then (cos theta sin phi u rx, sin theta sin phi u ry, cos
phi u rz), each axis with its own u. Radial and RadialDirection put it on a
ring about `emitRadius`'s longest axis (the first of equals) at
`radialDirection` +- `randomRadialDirection` degrees, its distance along
each axis from `emitRangeX/Y/Z` (sampled Z, Y, X); RadialDirection sends it
out along the ring's radius, the others along `emitDirection`. Box puts it
at (emitRangeX, emitRangeY, emitRangeZ). Each axis is drawn by
`0x1013a080` over `0x1013a020`: CRD_NONE a, CRD_UNIFORM a..b,
CRD_EXPONENTIAL −ln(u) a, CRD_NORMAL a + b × a Box-Muller normal; a
non-zero fourth field (`+0xc`; 517 shipped CRD_UNIFORM and 13 CRD_NORMAL
ranges) flips the result's sign with p = 0.5, its random drawn first, so
those systems spawn on both sides (`emitRangeSample`,
`Effects_EmitRangeSignFlip`). `randomDirectionAngle` then turns
the direction for every type.

**isStaticSystem** (setter `0x00626cf0` → slot `0x190`, `+0x26d`): on the
system's first update it is run for its `timeToLive` (`+0x88`) in steps of
0.1 s (`0x101407c0`), so standing smoke and fire start in their steady
state.

**Debris emitters.** BF2142.exe's own `Emitter` template (class `0x9475`,
vtable `0x0097d310`; defaults `0x00620d50`: delay 0, timeToLive 0.1, intensity 11) makes
objects, not particles (update `0x0061f360`): after its delay, for its
timeToLive, one every 1 / intensity seconds (`0x0061ef80`; intensity times
a 101-point curve, 1 unless scripted, and a distance factor of 1 unless
`+0x24c` is set) of its `template` or of `alternateTemplate0..4` (index
floor(u (n + 1)), the main one past the last; the rows of alternateTemplate1
`0x005303e1` / `0x0053045e`, `+0x474`, and alternateTemplate2 `0x00530557` /
`0x005305d4`, `+0x490`, 60 shipped calls each). Each is placed at the
emitter plus `relativePositionIn{Right,Up,Dof}` along its axes, moved on by
its velocity for its share of the tick, turned about the emitter's forward
by `startRotation` + `zRotation` rounded to `zRotationSnap` (radians,
`0x005b1a70`), and sent off at `positionalSpeedIn{Right,Up,Dof}` along the
emitter's axes (plus the emitter's velocity x `emitterSpeedScale` with
`addEmitterSpeed`), spinning at `rotationalSpeedIn{Dof,Up,Right}` (handed
to its physics node's slot `0x6c` in that order), unless `noPhysics`. A
`Particle` (class `0x947b`, object `0x00621250`, update `0x00621480`) is a
debris piece: life `timeToLive` (10 by default; below 0, 0.5 s), drawn at
`size` x `sizeModifier` (the axes above 0), its alpha `transparencyGraph`
at its life's share (clamped, `0x00621210`) x (1 - `Transparency`), its
gravity x `gravityModifier`, its `drag`. Another template (an effect
bundle, a particle system) is started there instead. The wrecks'
`p_wreck_*` bundles are made of these (`em_wreck_*_Genericparts` throws
`p_wreck_01/04/06`, each part emitter one piece of the hull's bundled mesh
by `geometryPart`). **Each piece has its own body**, as the exe gives
each its physics node (the shipped pieces are `physicsType 3`, Mesh, with a
`collisionMesh` and `collisionPart`): a `physics::RigidBody` under Physics'
gravity (-14.73) x `gravityModifier` and the 0.99-a-tick damping, its box
inertia from its mesh, whose contact points (the eight corners of its
collision mesh's vehicle-LOD box; the origin alone without a mesh) meet
the terrain as a vehicle's do (`collideWithGround`) and the static
objects' faces (each point's motion over the tick,
`CollisionWorld::segmentContact` on the soldier-LOD statics), the contacts
solved as ResponsePhysics does with the materials' friction and
elasticity (the piece's `material`, the surface's). It sleeps as a
PhysicsNode does (`physics::SleepState`, a second still) and is not stepped
again. GameWorld hands the effects its terrain, statics and collision
meshes when it builds the static collision (`EffectManager::DebrisWorld`).
`EffectManager::debris()` holds at most 384 (a guard of the rewrite's,
the oldest go first); the renderer draws each as an instance of its mesh
with the other parts collapsed (`LevelRenderer::syncDebris`), faded by its
alpha. Bot rounds cost no more CPU with it (Cerbere 2.1 s, Suez 2.5 s,
minsk_coop 4.4 s, Highway_Tampa 1.9 s user for 120 s).

**The object caps** `GSDestroyableObjectsLimit` (100),
`GSDestroyableWindowsBundlesLimit` (50) and `GSDynamicObjectsLimit` (50)
are read from the SettingsRepository (`DAT_00a7a008` slot `0x10`,
`0x00659a40`: the value or the default) by `0x004d2250` and the results
dropped: nothing in BF2142.exe limits by them. That function turns the
level's DestroyableObjects (class `0xc4d0`), DestroyableWindowsBundles
(`0xc4dc`) and mobile physics objects into ObjectSpawners (class `0x94a1`)
of their own (one per template, `0x94a1`): distance 10 (slot `0x48`,
`+0x2cc`: the 10.0 is the spawner's abandoned-vehicle distance, not a
time), min / max spawn delay 0, maxNrOfObjectSpawned 1 and
nrOfObjectToSpawn 1; for a DestroyableObject unpaused, the time its
`respawnDelay` (`+0x29c`, 0 in every shipped template; `0x005afb20`:
min = max) and nrOfObjectToSpawn its `+0x2a0` (1, no script property).
With one to spawn the spawner (`0x005af230`) makes the prop once at the
round's start and never again: a broken prop comes back only with the
next round (`0x005ae580`'s reset).

**Destroyable props** (DestroyableObject, class `0xc4d0`, template
constructor `0x005bf100`; `src/Game/Props.cpp`). Five armoured templates
ship: `barrel_big_dest_c` and `crate01_dest_c` (40 hit points,
wreckHitPoints 100, canBeDestroyed 0, explosionDamage 150 over 7 m,
material 70, force 10; level-0 armour effects e_sfx_exp_close,
e_wreck_barrel_big / e_wreck_crate_c and e_exp_small; placed by most
levels' StaticObjects.con), `train_rail_bar_des` / `jbtrain_rail_bar_des`
(1 hit point, e_destruction_trainbar; placed on Strike_at_Karkand and a
few custom maps) and the bridge piece
`bp1_bridge_industrial_01_c_sjbvfindes` (1000, canBeRepairedWhenWreck,
placed nowhere); `eu_console3` has no armour. Any armoured object is hit:
the blasts' sphere query (`0x005a9090`, objectManager slot `0x44` with the
filter `0x00968210`: an armour, statics too) and the rounds' hits. At 0
hit points the armour's `0x00654120` sets the wreck flags and, with
wreckDelay at most 0.01 and no dontUseWreck (`+0x169`), at once (else
event `0x27` later) `0x00651c60`: the physics body goes (slot `0xd4` →
`0xc`); a render object of two geometries or more shows its second (slot
`0xcc(1)`), a single-geometry one takes slot `0x54(0, 2)` (read by the
rewrite as hidden); the children likewise. With explosionDamage above 0
the armour's blast goes off at the object (game logic slot `0xe8`, its
own object left out, the giver `+0x24` the attacker): barrels and crates
set off their neighbours. The level-0 effects are left in the world. The
wreck drains (`0x00652380`) only with canBeDestroyed and a
timeToStayAsWreck other than −1: the rail bars go after 20 s
(`0x00651db0`), barrels, crates and the bridge stay until the round ends.
Rewritten: `GameWorld::breakProp` (the collision taken out of the static
worlds, `CollisionWorld::removeOwner`, `removeStaticParts`; the second
geometry through `propGeometry` and the renderer's `geometryFor`, the
collision mesh's geometry count standing in for the render object's),
`stepProps`, `resetProps` at the round's start and the props in
`explode`.

**Level ambience: Trigger and AmbientEffectArea** (classes `0x9c45`,
`0x9c44`; the levels' `AmbientObjects.con`: Liberation of Leipzig 49
triggers, Port Bavaria 35, none on the Titan maps). A Trigger watches a
sphere of `radius`; its `events` bits: 1 a player in it, 4 a player
moving in it (above 0.1 m/s), 2 a weapon fired in it (`0x005c4500` →
`0x005149d0`), 8 an explosion in it (`0x005a6e70`). The trigger manager
(`DAT_00a3fc48`, `0x00514fc0`) looks at three idle triggers a tick, round
robin, and every tick at those with players in them; a trigger with bit 1
or 4 tests (`0x005d3890`) once `minimumTimeBetweenTriggering` (1 s by
default) has passed since it fired: the first player in it (each, with
`triggerForEachActivatingPlayer`) fires it with the chance 1 - (1 -
chance / max(`averageTimeBetweenTests`, 1))^t, t the seconds since its
last test clamped to 0..100 (`0x005d3600`); events 2 and 8 fire it with
`chance` (`0x005d3540`). Its random number comes from a generator reseeded
with the tick count each time (`0x005d2e60`). Firing (`0x005d3450`) sets
off each AmbientEffectArea with the same `triggerId` (linked at the level's
start, `0x005d33d0` / `0x005ba390`; a trigger with none is dropped). The
area (`0x005ba9c0`) plays its `linkedEffectContainer`, an EffectBundle or a
random child of a Bundle (the list `0x006f2f70` holds the bundle first), at
a random point of its disc (x = r u, z = r (-1..1) sqrt(1 - u^2)), or at the
activator or explosion with `playAtEventPosition`, on the terrain with
`projectOnHeightmap`; at most ten of its effects alive, none whose bundle's
`timeToLive` comes out -1 or 30 (`0x005ba490`). `numNetworkedEffects`
above 0 makes the area the server's (the effect is sent to the clients,
`0x00510270`); a joined client's networked area returns at once (the
game's slot `0x144`) and plays only the server's events.
**Networked areas** (`numNetworkedEffects` above 0; every shipped level
with ambience uses 1): the server sends what such an area plays as the
AmbientEffectArea event (`0x22`, built by `0x00510270`, written
`0x00510160`, read `0x005100a0`, to everyone through `DAT_00a1b5d8` slot
`0x94`): the area's id (16 bits, its creation order in the level: `+0x19c`
from the counter `DAT_00a6bb08`, reset to 0 per level, looked up by
`0x005b9ea0`), the Bundle's list index played (8 bits; a dedicated server,
which loads no effects, picks 1..numNetworkedEffects), the activator's
ghost (16 bits, when the effect sits on it: playAtEventPosition with the
unnamed `+0x2c9`, which the template's constructor `0x005b9340` sets and
nothing clears) and the offset from the area (or the activator), three
floats. The client (`0x00510230`) plays it through `0x005ba490`'s checks.
`projectOnHeightmap` is on by default (`0x005b9340`; the editor's writer
saves only a 0, and every shipped area says 0). In the rewrite:
`AmbientTriggers::client`, `GameWorld::takeAmbientEvents` (HostedGame
sends them), `GameWorld::playAmbientEvent` (main's remote step).

**Lock-on feedback** (the target component: update `0x005e1b30`, fire
`0x005e1ee0`). The lock is announced 35 ticks after its target was taken
(`+0x4c`, set by `0x005e1e70`) once locked (`+0x44`, set when the lock
delay `+0x90` ran out): "target_aquired"; a locked target gone or
destroyed (`0x0058e3e0`): "target_lost"; both to the local player as radio
(game slot `0x58`, `0x0042e8f0`, channel 2) and only for `TSLaserGuided`
(`+0x80` = 2), which no shipped weapon uses. A round fired with a target
says "missile_away" on TCPlayer to the target's player (game slot `0x50`)
when the local player fires. `GameWorld::takeLockEvents` hands all three to
the HUD for every lock system.

**Hit reactions** (`0x005eda90`, from a round's first hit on a soldier left
above 0 hit points, `0x005e7520`): by the hit bone's node of `3p_setup.ske` (`0xf`
left_shoulder / `0x11` left_low_arm: Left, `0x1f` / `0x21`: Right, `0x2f`
head: Head, else Body) and the round's flight against the soldier's facing
(dot >= 0: Back, else Front), the 3P animation system's trigger
`hitBackLeft` ... `hitFrontBody` (RandomTriggers of
`AnimationSystem3p.inc`), not in a vehicle.

**Template behaviours.** `hasOnTimeEffect` (GenericProjectile `+0x328`,
1 by default, `0x005b3500`): a round whose time runs out (events
`0x18`/`0x1d`) detonates (`0x1f`) with it, else is only removed (`0x20`;
`0x005b62a0`). `ammo.reloadWithoutPlayer` (ammo template `+0x41`): a gun
not held by a soldier finishes a reload begun while nobody uses it
(`0x005f4bb0`); without it the reload is dropped when its user leaves
(`0x005f3a40`). Settled: ControlPoint `isHemisphere` has no reader but
the scripts' `cp_getParam` (`0x0056a010`; the template's field is otherwise only
initialised, `0x005bd4c0`); LightSource `castsDynamicShadow` reaches no
shader (the projector and per-light shadow passes are never drawn, see
coverage-2 #13). `keepProjectiles` (the firearm template's `+0x318`, 5 by
default, `0x005c2800`; shipped 5, 30 for the hubs, beacons, camo, EMP and
motion mines, 60 for the sonars, 3 for C4, 0 for the AP mine and the
sentry drone's detonator): when a firearm goes, `0x005f1cc0` hands each of
its rounds still alive (its list `+0x18`; not class `DAT_00998768`) to the
object manager's slot `0xd0` with event `0x20` (a projectile: removal
without its effect) or `0x21`, and the seconds (the argument the
disassembly pushes before the QueryInterface `0x94c1`). The rewrite: a
player leaving the game (its kit's firearms deleted) leaves its rounds,
mines, hubs and deployables for that long (`GameWorld::keepProjectilesOf`).
`replaceItem` (ItemContainer, `0x004e0758` -> `0x005bdd80`: each call
appends to the container's list `+0x2b4`): an equipped unlock's item takes
the place of the kit items it names (`unl_har_rifle` for `eu_ar_rifle` and
`unl_best_buy_rifle`), the one in hand if it replaced that (fillKit; the
console keeps `replaceItem.list`). `cullRadiusScale` (template `+0x58`,
slots 27 / 28: `0x00504987` / `0x00504994`; 239 lights and meshes) is the
object manager's view fade and changes no play. The manager's visible-set
walk (`0x006ff110`, its thunks `0x007003c0` / `0x007003f0`) builds two
records per frame — p0 = S × m² with S the view settings' slot 0x2c
(`DAT_00a2020c` slot 0x54) and m the manager's `+0x148`, p1 its slot
0x40, p2 = 10 S, the camera's position (`+0x1a4..+0x1ac`), the frame's
time — and for each object (`0x006fe3b0`, down its children) fades its
render object (`+0x44`; `0x006fa520`: `+0x2c` = f, slot 0x104 gets f ×
`+0x28`) by `0x006fb320` with R = cullRadiusScale × the object's radius
(slot 0x8c): d² = max(|camera − origin|² − R², 0), A = max(π R² p3, p0)
(p3 = the manager's `+0x140`² × p2, `+0x144` for soldiers 0x9493 / 0xc4c2,
`0x006fb280`, which also scales p0 by 0.25 and R by 0.8,
`*0x00a07f00..08`); hidden past (R + p1)² or (1 + 0.2) A, whole within
(1 − 0.2) A, between them easing in or out by 4 a second (`*0x00a07f0c`,
`*0x00a07f10`). Settled: the render view (the Renderer's slot 0x54,
RendDX9 `0x1000d0c0`: renderer `+0xf8`, built by `0x100671d0`, vtable
`0x101c6610`) answers slot 0x2c with its zoom `+0x1c` (`0x10066bf0`;
`0x10066b30` sets it to tan(first fov / 2) / tan(fov / 2)) and slot 0x40
with its view distance `+0x30` (`0x10066ca0`), which BF2142.exe
`0x00434610` sets each frame (slot 0x3c) to GSViewDistance × the
VideoSettings view distance scale (GSViewDistance: GameLogic
.maximumLevelViewDistance through GameLogic slot 0xb8, `0x004cc870`,
rounded and clamped to 20..3000; 500 when unset). The manager's scales
are 4 / 5 / 100 from its constructor (`0x00702de0`); RendDX9's frame
(`0x1002cef0`) sets them around the scene's draw (manager slots 0xb8 /
0xc0 / 0xc8 on `DAT_10221a50`) from the renderer's `+0x6b0` / `+0x6a8` /
`+0x6ac` and restores them after — the geometry quality's (`0x10010040`:
low 40 / 6 / 6, medium 60 / 7 / 8, high 80 / 8 / 10; the renderer's
constructor `0x1002aba0` 100 / 4 / 5; `+0x6b0` is also
renderer.minCullDistance, slots 0x84 / 0x88); `0x10028bb0` sets only
`+0x148` for its pass, `0x100ed480` (the top-world screen) 2000. The
0.25 and 0.5 (`*0x00a07f04` / `*0x00a07f08`) make a second record for
the children: p0 / 4 and 0.5 × `+0x140`² × p2, taken by a child whose own
R is under 0.8 (`*0x00a07f00`) × its root's. Rewritten in
`render/DistanceFade.h` and `LevelRenderer::prepareInstances`: each
object's instance in view steps its fade (`Instance::distanceFade`) with
R = its mesh's sphere × cullRadiusScale (the exe's slot 0x8c is the
collision mesh's radius, else the render object's, and the children's),
the actor scale for Soldier and PlayerControlObject templates, the
geometry quality's scales, the view's zoom, GSViewDistance from
GameLogic.maximumLevelViewDistance × the view distance scale; faded out
it isn't drawn, part-faded it is drawn blended. Not done: the
children's second record (the rewrite draws a vehicle's parts with its
root's instance) and the walk's filter flag 0x1000000 that skips the fade
(which views set it isn't traced; the commander's overhead view, 260 m
up, draws unfaded). Left:
`allowEmoteAnimation` (`+0x31e`, the soldier's emote `0x005edbf0`: the
rewrite has no emotes).

## The pure-server content check

`src/Net/ContentCheck` (BF2142.exe's "dep" check; the shipped
`generate_md5.py` writes the fingerprints it compares, and the rewrite's
fingerprint of the shipped content gives the shipped `std_archive.md5`
and `levels/*/archive.md5` lines, `Net_ContentFingerprintsMatchShippedMd5`).

- **Pure.** The game server's init (`0x004aff80`) loads
  `<mod>/std_archive.md5` (`0x004adb60`: "`<ordinal> <md5>`" lines into
  the map `+0x194`, and the md5 of the archive lists into `+0x178`); its
  success is the server's purity (`+0x1ac`) and the settings' content check
  flag (`DAT_00a3fcc0 +0x54`), data block 0's `contentCheck` bit.
- **Each level** (`0x004aefe0`): the ordinal, `rand() % 10` just after
  `srand` of the clock's milliseconds, goes into the level block (data
  block 2's last field, level info `+0x5c`), and the level's
  `archive.md5` (`0x004adda0`: "`<level> <ordinal> <md5>`" into `+0x1a0`;
  `+0x1ad` says it was there).
- **The client** of a pure server, once the level is loaded (`0x004b5eb0`
  case 2, after its LoadComplete), fingerprints its content for the ordinal
  (`0x0068ba40(0)`) and sends the ContentCheck event (`0x2e`; built by
  `0x005123f0`, vtable `0x0091d0c8`, which copies the fingerprint's three
  digests at `+4`, `+0x14`, `+0x24` through `0x005a9ea0` / `0x0087b560` /
  `0x0058cc60`; written by `0x005124d0`, read by `0x00512470`, 128 bits
  each). The digests, MD5 throughout (`0x0071b140` / `0x0071bac0` /
  `0x0071bb80`):
  1. ClientArchives.con, ServerArchives.con, Init.con and
     GameLogicInit.con, whole;
  2. the striped fingerprint of the mounted archives outside `/levels/`
     (sorted, `0x0068b910`);
  3. the same of the level's archives.

  The striped fingerprint: of each archive its 16 KB blocks whose index %
  10 is the ordinal, at most 500 blocks (`(size >> 14) + 1` of them); an
  archive over 500 blocks contributes its first ten blocks whole and then
  its last 500; then its size in decimal (`"%d"`, `0x00918be0`). The
  rewrite lists the archives as `generate_md5.py` does (the two .con
  files' `mountArchive` lines, lower case, sorted) and finds them on disk
  without regard to case.
- **The server** (the event's server handler `0x005123a0` -> game server
  slot 51, `0x004aec40`, for a connection past state 2): the lists' digest
  against its own, and, when the level's `archive.md5` was there, the
  other two against the ordinal's lines (as hex, `0x0068b100`). A match
  marks the connection checked (its slot `0x28(1)`, read by `0x2c`); a
  mismatch logs "dep: kicking client <id> (<name>) for using modified
  data" and queues the kick with reason `0x1b` in the game server's kick
  list (`+0x20`). A client still unchecked when it echoes DatabaseComplete
  (`0x004af710`; not the local connection `0x81`) is kicked with `0x1b`
  too.
- **The rewrite:** `HostSetup::contentRoot` (main sets the game folder:
  a hosted game with the shipped content is pure), `GameClientOptions::
  contentRoot` (the joining client answers), `HostedGame::checkContent`;
  the kicks go after the tick's events (`m_kickLater`). Tested over
  loopback with a small mod (`NetHost_PureServerContentCheck`: the same
  content plays, a changed archive and a client without a fingerprint are
  kicked with `0x1b`).

## Titans' parts, the underwater view, particle and material detail (RendDX9)

**Titan interiors and exteriors.** `GeometryTemplate.isTitanInterior` /
`isTitanExterior` (property objects `0x1007352b` / `0x10073412` → the
template's slots 0xd0 / 0xc8, `0x10148690` / `0x10148670`: `+0xc9` /
`+0xc8`, setting one clears the other) and `titanExteriorPartIndex`
(`0x10074341`, bundled template `+0x2bc`). The object drawer
(`DAT_1020ef1c`, vtable `0x101d4e98`) answers "is the camera inside a
Titan" at slot 0x40 (`0x100b9db0`: `+0x90`, set each frame from the game's
slot 0x110 — the Titan the camera is in, BF2142.exe `0x006fa8b0`: the
local soldier's Titan, else a ray from the camera up through each Titan's
hull, `0x006f2b00` — or `+0x91`, `ObjectDrawer.isInsideTitanOverride`,
`0x1007597d`) and slot 0x48 (`+0x92`, `ObjectDrawer.showAllTitanParts`,
`0x10075a7e`). The mesh renderers:

- static meshes (StaticMeshRenderer's draw `0x100bdb00`): unless all parts
  are shown, an interior template is drawn only from inside (through the
  interior path `0x100bd0a0`), and from inside nothing else is;
- bundled meshes (`0x100c5030`): from inside, no exterior template and
  nothing farther than `renderer.indoorBundledMeshCullDistance` (`+0x59c`,
  53 at `0x1002aba0`); the rest by the interior path `0x100c3880`;
- skinned meshes (`0x10162070`): from inside, nothing farther than
  `renderer.indoorSkinnedMeshCullDistance` (`+0x598`, 53).

The hull's exterior static parts (front 1 and back 2 on both Titans) share
their LODs in pairs: each records the LOD its distance picks
(`0x100baf40`: the renderer's `+0x9c..+0xa8` by part 1..4) and draws at
its pair's smaller one of the last frame (`0x100baf90`: parts 1–2 `+0xac`,
3–4 `+0xb0`, remade once a frame by `0x100bb470`, called from
`0x10020000`'s frame), at most the LOD count. Rewritten in
`src/Render/TitanParts.h` and `LevelRenderer::prepareInstances`; the
rewrite takes the camera as inside a Titan when it is within the box of a
room (a static mesh marked isTitanInterior), which also counts the cargo
bays' open floors (seen from them, the world's statics below are left out,
as the exe's ray up through the hull would). The Titan hemi maps
(`hemiObjectFor`) follow the same test.

**The view under water.** The fog object (`DAT_101fb808`, `0x1004a590`)
keeps the level's fog and the water's (`renderer.waterFogColor`,
`0x1004f740` → `0x10049640`, kept / 255 at `+0x54`, default 51.5 / 51.5 /
128; `renderer.waterFogStartEndAndBase`, `0x1004f4a0` → `0x10049680`,
`+0x60`, default 10 / 250 / 1 / 0.5). The colour (`0x100497a0`) and the
start, end and base (`0x10049850`) are the water's with the camera at or
below the heightmap cluster's sea level (slot 0x60; −1000 without a
cluster), and the sky dome draws `SkyDomeUnderWater` (the water's fog
colour, `0x100fd2f0`) below it. The end and the fourth value scale by the
view distance (`0x10028020`: the settings object's `+0x108`,
`VideoSettings.setViewDistanceScale` clamped to 0.5..1 by slot 0x28,
`0x1000f0c0`) before `0x100355c0` makes RaCommon.fx's FogRange
(calcFog: max((e − base w) / (e − s), w₄) − ((w − s) / (e − s))³).
Rewritten in `src/Render/Fog.h`: under the sea the clear colour and the
shaders' fog are the water's, its end as scripted (Cerbere Landing 10 m),
and the dome isn't drawn. Above it the level's fog is drawn the same
way: the shaders take calcFog at the clip-space w (`Out.Pos.w`, the view
depth in metres), FogRange as `0x100355c0` makes it from the start, end
and base, FogColor.w the fourth value (`src/Render/Shaders/fog.glsl`,
`Fog.h fogRange`). The units are metres: the scripts' ends match the
levels' `GameLogic.MaximumLevelViewDistance` (Cerbere Landing 140 / 140,
Sidi Power Plant 345 / 345) and the exe's AI reads the same values as
metres (`0x008959f0`). Cerbere Landing's 0 / 140 / 1 / 0.5 leaves 62 % of a
surface's colour to the fog at 70 m and all of it at 140 m. (A second
caller sets 0 / 10000 / 1 / 0.5 around a pass of its own, `0x10020000`
region, not followed.) `terrain.waterSunIntensity` (`0x100766e2` → `0x100767e9`) sets the
water material's PointColor (`+0x4c` of its parameter block, `0x10040070`)
to (1, intensity, 0.8, 1); without a water lightmap (none ship)
RaShaderWaterBase.fx takes it as the lightmap: the sun's share scales the
specular and lowers the envmap's share by 1 − saturate(share + 0.75)
(`water.frag`). The other `terrain.water*` setters (`0x10075eb4`..
`0x10076929`) call the terrain's slots `renderer.water*` call, so they are
the same settings (`registerWaterConsoleMethods`).

**Sprite flipbooks and the systems' flags.** The sprite template's
`animationEnable` (`+0xd8`), `animationSpeed` (`+0xd4`, 1),
`animationPlayOnce` (`+0xd0`: the setter `0x10138790` and the frame
count's `0x101387f0` make the speed frames / timeToLive, one pass over a
life) and `animationRandomizedStartFrame` (`+0xd1`): a particle's frame
clock (`+0x78`) starts at 0 or floor((frames − 1) u), drawing that random
before its life's (`0x1013fdc0`); when drawn (`0x10131f80`) it advances by
animationSpeed × clamp(rotationGraph, 0, 1) × the frame time (the
template's `+0x100` graph is the rotation graph, `0x101392c0`), and the
frame is its whole part modulo the frames (u from frame % across, v from
frame / across). Particles.fx as shipped is `LOW`: the frame alone, not
blended with the next. `selfShadowIntensity` (`+0xa4`, 1) is copied into
each particle (`+0x8`) and read nowhere in the sprite path or the shipped
shader. `showInZoomedMode` (the exe's particle template `+0xaa`, 1 by
default, `0x00626d40`) and `showInFirstPerson` / `showInThirdPerson`
(`+0xa8` / `+0xa9`) are the flags an EffectBundle's start
(`0x00619f90`) keeps per system (bits 0..2); in first person it starts
those with bit 0 or 2 and marks them zoomed (the system's `+8`) when the
bundle's holder is zoomed (`0x006187c0`); the scoped muzzle flashes set
it 0. `noRotationFromParent` (RendDX9 `+0x222`, slots 0x11c / 0x120): the
system takes its parent's position, not its turn (`0x1013eff0`). The
bundle's `randomAgeFactor` (`+0x410`) is sampled once a start and scales
its systems' age (`+0x12c`, slots 0x7c / 0x78), and `speedFromPhysics`
(`+0x45c`) has the exe set, each tick (`0x00618ae0`), the velocity its
particles inherit to the root object's physics velocity's direction
times the square root of its speed (slots 0x40 / 0x4c, the instance's
`+0xcc` / `+0xdc`). Rewritten in `src/Effects` (`spriteFrame`,
`ParticleTemplate`, `EffectManager::setPhysicsVelocity`) and
`particle.vert`; the rewrite's zoomed first person is the view's field of
view narrower than its first. The flags act each frame (`0x0061a1c0`):
a first-person bundle (`0x006187c0`) hands RendDX9 its systems with bit 0
or 2, zoomed or not, a third-person one those with bit 1, each with `+8`
set while the holder is zoomed. So showInZoomedMode hides nothing; it
shows a system in first person as showInFirstPerson does. `+8` is read by
the first-person particle pass (`0x10099860` → `0x100990b0` with 0, then
1; the sprite list `0x10131680` and the others draw only the systems
whose `+8` matches): the unzoomed systems with the world's camera
(renderer slot 0x5c, `+0xf8`), the zoomed ones with the first-person
meshes' view (slot 0xdc `0x1000d0d0`, `+0xfc`). Rewritten in
`EffectManager::spawnTemplate` and `LevelRenderer::drawFirstPerson`. `nearCullingEnable` (sprites; the exe's
`0x00623740` / `0x00623760` forward to RendDX9's template slots 0x248 /
0x24c, `+0x284`): in the sprite draw (`0x101318e0`) a particle less than
6 m (`+0x270`) past the near plane and bigger than 0.15 (`+0x278`) has its
distance fade replaced by (1 − t) + t f (t = (6 − d) × 0.5 at most 1, f =
max(1 − (size − 0.15) × 4, 0)), and below 0.01 (`+0x280`) isn't drawn
(`ParticleView::nearFade`).

**Projector lights and the lights' shadows.** The LightSource template
keeps `castsStaticShadow` / `castsDynamicShadow` / `selfShadows` /
`objectShadows`, `softness` and `projectorTexture` / `Fov` / `Aspect` /
`Near` / `Far` (the writer `0x00617030`; slots 0xfc..0x1e0). RendDX9's
light manager loads `Shaders/LightManager_r3x0` (`0x100a9a00`, the
manager's `+0x788`), whose SpotProjector, PointLightShadow and
SpotLightShadow techniques take them, but only fetches its parameter
handles (LIGHTPOS … PROJECTORMASK, `+0x79c..+0x7b4`) and releases them:
nothing sets a technique of it or draws with it (no reader of `+0x788`
besides the load and the release), and no "SpotProjector" string exists
in RendDX9_ori.dll. So retail draws no projected textures and no per-light
shadows; the rewrite keeps the templates' values unread. Checked again:
the load (`0x100a9a00`, called with the manager less 8, so its effect is
the manager's `+0x788` and the handles STENCILFUNC … VIEWPROJ
`+0x78c..+0x7c4`) is the only code that touches them besides the release
(`0x100aa720`); no function reads a handle to set it, the effect's
techniques are never looked up (FUN_1001dd30 / 1001dd90 are never given
it), and the light filter's shadow bits (4, 0x10, 0x20, 0x40) are asked by
no caller (MeshLights.h). The projector fields' template getters (slots
0x18c..0x1b0) and objectShadows / shadowIntensity / softness (0x1d0 ..
0x1e0) are read only by the lightmap generator (`0x1006a310`). The cone
angles' setters clamp to 180 (`0x00617790` / `0x006177c0`, the
template's `+0xd8` / `+0xdc`); the light object turns coneAngle2 into the
shaders' radians (see the spot lights above).

**Static-mesh and bundled material detail.** `setMaterialReflectionScale`
and `setSpecularStaticGloss` (`0x10073caf` / `0x10073eb9`) act on bundled
templates only (`0x100713c4`): maps keyed geometry << 16 | lod << 8 |
material (`0x100a25d0` `+0xec`, `0x100a26b0` `+0xf8`);
`setMaterialParallaxHeightScale` (`0x10073208`) is any template's slot
0x38, empty for bundled ones (`0x100a7d70`); `nrOfAnimatedUVMatrix`
(`0x10073ba7`) the bundled template's `+0x110`. The rewrite keeps all
four (`geom::GeometryTemplate`) and draws a bundled material's StaticGloss
from its setSpecularStaticGloss (0.15 otherwise).

*Static meshes per pixel.* Every shipped static mesh declares a FLOAT3
position and a FLOAT3 TANGENT; the vertex format now carries the tangent
and the binormal's sign (`Vertex::tangent`: RaShaderSTM
getBinormalFlipping's 1 − 2 × Pos.w, −1 with Direct3D's default w of 1;
bundled and skinned meshes' sign from the third blend-index byte as
before, no longer packed into the layers' coordinates). The techniques'
literals (RaShaderSTM.mfx) name the maps after the colour layers: NDetail's
"_deb" map, NCrack's "_crb" (3,152 BaseDetailNDetail materials, 269 with
NCrack, 24 parallaxdetail across the static archives). With any of them
the material takes RaShaderSTM's PERPIXEL path (mesh.frag): the normal from
the detail normal map, the crack normal map over it by the crack's alpha,
the sun's N·L and the specular by it, the sky by
`lightmap.b × dot(N, skyNormal (0.78, 0.52, 0.65))` in the tangent frame
(getDiffusePixelLighting). Parallax (calculateParallaxCoordinatesFromAlpha):
the detail normal map's alpha × scale − scale / 2 along the tangent-space
eye's (x, −y), on the detail and normal maps' coordinates;
ParallaxScaleBias's scale is the template's height scale (the
setMaterialParallaxHeightScale map at `+0x80`, 15 by default, `0x100db690`)
over the detail map's width and height (`0x100d9c00`; `0x100d9d90`'s
default 1/512, 1/2048 is the shipped 512×2048 detail map's). The lighting
level drops parallax at medium and the normal maps at low (the
DeprecationList; `0x10151830` skips "_deb" / "_crb"). The reflection scale
reaches no shader line: RaShaderBM.fx lerps by a fixed gloss / 4 (its
comment names eyePos.w the reflection scale, nothing reads it). The
animated UV matrices (the per-part UV transforms, the tracks') are drawn
since d9a49fe: see "Animated UVs" (`src/Render/AnimatedUV.h`).

**`undergrowth.simpleShaderEnable`** (`0x100862e7`) writes the
undergrowth's slot 0x40, the value the quality switch also writes: the
script's or console's setting holds until the video settings are applied
again (`QualitySettings::undergrowthSimpleShaderSet`).
`HemiMapManager.makeHemiMap` (`0x10085a91` → the manager's slot 0x40,
`0x100ed480`) renders the level from above into two render targets the
size given (at most the device's texture size) and saves the hemi map: an
editor tool no shipped script calls; still a stub.

**Tests.** The renderer's GPU-free parts are headers the tests include
(`bf2142_tests` doesn't link the renderer): `TitanParts.h`, `Fog.h`
(with FogRange), `EnvMaps.h`,
`SceneMath.h` (the shadow region and map size, BC3 alpha, the hemi maps'
texels and the Titan maps' bilinear sample, HeightOverTerrain, the clouds'
offsets, the normal maps' kinds) and `OverheadView.h` (the overhead
camera's place), with the quality's mip skips and lighting level;
`tests/RenderSceneTest.cpp`.

## Shadows, hemi maps, sky and post-production (RendDX9)

`src/Render/LevelRendererPost.cpp`, `src/Render/PostProduction.h`, the
settings in `src/Scene/PostProductionSettings.h`; shaders `shadow.glsl`,
`shadowcaster.frag`, `sky.frag`, `bloom.frag`, `post.frag`, `camo.frag`,
`fullscreen.vert`. A frame is now: the shadow maps, the world pass into a
scene texture, the camouflage mask, the first-person pass, the bloom
chain, then `post.frag` into the target with the HUD and the menus over
it.

**Dynamic shadows.** The settings live in the light manager (class
`dice.hfe.geom.LightManager` `0xd01c1`, created by `0x10070472`,
constructed by `0x100aafe0`, which sets the defaults; its vtable
`0x101d42e0` slots 41 to 94 are the `shadowManager.*` setters and getters
the console's `0x100802eb`..`0x100821b3` call, e.g. `0x1014a580` the map
size, which keeps the old one when the device refuses it, `0x1014a5d0` the
object size, at most the map's, `0x1014a600` the bit depth as
D3DFMT_D16/D24S8/D32, `0x1014a840` the alpha threshold that it uploads as
SHADOWALPHATHRESHOLD). Defaults: map 1024, objects 512, depth distance 40,
dynamic, static-mesh and first-person shadows on, alpha shadows off
(threshold 0.2), update factor 1, the PSM/TSM tuning (fov 60, TSM focus
0.52, 80 % line -0.6). The shipped scripts never call `shadowManager.*`;
the menu's `VideoSettings.DynamicShadowsQuality` (0 off .. 3) picks the
quality. The receivers' shaders are RaCommon.fx's `calcShadowProjection`
and `getShadowFactorExactOther` (four taps half a texel apart) behind the
`_HASSHADOW_` techniques (the `*Shadowed.fx` variants), the occluders'
map (`ShadowOccluderMap`) multiplied in for bundled meshes, and
LightManager_r3x0.fx's `saturate(lightmap.a + ShadowIntensityBias)`.

The rewrite keeps two orthographic maps along the sun over a square region
(half side `shadowMapDepthDistance` × 1, 1.5 or 2 by quality; the map's
size doubled at quality 3), centred half a region ahead of the camera and
snapped to a quarter of the region's side so the projection holds still between
moves: the dynamic objects' map (bundled and skinned meshes, including
the first person's own soldier when `dynamic1pShadowsEnabled`) is redrawn
each frame, the static meshes' (with `shadowMapIncludeStaticMeshes` and
`dynamicStaticMeshShadowsEnabled`) only when the region moves or objects
come and go. Terrain, roads, undergrowth (`undergrowth.dynamicShadowsEnable`,
`0x100861d8`) and lightmapped meshes take only the dynamic map (their
lightmaps hold the statics' shadows); unlightmapped meshes (soldiers,
vehicles, unlit statics, the first-person models) take both. Blended and
additive materials cast nothing; alpha-tested ones only with
`allowAlphaShadows`. The comparison is a filtered depth compare at four
taps, faded out over the region's last fifth. `BF2142_SHADOW_DEBUG=1` shows
the terrain's shadow factor, `BF2142_SHADOW_STATS=1` prints the casters,
`BF2142_SHADOW_REDRAW=1` redraws the static map every frame (its cost).
`shadowManager.shadowUpdatesEnabled 0` (LM `+0x755`, `0x1014a900`;
the shadow pass `0x10127420` runs only with it set) stops the maps'
redraws: they keep what they hold, with their projection.
`GeometryTemplate.useRadiusForShadowDepth` / `useRadiusForShadowSpatial`
(`0x100a7e60`..`0x100a7e90`, the bundled template's `+0x204` / `+0x205`;
the heavy mechs set both) make the light manager fit a caster's depth
range (`0x10125780` → `0x1012b190`) and light-space bounds (`0x10123e70`)
to the box `pos ± radius·√2` instead of the mesh's oriented box, steady
while the legs move; the rewrite's region test takes that wider bound
for them. Settled as unused by RendDX9: `shadowUpdateFactor` (`+0x750`)
and `dropShadowClipHeightOffset` (`+0x1d8`) have no reader but their
getters; `lightmapIntensityBias` (`+0x1d4`, uploaded at once by
`0x1014a780` as LIGHTMAPINTENSITYBIAS) is read only by
LightManager_r3x0.fx's Combine technique, which nothing selects. Not
done: RendDX9's light-space perspective (LSPSM/TSM) fit and its
per-object maps (`shadowMapObjectSize`). A view-fitted perspective map
moves with every turn of the camera, so the static casters' map could no
longer be kept between moves of the region (its redraw costs up to ~1 ms
a frame, see above), and per-object maps add a pass per caster; both
would raise the frame cost well beyond the current 0.2-0.4 ms, so they
are left out on purpose. For the same reason the terrain takes the
dynamic map in its one pass (terrain.frag) where RendDX9 draws a second
pass over just the cells under each map: before the terrain's draw
(`0x100b4d80`), with shadowUpdatesEnabled (LM `+0x755`, `0x1014a910`) and
the terrain's shadow strength `+0x3ec` (4, the constructor) over 0.1, it
sets `+0x3f0` = `+0x3ec` × (1.643 + the sun's direction y, LM slot
0x1ac `0x1014ad90`) and has `0x1014c4e0` list, for each of the light
manager's maps (`+0x6f8`, `0x1014ab00`; 0x494 bytes each, skipped when
`+0x444` is set), the patches at LOD levels 0..2 whose cells meet the
map's light-space box (its 8 corners, `0x100abee0`), with the half-cell
edge fans towards coarser neighbours (the patch's `+0x100` bits 1 / 2 / 4
/ 8), into an index buffer of at most `+0x3e8` indices; the patches it
lists (`0x100b6a00`) get the shadowed pass.

**The SimpleShadowmap** (`src/Render/SimpleShadowmap.h`;
`LevelRenderer::loadSimpleShadowmap` / `simpleShadowFor`; mesh.frag).
The light manager loads two lightmapper files at the level's load
(`0x100aa290`): `SimpleShadowmap.raw` (the sun's occlusion by the terrain
and the statics, kept in 2-bit steps) and `SimpleShadowmapIO.raw` (an
outdoors bit), both from the level's server.zip.
- Each file is N x N bytes, N half the cluster's heightmapSize, a texel
  2 m, centred on the origin, the first row at +z. The lookups are
  bilinear (`0x100a8cb0` / `0x100a9160`).
- The bundled meshes (`0x100c3880` / `0x100c5030`; unless drawn with the
  shadowed technique: quality 3 and in the dynamic map) and the skinned
  meshes (`0x10162070`, always) multiply their sun and specular colours by
  f at their origin:
  - outdoors with nothing above, the map faded to 1 between 3 and 6 m over
    the ground;
  - indoors under a roof, the map;
  - otherwise 1.
- This is how RendDX9 has hills shade vehicles and soldiers. Its terrain
  occluder pass (TerrainOccluderShadows `0x1014d450`, from `0x100b0a40`)
  is dead code that nothing reaches.
- The original casts collision rays for the height and the roof
  (`0x100c2b70`). The rewrite takes the height over the terrain and the
  IO bit for the roof.
- Where the shadow maps also apply, the shader takes the darker of the
  two.

Note on the hemi map's scale: Cerbere_Landing's `groundhemi` (and its
SimpleShadowmap) cover the 1024 m primary heightmap. Sky.con gives
2048, and RendDX9 uploads that size unchanged as HemiMapConstants.z
(the base map's `+0x40`, `0x100ed200` → `0x100ecae0`, copied by
the frame `0x1002cef0`). So the original, like the rewrite, samples
that level's hemi map at half its scale.

**Hemi maps.** `HemiMapManager.setBaseHemiMap <texture> <corner> <size>
[<height>]` (`0x100857b8`; every level's Sky.con: `groundhemi`, 0/0/0,
2048, 500) names a DXT5 map over the level: rgb the ground's bounced
colour, alpha the sun's occlusion (roofs, bridges, the buildings'
shade; Camp Gibraltar's is 97 % at 255). RaShaderBM.fx / RaShaderSM.fx
`calcGroundUVAndLerp` look it up under the point a metre along its normal,
`uv = ((p + size/2 + n).xz - corner.xz) / size`, v flipped, and lerp the
ambient from that ground colour to `HemiMapSkyColor` (the sky colour) by
`clamp((n.y + offset) / 2 + 0.5, 0, 0.9)`, offset = `clamp(localHeight × 2 −
1 + HeightOverTerrain, −2(1 − HeightOverTerrain), 0.8)` with the point's
height over its object's origin at InvHemiHeightScale (0.5 for skinned
meshes); `_HASHEMIOCCLUSION_` multiplies the sun term by the map's alpha.
The renderer uploads HemiMapConstants (corner, size, lerp bias) and
HemiMapSkyColor with its per-frame constants (`0x10030000` table: 0x110,
0x124; TreeSkyColor 0x138). The rewrite applies it to every unlightmapped
mesh in mesh.frag. Per object (the block `0x10041100` builds:
HeightOverTerrain `+0x1e4`, HemiMapConstantColor `+0x1ec`; only RaShaderBM
and RaShaderSM read them):

- *HeightOverTerrain* (BM `0x100c2b70`, SM `0x10160e90`): a ray from the
  object's origin 4 radii down, `h` the height over what it meets (4 r
  if nothing), `max(h − r, 0) / max(r, 2)`; it lifts the lerp's offset,
  `clamp(localHeight × 2 − 1 + HOT, −2(1 − HOT), 0.8)`. The rewrite's
  ray meets only the terrain.
- *HemiMapConstantColor* multiplies the hemi colour: 1 with the hemi
  technique outside the Titans. With the camera in a Titan (the game's
  test, `0x006fa8b0`: the Titan the camera's soldier is in) bundled and
  skinned meshes take the interior path (`0x100c3880`, `0x10162070`):
  HeightOverTerrain 0, and the colour from the Titan maps.
  `HemiMapManager.loadTitanHemiMap <texture> <offset> <size> <which>`
  (`0x1008560d` → `0x100edf90`; 14 calls in the Titans' playtest and
  wake files, `Common/Textures/eu_titan_interior_hemimap_level1_small
  2/-10/-33 128 0` and the `as_` one `2/-9/-33 128 1`: 1 the PAC's Titan,
  0 the EU's) keeps a map (`0x100ed200`, a missing file an 8 × 8 white
  one); each frame (`0x1002db21` → `0x100eda70`) its matrix is the
  Titan's inverse then the offset taken off; an object over a map's
  square (local y > 0, |x|, |z| < size / 2, the nearest above,
  `0x100edce0`) takes its texel bilinearly at `u = size/2 − x`, `v =
  size/2 + z` (`0x100ecb10`, on the CPU), else keeps its last one (0.5
  at first). The rewrite takes the camera as in a Titan when it is over
  a Titan map's square (it has no soldier-in-Titan test of the
  renderer's), the Titans from `LevelSources::titanObject`.

**The light manager's other colours.** All of `lightManager.*` is now
registered; `enableSun` gates the sun term. What RendDX9 does with the
rest (the light manager `DAT_101ffc84`; per-frame table `DAT_101fae14`
filled at `0x1002a4a0` / `0x1002cef0`):

- `treeSkyColor` is uploaded as TreeSkyColor × 0.5 (table 0x138) but no
  shipped shader reads it (commented out in RaShaderLeaf.fx and
  RaShaderTrunkSTMDetail.fx): settled unused. Trees take OverGrowthAmbient
  from `treeAmbientColor` and their light from `treeSunColor`.
- `staticSpecularColor` (StaticSpecularColor, 0x1d8): RaShaderSTM's
  `pow(saturate(N·H), 32) × lightmap.g × gloss` times it (the gloss the
  detail map's alpha when the technique has a detail layer and isn't
  alpha-tested, else StaticGloss: `getCompositeDiffuse`); `sunSpecColor`
  builds SpecLUT64SpecularColor (`0x1014aec0` → `0x101ac540`: a 256 × 1
  texture, texel `i` = `(i/255)^64 × sunSpec`) that BM per-pixel
  specular samples at H·N times the gloss (the colour map's alpha with a
  ColormapGloss technique, else StaticGloss, `setSpecularStaticGloss`,
  default 0.15), killed by the shadow and the hemi occlusion. Drawn by
  mesh.frag's `specularTerm` (LightingUniforms `eye` / `specular`; the
  submesh's `specularKind` from its effect and technique). Bundled meshes
  without a normal map or ColormapGloss take the per-pixel LUT with
  StaticGloss where RaShaderBM lights them per vertex (`lit(N·L, R·V,
  SpecularPower)` clamped to StaticGloss). Skinned meshes (RaShaderSM):
  pow(N·H, SpecularPower) × the gloss × the sun's specular colour,
  SpecularPower the material block's default 20 (`0x10040070` +0x74), the
  gloss the normal map's alpha, else StaticGloss 0.15 (and nothing facing
  away, lit()).
- *Normal maps* (RaShaderBM/SM `_HASNORMALMAP_`, at the top lighting level
  only): a bundled mesh's second map ending "_b.dds" (`0x101499b0` +0x35)
  is in tangent space; a skinned mesh's second map unless the SpecularLUT
  is in tangent space when the technique names "tangent" (`0x100d4160`
  +0x100), else in object space (`_OBJSPACENORMALMAP_`: the first-person
  arms' "_b_os.dds"). The tangent is the vertex's TANGENT, the binormal
  cross(tangent, normal) × (1 − 2 × the third blend-index byte)
  (createWorld2TanMat / getTangentBasis). The tangent and the sign are
  the vertex's (`Vertex::tangent`), mesh.vert hands mesh.frag the map's frame in the world,
  and the map is bound in the dirt map's place; the bumped normal lights
  the sun, the point lights and the specular, a skinned mesh's hemi lerp
  too (per pixel at RAPATH 0), its alpha is the gloss unless the colour
  map's (ColormapGloss). `LevelStats::normalMapped` counts them (17 on
  Cerbere Landing at load).
- `effectSunColor` / `effectShadowColor` light the particles (FXCommon.fx
  `calcParticleLighting`: `lerp(1, lerp(shadow, sun, saturate(lm + off)),
  f)`, `lm` the base hemi map's alpha under the particle, `off` =
  `saturate(clamp((y − HemiShadowAltitude) / 10, 0, 1) +
  lightMapIntensityOffset)` (vsParticle), `f` the light factor).
  Settled: HemiShadowAltitude is the base hemi map's fourth argument (the
  height, 500 in every Sky.con; HemiMapManager's map `+0x44`, uploaded by
  the sprite manager's `0x10131d70`); the light factor is the template's
  `+0x1fc` (TemplateParameters `m_color1AndLightFactor.a`), which the
  constructor `0x10138b40` sets to −1 and no script property reaches
  (its setter, slot 0x15c, has no caller), so `0x10139800` takes
  `lightManager.defaultEffectLightAffectionFactor` (1 on every level).
  The shader quality (`ParticleSystemManager.particleSystemShaderQuality`,
  the effects row's) picks psParticleLow (1: unlit), Medium (2: `lm` 1)
  or High (3: the hemi map). The rewrite lights each particle on the CPU
  (`LevelRenderer::particleLight`, the hemi map's alpha decoded from its
  DXT5 blocks, a level of at most 512 texels; `hemiShadowAt`).

**Environment maps** (`envmapManager.*`, EnvMapManager `DAT_101ff9cc`,
vtable `0x101c6378`). At level load `0x100639b0` reads
`<level>/Envmaps/EnvironmentMapInfo.emi` (`loadEMIFile` `0x10064770`:
lines `EnvMapN x,y,z,bool`); each frame `0x10064f30` binds the entry
nearest the camera as the one cube for bundled materials whose technique
names "envmap" and static meshes (BM `_HASENVMAP_`: `lerp(diffuse,
texCUBE(R), gloss / 4)` with a Fresnel alpha; reflection scale
`setMaterialReflectionScale`, default 0.25), and the Titan interiors bind
`common/textures/indoorenvmap`. `generateEnvMaps` and `save` are the
editor's. Every retail level ships its .emi in the server archive (Cerbere
Landing, Belgrade: one map, `EnvMap0 -88,54,66,1`) and the cubes in the
client's. The static drawables take the cube unconditionally (`0x100bdb00`,
`+0x13c`), the bundled ones with an envmap material (`0x100c5030`,
`+0x37` → `+0x120`; with no cube a technique without, `0x1014e570`).
RaShaderSTM lerps the lit colour towards the cube: per pixel at the
reflection off the bumped normal by (1 − saturate(0.95 (E·N)²)) × gloss,
per vertex by gloss × 2 × (1 − |E·N|); RaShaderBM the diffuse by gloss / 4
before lighting. Rewritten in `src/Render/EnvMaps.h` (the parse and the
nearest map) and mesh.frag (sampler 10). The Titan interiors' indoor cube
(EnvMapManager +0x6c, `common/textures/indoorenvmap`, loaded by
`0x10063900`) replaces it for the envmap materials of bundled meshes drawn
by the interior path (`0x100c3880`: material +0x37 → +0x120); the static
interior path binds none of its own (`LevelRenderer::DrawItem::interior`).

**Sky layers and the sun flare** (`0x100fd2f0`, `0x100fd900`, SkyDome.fx).
With `skyDome.hasCloudLayer` the dome's technique is SkyDomeNV3x (one
cloud texture on the dome's second coordinate set, scrolled by TEXOFFSET),
with `hasCloudLayer2` SkyDomeNV3xDualClouds (`cloud × lerp.x + cloud2 ×
lerp.y`; the choice, `0x100fc410` when the cloud count changes and
again each frame in `0x100fd2f0`: DualClouds needs both flags and two
clouds, SkyDomeNV3x the first and one, else SkyDomeNV3xNoClouds; the
effect and its handles `0x100fcd80`; `LevelRenderer::buildSkyLayers`'s
cloud count); both fade out from CLOUDSFADEOUTDIST = (fadeCloudsDistances.x,
y − x) along the dome's radius and below its horizon, then `lerp(sky, c,
c.a)`. The offsets grow by `scrollDirection` a second. The flare is the
flare template's sprite (`Skydome.flareTexture`, loaded by `0x100fc9f0`:
none for an empty name, the "flaresprite" quad made once) towards
`-flareDirection`, added (SkyDomeSunFlare:
ONE/ONE, no depth test) at a strength of the occlusion query's visible
share (`(visible / total + flareFadeAdd) × flareFadeMul`, `SkyDomeFlareOccludeCheck`
every few frames); the rewrite draws a camera-facing quad of the flare
texture 4 km out, depth-tested instead of the query, brightest looking
into it. `renderer.drawSunFlare` and `skyDome.domeSize` are not read.

**Post-production** (PostProduction_nv3x.fx, FSQuadDrawer.fx; the object
`0x1004a590` constructs, `DAT_101fb808`; driven from the renderer's frame
at `0x1002df12`..`0x1002e6d0`). The order:

1. *Glow and camouflage* (`0x1004a0b0`, `0x10049560`, `0x10048a80`,
   `0x100495f0`, `0x10048b50`). Cloaked soldiers draw with
   RaShaderSMActiveCamo.fx / RaShaderBMActiveCammo.fx technique Camouflage
   (alpha only); FSBMExtractCamouflage (`(max(0.4, a) − 0.5) × 2`), a 5 × 5
   blur and FSBMCamouflageBlurPassThrough blend the backbuffer shifted by
   CAMOUFLAGEOFFSET (`renderer.camouflageOffset`), its luminance's
   contrast × 0.1 added, by that mask: the soldier refracts what is behind
   him. The rewrite draws cloaked soldiers (GameWorld hides them; the
   renderer asks `LevelSources::cloaked`) into a mask tested against the
   world's depth. *Glow is dead code in RendDX9.* The list at
   `*(DAT_101fae6c + 0x38)` is not a glow list: `DAT_101fae6c` is the
   RaShader manager (ctor `0x1003ed70`), its +4..+0x3c the 15 render
   queues (`0x10038250`), and +0x38 is RSMTCamouflage, filled only by the
   bundled mesh (`0x100c2990`, BMActiveCammo / AdditiveAlpha) and the
   skinned mesh (`0x10161150`, SMActiveCamo Camouflage, or
   BrokenCamouflage flickering by a random draw): the cloaked soldiers'
   mask above. The glow passes (`0x10049560` ExtractGlow, `0x100495f0` →
   `0x10048c40` GlowH/GlowV and the additive composite) run only when
   PostProduction `+0x21` is set, which only `0x10048d10` (GlowMaterial
   with GLOWSTRENGTH) does, and neither it nor `0x10048e80` (Glow) has a
   caller or a pointer anywhere in the DLL. `renderer.glowEnabled`
   (`0x1004ed50` → `+0x20`, default 0) and `renderer.glowStrength`
   (`0x1004eee0` → `+0xe8`, 0.5) are read only by that dead function, and
   `renderer.colorBrightness` (`0x1004fad0` → `0x10035c40`, `+0xa58`..)
   only by its getter: all three are stored, and nothing glows. The
   shipped `hasGlow 1` (the EU Titan's monitor, the floodlight cones) and
   its `glowFrequency` / `glowType` / `glowOffset` are the EXE's SimpleObject
   template `+0x228..+0x234`, which only their console rows
   (`0x0051be6e`, `0x0051c27a`, `0x0051c397`, `0x0051c4ab`) touch: no
   getter in any vtable, no other access. Inert.
2. *Bloom* (`0x10049140`): FSBMContrastFilter (pass 28: the backbuffer
   cubed, to luminance, less CONTRAST = `bloomFilterContrast`) into a
   small target, FSBMLargeBloomFilter across (pass 29: 13 taps 0.01 and
   0.015 × BLOOMSIZE × 1..3 apart, weighted 1, 0.45 .. 0.15 × BLOOMWEIGHTSCALE
   × 0.9), FSBMGaussianBlur5x5Cheap (10), the large bloom down (30), then
   Soften: `saturate(backbuffer + bloom × GLOWSTRENGTH)` with GLOWSTRENGTH
   = `bloomOverlayAmount`; `showBloomOverlayTexture` shows the bloom alone.
   The setters `0x100508d0`..`0x10050f80` write +0x104..+0x114; defaults 1,
   1, 1, 0.2. The rewrite's small targets are a quarter of the screen.
   `VideoSettings.setUseBloom` (the menu's BloomEnabled) turns it off.
3. *Tinnitus* (`0x1004a2f0`) instead of the bloom while one runs: the game
   logic's event 0xd (ECGameLogicGLTinnitus, data type 1 and three times,
   Sound.tinnitusSetup's 1 2 4) lasts `(a + b + c) × 30` frames (at least
   20, `0x10049440`); the last four frames weighted 0.5, 0.25, 0.125,
   0.0675 at a random SAMPLEOFFSET, lerped to the frame by its progress
   (halved below one half).
4. *Colour grade* (`0x1004a120` then ColorTransform `0x10049a40`): the
   matrix `0x10049900` builds, `out_r = Σ_c ((1 − s) lum_c + s[r = c]) tint_c in_c`
   (lum 0.3086, 0.6094, 0.0820; s `defaultSaturation`, tint
   `defaultColorTint`), transposed into COLORTRANSFORMMATRIX, then
   CONTRASTPOLYNOM `a x + b x² + c` (`defaultContrast`; Camp Gibraltar's
   2.1/−1/−0.04 lifts the mid-tones). It runs unless the view is tinted or
   the player is EMPed (`0x10025be0`). CameraEffect (`0x10049b90`) takes its
   place while the view's camera asks for it: the same grade on a
   fisheye from `common/textures/frame` with `common/textures/scanline`
   rolling (FRACTIME + 0.15 a frame's seconds, used below 1, reset at
   1.5). The backbuffer is read wrapped (sampler0bilinwrap: the scanline's
   3 % push past the right edge comes in from the left) and the scanline
   point sampled and wrapped (sampler2wrap). The streaks at the left and
   right edges of these views are the effect itself: frame.dds is white in
   the middle with vertical ridges towards its sides, so the fisheye's
   `(uv − 0.5)³ × frame × 0.5` moves each ridge's columns by a different
   amount (up to 0.06 of the screen vertically near the corners). The exe
   asks for it from the HUD manager's vehicle HUD (RendDX9 `0x1002e2xx`
   calls HudManager slot 0x2b8 → `+0xd8`, the object `0x007a24c0` builds,
   whose slot 0x20, `0x007a0080`, is true when the player's object's
   PostProcess component has settings for the HUD's gui index). The
   rewrite turns it on in a vehicle seat in first person whose
   weapon's `weaponHud.enablePostProcessingOnGuiIndex` names the HUD shown
   (`altGuiIndex` zoomed, else `guiIndex`: the tanks' and walkers' zoomed
   sights, and unzoomed guns such as the FAV gunner's machine gun, whose
   `guiIndex` and `enablePostProcessingOnGuiIndex` are both 74). Also on
   in the inside view of a seat whose controlled template sets
   `vehicleHud.enablePostProcessingOnGuiIndex` (a 32-bit flag at the
   template's `+0x11c`, setter slot 0x158 `0x006376c0`, executor
   `0x00554a71`; 48 seats: the APCs' pod cannons and second turret, the
   tanks' cupolas and driver cameras, the ATs' passenger guns, whose guns
   carry no weapon-side index). That flag's reader isn't traced; the seats
   that set it are taken to turn the pass on for their own view
   (`menu::seatPostProcessing`).
5. *EMP* (`0x10049d70`): a vehicle's EMP level (the player's slot 0x380)
   loads the static from the table `0x10048950` builds (`0x10048a30`:
   INTERFERENCE 0 then 8 for levels 1-5, DISTORTIONROLL 0 then 0.02, no
   warp) and a second grade (`0x1004a280`: the view's colour at saturation
   0 when the view is tinted, else neutral); a soldier's level + 3 (5 for
   3) with the saturation swinging ±3 by 0.01 a frame. `psDx9_EMP20`: the
   random texture's row shifts the image across by DISTORTIONROLL, the
   static takes from it and adds a little red, the contrast polynomial
   again. `renderer.emp*` (`0x10050250`..`0x10050730`) override the table.
6. *Titan explosion* (event 0x14, `0x10049360`, run by `0x1004a120`): the
   grade's tint 1 + 20 t with the contrast's constant t / 2 for two
   seconds, then white (tint 40, saturation 0, + 1) until 12 s. The
   rewrite starts it when `GameWorld::titans()` reports a core explosion.
7. *TVEffect* (`0x10048f80`, `ps_TVEffect20`: grey image, rolled by the
   noise and `1 − x²` bands, the random texture's interference; the
   PostProcess component's `tvInterference`, `tvDistortionRoll`,
   `tvDistortionFreq`, `tvDistortionScale`): no direct call or vtable
   slot reaches it in RendDX9, but it is the view through a guided
   round's camera (`useProjectileCamera`, see the projectile camera
   above). The rewrite (`PostEffects::tv`) turns it on while
   `GameWorld::projectileCamera` gives the local player a round's camera
   (main.cpp's postEffects), and off when the round goes and the view
   comes back (`0x005b4b00`).

The rewrite does all of these in one full-screen pass: the passes that
move pixels (the roll, the fisheye, the TV's bands) read the earlier
stages at the moved coordinates. `renderer.drawPostProduction 0` draws
the world straight into the target. `BF2142_POST_EFFECT=emp:N |
soldieremp:N | tinnitus | tv | camera | flash | camo` forces one for a
screenshot. PostProduction's Fog (a full-screen fog from a position
buffer) and ThermopticCamouflage (returns black) techniques are named
nowhere in RendDX9 (no technique string selects them): not drawn; fog
stays in the shaders, the camouflage is FSQuadDrawer's passes above.
The game state: the soldier's own EMP level is its armour's on foot
(the player's `0x005921b0` walks from its control object to the first
armour, slot `0x14c`), which an EMP raises like a vehicle's when the
soldier template has `armor.takesEmpDamage` (no shipped soldier sets it);
`PlayerInfo::empLevel`. The tinnitus event's sender is the blast shake
(no `sound-tinnitus-range` setting exists in BF2142.exe): `0x005a6e70` posts
event 0xd for a local soldier on foot within 0.6 × a blast's radius (see
**Blast shake**; `GameWorld::takeTinnitus`, the setup's 1 + 2 + 4 s). The view's tint colour (its slot 0x7c) is not decoded.

## Kits on the ground

`src/Game/Kits.cpp`. A dead soldier's kit (on foot or thrown out of a
seat) drops (`0x00589890`): its items go back in with their rounds, and a
ray 1000 m straight down from the soldier places it on what it meets
(statics, bodies, the terrain); on a Titan it rides with it
(`0x00561b20` / `0x005ad2e0`, put at the Titan's position plus its offset
each tick, `0x005aa5b0`). It lies timeToLiveAfterDeath (kit template
`+0x2b8`, 30 s by default, `0x00570080`) and goes. ServerGameLogic's
pickUpClosestKit (`0x004bcd80`): the closest kit within the radius whose
slot 0x24 matches the holder's 0x20 (the soldier template's `+0x2bc`
against the kit's ItemContainer `+0x2a4`, neither set by a script: every
kit); the taker drops his own first (`0x0058b680`), takes its items with
their rounds and its battery, holds the first from slot 3 up, and the
player's kit time stamp is set. The use key asks for one within 3 m when
no vehicle takes the soldier and 2 s have passed (`0x004bda00`); a revive
within 10 m, else a new kit (`0x00587b90` event 0x19, `0x004bfcc0`).
DropKit and PickupKit go to the scripts. The renderer should draw a lying
kit with its `geometry.dropGeom` (`GameWorld::isDroppedKit`).

## Ragdolls

A dead soldier's body is a ragdoll: particles on a few skeleton bones,
held together by constraints, which then pose the skeleton. The code is
`BF2/Animation/BoneAnimation/RagDoll.cpp` (`0x008a7900`–`0x008ae4e0`). One
template, the RagDoll manager (`DAT_00b4cb94`, built by `0x008adac0`), is
filled by the `ragDoll.*` console methods in
`Objects/Soldiers/Common/Animations/ragDollInit.con` and its
`ragDollConstraints.inc`:

- `addParticle bone mass` (`0x008abe00`): 13 particles on the hips (1, 6),
  knees (2, 7), feet (4, 9), shoulders (15, 31), elbows (16, 32), wrists
  (19, 34) and head (47). Knees get `ragdoll_kneeBoneSize` (0.05 m) as
  their radius, hips and shoulders `ragdoll_bodyBoneSize` (0.12 m), the
  rest `ragdoll_boneSize` (0.1 m). The right hip's particle is the middle
  one: where the body is.
- `addConstraint a b` (`0x008ab1c0`): a fixed distance, measured on the
  setup skeleton named by `ragDoll.skeleton` (`0x008a7b70`).
  `addDistanceLessThanConstraint a b d` (`0x008ab140`) keeps two particles
  at least `d` apart (the wrists from the hips).
- `addAngularConstraint a b c degrees` (`0x008aae60`) turns the angle at
  b into a distance a–c by the law of cosines: a minimum, or a maximum for
  a negative angle. The same triple again replaces the limit, so the
  file's pairs such as `1 2 4 110` then `1 2 4 -150` leave only the
  second. `addDihedralAngleConstraint a b c d degrees` (`0x008aafb0`)
  keeps the arms a–b and c–d from folding together: their sum must be at
  least `sqrt(ab² + cd² − 2·ab·cd·cos)` long.
- `addCapsuleCollision a b` (`0x008ab250`): segments that collide with
  objects.
- `lockBone from to` (`0x008aadf0`): bones (fingers, face, the weapon's
  mesh nodes) that keep their pose relative to their parents.
- `toSkeleton bone a b` (`0x008abbd0`): how a bone's matrix is rebuilt
  (below).

The `ragdoll_*` variables are registered by static initialisers at
`0x008ffa00`–`0x008ffe60`. `ragdoll_dT` is 1/90 s, `ragdoll_iterations`
2, `ragdoll_sleep` 2.5 s, `ragdoll_sleepDelta` 0.02 m,
`ragdoll-max-inherit-speed` 40 m/s and `ragdoll_expRotateForce` 13.
`ragDollInit.con` sets `ragdoll_slowMotion` to 0.75 and
`ragdoll_gravityOverTime` to 0.1 s. The manager's gravity
(`ragDoll.gravity`) defaults to −30 m/s².

At death (`0x005f0a00`) the soldier poses its skeleton a metre below its
object and starts an instance (`0x008adc00`, `0x008aca60`). Each particle
sits at its bone, and its previous position is 0.015 s of the body's
velocity behind (the velocity is clamped to the inherit speed). If an
explosion killed it, the explosion's push, kept by `0x005ee4d0` times
`rd_expForceMod`, goes to `addForce` with bone −2 (`0x008aa1c0`). A
negative bone pushes the legs against the body's normal and the rest
along the push, both times `ragdoll_expRotateForce`, so the body turns
over.

A frame (`0x008add10`) scales its time by `ragdoll_slowMotion` and runs
`round(time / dT)` fixed steps. A step does three things:

1. **Forces** (`0x008a8a10`): force / mass, plus gravity times a ramp that
   reaches 1 after `ragdoll_gravityOverTime`.
2. **Verlet** (`0x008a8860`): the displacement `(x − x_prev) + a·dT²` is
   averaged with the previous step's before it is added. This damps the
   motion.
3. **Constraints and collisions** (`0x008ac8f0`), `ragdoll_iterations`
   times: angular (`0x008a8f30`; a violated limit is followed by putting
   a–b and b–c back to length, with the inverse masses mixed as the
   original mixes them), dihedral (`0x008a92f0`), the legs' bend
   (`0x008aa360`; only `legPointForward` is active, at 0.01), the minimum
   distances (`0x008a8db0`), the distances (`0x008a8c40`, by inverse
   mass), then collisions (`0x008ac200`). The collisions keep the shins
   from crossing (`0x008a8ac0`). Each particle is then tested against
   objects, and failing that the terrain, with a segment from its
   previous position to a radius past its new one. A particle moving into
   a face is put back so the segment's end lies on the face, and its
   previous position is set to the new one: it stops dead, which is the
   ragdoll's friction. A particle that starts under the terrain is lifted
   1 % of the way a pass. Last, the capsules are pushed out of objects
   (`0x008abf20`).

Once the middle particle moves less than `ragdoll_sleepDelta` a frame for
`ragdoll_sleep` seconds, the instance sleeps. Asleep, every 1/30 s it
rebuilds its object list and wakes (`0x008a79d0`) on the first object
whose physics isn't at rest and moves at 0.001 m/s or more. `addForce`
also wakes it, but only the first force counts (`+0x1c` is never
cleared), so a later explosion's push neither moves nor wakes a settled
body. Each awake frame, whatever lies under the middle particle (a ray 2 m
down, `0x006f2250`) carries every particle and its previous position by
its point velocity × 1/30 s (`0x008add10`).

**The object list** (`0x008ab6b0`, each solve): the objects with
collision for soldiers whose physics flags lack `0x10` and whose soldier
LOD box comes within `ragdoll_completeCollRadius` (1.5 m) of the middle
particle (`0x006aec10`): static objects and vehicles. A particle's
segment goes through each in list order (collision-mesh slot 22 at LOD
2); the first face it moves into stops it. The capsules (`0x008abf20`,
with `ragdoll_useCapsuleCollision`) go through each object's slot 25
(`0x006e2ee0`, per face `0x006be990`), which tests the segment a→b with
a's radius against the faces' edges only: for each edge, where the
segment comes within the radius (`0x006bde70`), two crossings giving
