| 2 | the set's index | talk into another set (`0x00711710`) |
| 3 | the sets' indices, then their count | talk into several sets (`0x00711c10`) |
| 4, 5 | none | start or stop logging this player's voice to `VoiceTraffic_Player_*` (`0x10007060`, `0x10007230`; only while the routing log is open, and 4 only with quality 2) |
| 6 | none | keep-alive, the whole packet is 3 bytes (`0x00711760`), every 3 s |

There's no login. A packet with a session the game server announced is
accepted, and its source address becomes that client's (`0x10008b40`).
The keep-alives register the address before the player talks.

The voice payload is whole Speex frames followed by the 16-bit frame
sequence number of the first one (`0x0043be90`). The server appends the
speaker's player id (16 bits). It sends the packet to every listener of
every channel in the chosen sets, except the speaker, clients with no
address yet, and the speaker's own address (`0x10008830`,
`0x100088e0`). The client takes the speaker and the sequence off the end
(`0x0043c0b0`) and drops speakers it muted.

How the Bf2VoipClient picks its sets:

- A squad member uses set 0.
- A squad leader holding `c_GIVoipUseLeaderChannel` (B) uses set 1, the
  commander (`0x0043be40`).
- A commander holding it talks to all squad leaders. Otherwise the
  commander talks to the squads selected on the commander screen, as a
  multi-set packet (`0x0043cd40`). The selection is read only while that
  screen is open. If the screen is open and no squad is selected, the
  commander is held back (`+0xc0`); `0x0043c8d0` clears that once the
  screen closes. If the screen is closed, the last selection stays.
- Only commanders and squad members may talk (`0x0043c8d0`).
- After more than 10 s of talk (`+0xa8`, counted from the first captured
  packet, sent or not) the client is blocked (`0x0043c140` ->
  `0x0043c290(1)`; player `+0x388`) and sends nothing. A talk ends after
  0.5 s without voice (player `+0x398`). The block is lifted on the next
  update after that (`0x0043c8d0`). The 5 s stored at `+0xb8` is never
  read, so talking on keeps the block.

### Codec and audio

Speex narrowband (`speex_nb_mode` at `0x00a090a4`, bit-stream version 4)
runs at 8 kHz with 20 ms frames of 160 samples. The decoder's perceptual
enhancement is on. `sv.voipQuality` 1-5 becomes GameSpy Voice's codec
4..0 (`0x00711120`) and Speex quality 1, 2, 4, 7 or 10 (`0x007217f0`). Any
other value gives 2.

A frame is written as `SPEEX_GET_BITRATE / 50 / 8` bytes (`0x00737b89`):
9, 14, 20, 37 and 61 bytes. That cuts the last 4-7 bits of a frame at
every quality but 3, and the decoder reads them as zeros. The rewrite does
the same, so frames stay the size the original's clients expect.

The capture path (`0x007210f0`):

1. DirectSound captures 8 kHz mono 16-bit. The rewrite uses SDL3 audio
   streams.
2. A frame is sent when one of its samples exceeds
   `voipCaptureThreshold` × 32767, and for 20 frames after the last loud
   one (`0x00737a20`). With push-to-talk (`c_GIVoipPushToTalk`, V) the
   threshold is 0 while the key is held and 1 when it's released
   (`0x0043bdd0`).
3. The capture volume scales the samples.
4. BF2142's filter runs: an RBJ band-pass at 2500 Hz with a bandwidth of
   1.75, at 8000 Hz, its output doubled and clamped. The filter's history
   is cleared every frame (`0x00712250` set up by `0x0043c420`, run by
   `0x0043bb60`).
5. Speex encodes the frame.

`voipBoostEnabled` never scales samples. `0x0070ff50` finds the
microphone line on the OS mixer's two destinations: component type
`0x1003`, or a name containing "Mic" (`0x0070fa90`). It switches that
line's LOUDNESS control (`0x20010004`), or its ONOFF control
(`0x20010001`), with `mixerSetControlDetails`. How much this adds depends
on the sound card driver, so it can't be known from the binary. The usual
case is AC'97's "Mic +20 dB". The rewrite adds those 20 dB itself.

The mic test (`0x007115e0`) loops the encoded frames straight into
playback.

On playback the rewrite follows GameSpy Voice 2's source list
(`0x00737710` adds a packet, `0x00737630` stores its frames, `0x00737590`
makes a source, `0x007378c0` mixes):

- There are up to 8 sources. A new speaker takes a free source, or else
  the first source whose frames have all played; failing both, the packet
  is dropped.
- Frames are stamped on a 16-bit play clock that counts mixed frames. A
  speaker's first packet gets the offset `clock - sequence + 10`, so it
  plays 200 ms later (`DAT_00b2d084`).
- Every later packet's offset feeds a running average
  (`avg × 31/32 + offset/32`, unwrapped by `0xffff`). If the source's
  offset is more than 10 above the average, it goes down by one and the
  packet's first frame is dropped. If it is more than 5 below, it goes up
  by one.
- A packet whose first frame is already behind the clock is dropped, as is
  one whose stamp is already in the list.
- Mixing decodes the frames stamped with the current clock and drops older
  ones. Nothing is concealed: a missing frame plays as silence. A source
  is freed once it is drained and past its last frame.
- The rewrite paces mixing by the wall clock, capped by the device's queue.
  This stands in for DirectSound's write cursor.

A speaker counts as talking for 500 ms after a packet.

### How a client starts

1. The server's settings transfer (data block 0, written by `0x00515bc0`)
   carries:
   - the server name (a u16 length and the text)
   - a u16 count of u16-length strings
   - seven flags, the second being voipEnabled
   - the voice server's IPv4 address (32 bits, network order; 1 means the
     game server's own)
   - `sv.voipServerPort` and `sv.voipBFClientPort` (16 bits each)
   - `sv.voipQuality` (a sign bit and 31 bits)
2. `0x004ab030` keeps these values in clientGameLogic (`0x004cbdb0`).
3. The VoipSession event (`0x00512250`) gives the local player its session.
4. clientGameLogic starts the client (`0x004cbe40` → `0x0043c630`).

VoipPlayerMute (0x26: mute, the muted player, the player muting) and
VoipOnOff (0x23: a player and whether their voice is on) go to the
players. The order of the settings flags around voipEnabled follows the
writer, but a live server's block hasn't been checked against it.

Rewritten in `src/Voip`:

- `VoipProtocol`: every format above.
- `VoipCodec`: Speex.
- `VoipServer`: the instance and CBF2VoipServer.
- `VoipServerConnection`: the game server's side.
- `VoipClient`: the client.
- `VoiceChat`: settings, events, role and keys around the client, on its
  own thread in the game.
- `VoipNatives`: the menu's `dice.bf2.Sound.voip*` natives (SwiffPlayer
  0x10059fa0..0x1005adf0). They work only after voipInitialize
  (0x10059fa0, flag DAT_1012c004), which opens the devices and loads
  AudioSettings' playback / capture volumes, boost and threshold into the
  client. Every setter writes the client and the AudioSettings object
  alike: voipSetEnable (0x1005a240) slot 0x3c and the client's disable
  (0x98), voipSetRecieveVolume (0x1005a850) 0x44, voipSetTransmitVolume
  (0x1005a6e0) 0x4c, voipSetThresholdVolume (0x1005a9c0) 0x54, voipSetBoost
  (0x1005aac0) 0x5c. voipGetEnable (0x1005a350) reads AudioSettings (0x38),
  false before voipInitialize; the other getters read the client.
  voipStartTest (0x1005a470) runs the loopback with the threshold at 0 and
  voipStopTest (0x1005a5b0) puts back the threshold set meanwhile (client
  and AudioSettings). Push-to-talk (0x1005acb0 / 0x1005adf0) is the
  client's alone. MenuBindings keeps inert stand-ins (voipInitialize
  false) for a menu without voice chat (`Voip_NativesWriteAudioSettings`).

`bf2142` binds the natives over MenuBindings' stand-ins, writing through
to its AudioSettings (`MenuBindings::storeSetting`), and applies
`AudioSettings.Voip*`. On a joined
server it feeds the data block, the voice events and the squad to
VoiceChat, and the viewer feeds the push-to-talk and leader-channel keys.

The tests run loopback sessions with synthetic tones. They cover:

- authentication, refused passwords, versions and second servers
- squad, leader and commander routing
- muting, removal and the routing table's repair
- the talk limit
- voice activity
- the mic test

Not rewritten: the DLL's debug logs (`mods/bf2142/Logs/Voip/`:
`VoipServerRouting_Instance_*`, written by `0x10006610` after every game
server packet once DEBUG_DATA opened it, and `VoiceTraffic_Player_*`).
Packets 4, 5 and 200 feed nothing but those logs: nothing else reads the
names DEBUG_DATA stores. The rewrite accepts and drops them
(`VoipServerInstance::handle`); `onLog` carries the DLL's console lines.

## HUD

At start-up the engine runs `Menu/HUD/HudSetup/HudSetupMain.con`. Its
`hudBuilder` commands build a tree of nodes in an 800 x 600 screen below
six roots the engine provides: `Global`, `TopLayer`, and the bottom-left and
bottom-right `Static` and `Animate` corners. The node types are split,
transform, picture, text, bar, button, compass, object marker, list and a
few more. Nodes take their colour, alpha, RGB, position and texture from
HUD variables, which the game registers by name and binds to its own fields
(e.g. `0x0044c...` for the soldier's HUD information).

A node shows when its show variable is non-zero and every
`setNodeLogicShowVariable` term holds. `AND` and `EQUAL` test `variable ==
value`, and `NOT` tests `variable != value` (the engine builds a NOT node
over an EQUAL node; `0x007b0fd0`). An `OR` entry joins the term before it:
`NOT AffectedByEMPShow 1` followed by `OR UpdateAllEnabled 1` is one term.
A colour variable tints the node and everything below it, and a position
variable sets the coordinate once the game gives it a value.

RendDX9.dll draws the HUD twice a frame (`0x1002d5d9`):

1. With `AffectedByEMPShow` 0 and `UpdateAllEnabled` 1: the communication,
   game info and soldier parts.
2. With `AffectedByEMPShow` 1 and `UpdateAllEnabled` 0: the weapon and
   vehicle parts, which an EMP distorts.

The engine-side flag (`HudInformationLayer +0xb38`) is only ever set by the
renderer. The weapon HUDs pick their crosshair by `GuiIndex`, the template's
`weaponHud.guiIndex`. The parts take `Cross{Left,Right,Up,Down}Pos`
(`0x007be770`): the spread is the deviation in degrees times
`weaponHud.deviationFactor` (default 10), and the parts are 20 long about
the screen centre (Right = 400 + spread, Left = 399 - 20 - spread; the
spread pushed out by minVisualDeviation and held at maxVisualDeviation,
see the weapon HUD below). Their
colour comes from the profile's `game.setCrossHairColor` (0-255, in
`Settings/Profiles/Default/GeneralOptions.con`). Bars fill
by their value variable (types 0 up, 2 from the right, 3 from the left;
inferred). Text uses `.dif` fonts: a text header and glyph table with A/B/C
spacing, top offset and texture rectangle, kerning pairs, and a `.dds`
beside it. Textures are under `Menu/HUD/Texture/`, mostly `.tga`.

Rewritten in `src/Hud` (nodes, variables, fonts, quads), with the drawing
in `src/Render` (`ui.vert/.frag`) and the variables set in `src/Main`.
The exe's HUD reads the same managers on a server and a client (the
player manager's players, the teams, the control points, the spawn
manager's groups), which a client fills from the server's events and
ghosts. The rewrite's one HUD update (main.cpp's `updateHud` and its map,
commander, team and scoreboard parts, the squad bar) reads a
`host::HudWorld` (`src/Main/HudWorld.h`): `LocalHudWorld` over the local
round (GameWorld, GameLogic) or `RemoteHudWorld` over a joined game's
`net::RemoteWorld` (players, tickets, control points by their ghosts with
the ids of the spawn groups at them, the requests, our soldier from the
control-object record and its own state, the ghosts as the level's
objects). What only the local round has (gun aims, projectiles, Titans,
silos) it still asks the round, which a client has empty; the commanders'
assets are a client's ghosts (their tools' reloads its own uses') and the
range finder's ray the level's. The
corner roots stand where the "Ingame" MemeFile 2.0 (Menu_server.zip)
places them: BF2142.exe has no such strings, the names are that dice::meme
tree's (Global and TopLayer at 0, 0; BottomLeftStatic and
BottomRightStatic under transforms at −1, 563 and 401, 563; the Animate
pair under BfTransformNodes, factory `0x007edcf0`, serializer
`0x007ed800`, whose X follows BottomLeft_XPos — the slide `0x007a0a90`,
−295 / −137 / 54 — or BottomRight_XPos, 503, `0x007bee10`, plus their
350, 10 and 10, 10; no shipped script draws in them). The crosshair spreads by the
weapon's soldier deviation (`GameWorld::weaponDeviation`, see Soldier
deviation; a joined client's from its own moves), its minimum without
one.

### Text and the scoreboard

Text ids such as `HUD_TEXT_MENU_SCORE_PLAYERS` are looked up in
`Localization/strings.csv` (`0x00405360`: the registry's `Language`,
English by default, kept as the `GSLanguage` setting; English when the
file has no such column; the rewrite takes `--language`, and
`hud::language()` keeps it for the fonts and `Locale.getLanguage`; `strings_patch.csv`, the patch installer's
strings, is never read). The file is UTF-16LE, one row per line with
tab-separated columns: the id, then one column per language named in the
header row. Values may be quoted. Ids ignore case: the lexicon upper-cases
them when it stores and when it looks up (`0x0065b2c0`), and an id seen
twice keeps its first text (`0x006956f0`). This is rewritten in `src/IO/Localization`.

The fonts are per language: the `*Local*` HUD fonts exist only in
`Fonts/<language>/` (and `Fonts/<language>/800/` for 800 x 600), the
others also in `Fonts/` and `Fonts/800/`, and their glyphs are by Unicode
code point (Chinese_Simplified's hudFontLocalBold_9 has 1,447, up to the
0x9xxx ideographs). The HUD reads its text as UTF-8 (`hud::nextCode`: a
valid UTF-8 sequence is one code point, a lone byte stays itself, for the
lists' `\xa7` font switch and Latin-1 names), and looks for a font in the
language's folders first, then English's; the menus' engine fonts
(SwiffRender's `0x10185e90`) do the same (`Hud_NonEnglishTextHasGlyphs`:
every character of a sample of German, Russian, Chinese_Simplified and
Polish strings is a glyph of that language's font). The menus' own SWF fonts don't matter: SwiffRender
draws every edit text with an engine font (`ui::Drawer::engineFont`), and
the embedded ones in mainMenu.dfm carry Western sets only (no Cyrillic or
CJK; gameswf's glyph layout `0x100c06a0`, which skips a missing glyph,
isn't reached). The engine fonts the menu's edit texts use cover German,
Polish, Russian and Chinese_Simplified menu strings, except the 24 px
titles' StandardTextBold_24, which every language folder ships with its 98
Latin glyphs (`Dfm_MenuEngineFontsCoverLanguages`). RendDX9's `0x1017af30`
is not a font path: it maps the language to a Windows LCID (English 0x409,
French 0x40c, German 0x407, Italian 0x410, Russian 0x419, Swedish 0x41d,
Danish 0x406, Finnish 0x40b, Spanish 0x40a, Dutch 0x413, Polish 0x415,
Czech 0x405, Korean 0x412, Chinese 0xc04, Japanese 0x411, Thai 0x41e; by
SwiffHost's slot 0x3a8) for GetDateFormatA / GetTimeFormatA /
GetNumberFormatA (`0x1017b2a0`, `0x1017b370`, `0x1017b3f0`, `0x1017b460`),
whose only caller is SwiffHost's graph object (`0x10172af0`: its axis
dates and values), which the rewrite doesn't have.

The scoreboard (`ScoreboardShow`, menu state 0xd in `0x0079ab90`) is built
from list nodes. Each node names a data source with `setListNodeData`:

| Source | Contents |
|---|---|
| 2 | friendly players |
| 1 | enemy players |
| 10, 9 | the two teams' totals |
| 3 | chat |
| 5 | squad members |
| 12 | maps |

The engine sets the team names (`HUD_TEXT_MENU_SPAWN_ARMY_MEC` and
`_USMC`) and the flags, at `Ingame/Flags/Icons/Hud/Score/<team
name>/scoreBoard_Flag.tga`. The lists are BF2142.exe's
`Bf2NewListBoxNode` (render `0x007de7d0`; RendDX9.dll only draws quads):

- `setListNodeBorder top bottom left right` (`0x007add90`) also turns the
  border on. The background colour fills the node; the border colour's
  bands go top (across), right, bottom (up to the right band) and left.
  The top band is where the column headers go.
- Rows start at the top border plus the row spacing and go a row height
  plus the spacing apart while one fits above the bottom border. A
  selectable list (`createListNode`'s last argument) fills the selected
  row in the select colour (default (1, 1, 1, 0.5)) less the side borders.
- A cell's text sits at its column: left, centred, or right-aligned to the
  column's end (its x plus its width, else the node less the right
  border, 6 pixels in or clear of the scroll bar, `0x007dd800`); it is
  centred in the row by its glyphs' extent and stops at the glyph that
  leaves the column. `§n` switches to font n (0..3, `setListNodeFont`),
  `|c` toggles the highlight colour (0.996, 0.639, 0.169); outlined lists
  (`setListNodeOutline`) draw each glyph eight times one pixel around in
  (0.15, 0.15, 0.15) first.
- With more rows than fit, the scroll bar (`setListNodeScrollbar width
  margin`): its track down the right inside the borders, its thumb the
  shown share of the track less two rows (at least 4 pixels).
- The cells sit under `scoreboard_icons.tga`: score, teamwork, kills,
  deaths, ping.
- The text colour is the list data's per cell (`0x007ddb90`). The data
  sources come from the HUD manager's slot `0x214` (`0x007c6d70`: 1 and 2
  are the scoreboard's +0x394 / +0x38c lists, 9 and 10 its totals
  +0x398 / +0x390, made by `0x007b9aa0` with their 12 columns), and the
  scoreboard's row filler `0x007bb540` writes each cell (`0x007e0be0` /
  `0x007e0d60`: text, colour, flag) in font 1 (`"§1%s§0"` `0x009b4f1c`,
  `"§1%d§0"` `0x009b6854`) and one colour a row from three static tables
  (`0x008f24b0`, `0x008f2350`, `0x008f2400`), index 2 on the local
  player's team's list and 1 on the other: a player not alive (slot
  `0x74`, `+0xd5`) black (the scoreboard's grey rows take black text), the
  local player's squad (slot `0x120`) and the commanding local player
  (slot `0x128`) green (0.031, 0.467, 0.008), other friends blue (0, 0.38,
  1) and enemies red (0.992, 0, 0.004). The local player's row has the
  background (0.392, 0.392, 0.392, 0.35) and every odd row (0.651, 0.651,
  0.651, 0.8) (`0x007dd5d0`: the row's cells +0x6c/+0x70, filled between
  the side borders by `0x007de7d0` except on a selected row). The HUD
  manager's slot `0x410` and the player's `+0x404` (slot `0x3bc`, set
  through `0x3b8`) also make a row black; what they mean isn't traced.
  `menu::scoreboardStyle` (`src/Main/HudMenus`).
- Rows are sorted by the scripts' score. The "Squads" tab
  (`scoreboard.setToggleShow 1`, ToggleSquads) groups them
  (`menu::scoreboardBySquad`): the commander under
  "HUD_HUD_MENU_COMMANDER_HEADING" (`0x007bad00`, no totals), then each
  squad under its header row (`0x007baed0`: its number and name, squad 0
  "HUD_TEXT_MENU_SPAWN_SQUAD_UNASSIGNED" last) whose cells `0x007ba570`
  fills with the squad's score, teamwork, kills, deaths and average ping;
  the headers' text (0.5, 0.5, 0.5) (`0x00a0bc60`), the local player's
  squad's (0.141, 0.502, 0.259) (`0x00a0bba0`), on (0.843, 0.847, 0.847,
  0.9) (`0x00a0bc40`). The squad header's icon cell (`+0x330` at x
  `+0x300`, 15 x 15) isn't drawn.

Tab shows the scoreboard in play; `--scoreboard` forces it on.

Lists with commands (`setListNodeConCmd <event> <command>`: 1 a click, 2
a double click; the squad and commander menus' lists) take clicks on their
rows: the row is selected, the column under the pointer kept (the column
whose left edge is the nearest one left of it) and the commands run; a
second click on the same row within half a second runs event 2 as well.
The game reads the clicked row's cells back (`0x007dd3b0`), including
cells past the drawn columns (`HudManager::listCell`, `lastListClick`).

Every node but a split places its children from its own position: the
commander screen's tab pictures carry their buttons, labels and lists
(`CommanderToolsTabSelected` at 3,519 with its button at 0,0), as do the
transforms.

### The weapon, item selection and vehicle HUD

(`src/Main/HudMenusVehicles.*`.) The WeaponHud (class id `0xc4ee`,
properties from `0x00556f94`, written back by `0x006381d0`) and VehicleHud
(`0xc4ea`, from `0x005532c2`, written back by `0x00636440`, constructor
defaults `0x00637b30`) keep their fields in the template; the HUD reads
them through the component's slot 0x50 (weapon) / 0x78 (vehicle), a block
0x44 bytes below the template's fields (the weapon's guiIndex at +0xa8 is
the template's +0xec; hasMag +0x117, showAmmo +0x11a, showClips +0x11b,
showBatteryIconInHud +0x127), and their textures through slot 0x4c.

- **The weapon HUD** (`0x007c1f10`, the variables of `0x007bf6f0`):
  PrimaryAmmoShow while guiIndex isn't -1, PrimaryAmmoBarShow and
  PrimaryClipsShow by showAmmo and showClips (both default on),
  PrimaryWeaponNameString the hudName, CrosshairIconPathString,
  PrimaryAmmoBarFront/BackPathString; with hasMag and a magazine the clip
  icon (PrimaryClipPathString), else the ammo icon
  (PrimaryAmmoIconShow/PathString); FireRateIconShow and
  "Ingame/Weapons/Icons/Hud/firerate_<n>.tga" for hasFireRate and a fire
  rate n (`0x007be640`; the rewrite's firearms don't report one yet). The
  ammunition (unless the bar is off or a reload runs, which hides the
  texts, `0x007bede0`): no magazine (magSize < 0) shows PrimaryEternalShow
  with a full bar; else PrimaryAmmo rounds / magSize, PrimaryAmmoString,
  TotPrimaryAmmoString "/ %i" (all rounds), PrimarySingleFireShow for a
  magazine of one round, PrimaryBatteryIconShow for showBatteryIconInHud,
  PrimaryEternalMagsShow for endless magazines. The colours through the
  HUD manager's slot 0xa8 (`0x0074eb60`: below the threshold (0.949,
  0.184, 0.184), else white): the ammunition's below 0.3 of a magazine
  (0.1 for single rounds), the clips' below 0.3 of the magazines. The clips
  (`0x007be960`): PrimaryClip1..3Show for 1..3 spare magazines,
  PrimaryClipStringShow and PrimaryClipString "(%i)". The reload
  (PrimaryReloadTime / Show while between 0 and 1) and the heat. The
  overheat (the firearm's slot 0x2c) starts the weapon's overheatSound once
  each time (latched at +0xb0).
- **The item selection** (`0x0079bc70`..`0x0079c720`, the HUD manager's
  +0xf4, menu state 0xb): up to ten slots, the kit's weapons by item index
  (`0x0079c290`; 10 - index with `ItemSelection.setReverseItems`), packed
  from slot 0 at the bottom (`0x0079be20`): Item%iIcon the weapon's

  group with the key's slot flashing (`0x004d2a50` → `0x0079c190`; see a
  seat's weapons).

  (`menu::AbilityBar`, `GameWorld::abilityBar`.)

  DAT_00a6e194) and clears both at 1, so a scan shows for a second

  firer's drone (`0x005d9cf0` looks for a 0x9493 object), as the recon
  drones' does.

- **Read by nothing in BF2142.exe**: vehicleHud.typeIcon (string `+0x1f0`, its texture

- **useSelectionIcons** (block `+0xbc`, component `+0x104`, 0 by

  **The wheel and the pick** (`0x00755d50`, the HUD's input pass, run on
  the frame's input before the player's control object takes it): with
  the list allowed (above), the menu state 0 or 0xb and fire (input 8) not
  pressed, a wheel step (c_PINextItem 0x30 / c_PIPrevItem 0x31, Controls.con's
  `addAxisToTriggerMapping c_PINextItem c_PIPrevItem IDFMouse IDAxis_2`)
  sets the list's open time (`+0x20`) to 2.0 and state 0xb when it isn't
  open, then moves the selection: `0x0079c1e0` the next slot if it is
  usable (the entry's `+8`), else the first if usable, else nothing;
  `0x0079c230` the previous if usable, else the last if usable, else the
  first. A move selects by item index (`0x0079c120`: the open time anew,
  the HUD sound "weaponOver"). The pick: in state 0xb a press of fire
  takes the selected entry's item index + 0xd, clamped to 0xe..0x16
  (`0x0079bdb0`), and presses that input (PIWeaponSelect1..9, `0x00583880`
  sets the float when the mask has it), clears fire's float (input 8), and
  sets the list's `+0x38` to the time + `+0x30` (0.3, its constructor's).
  In states 0, 10 and 2 fire is cleared while the time is under `+0x38`:
  the pick's click and a held fire don't shoot for 0.3 s after the list
  shuts. The wheel's input is not cleared: it also reaches the weapon
  (the airburst distance below), whose range mode is on only zoomed in,
  and zoomed in (the firearm's slot 300) the list isn't allowed. The
  rewrite: `menu::ItemListInput` (main.cpp's itemListInput in both input
  handlers), `ItemSelection::next` / `previous` / `selectedItem`, the
  Viewer counting the wheel in play by the control map's axis-to-trigger
  bindings (`PlayerInput::itemStep`, `SoldierInput::itemStep`, sent as
  PIPrevItem / PINextItem) (`HudItemSelection_MouseWheel`). Not traced:
  the active weapon's `+0x14` bit 0 that also forbids the list.
- **canBeSpotted** (block `+0xc2`, 1 by default): the map node's spot

  unless it is alwaysShowOnMinimap (`+0xb1`); also read by `0x0075bfe0`

  object (`0x0075be30`) is that root, or its enemy rider's soldier when

  soldier; a joined client picks it from its own view
  (`menu::crosshairEnemy`) and sends its ghost's id, as the exe's client
  does (the server's `playerOf` takes a vehicle's occupant).
