  cannon, the static AA). The function's first test is vehicleHud
  `disableOnSprint` (above). The rewrite: WorldConsole keeps the lists as
  `<component>.showOnCamMode.list`, `menu::vehicleGuiIndex` and
  `showOnCamModes` (`HudVehicle_GuiIndexByCameraMode`).
- **weaponHud.showInfo** (template `+0x114`, block `+0xd0`, 1 by default;
  the horns Car_horn / Car_horn_Alt set 0): `0x007c1f10` runs `0x007c1b90`
  (the show flags off, CrosshairActive `+0xed` too unless the local player
  commands, slot 0x128) and stops after the crosshair's parts, so no name,
  icons or ammunition (PrimaryAmmoShow stays 0); the second weapon's
  `0x007c2d50` clears SecondaryAmmoShow (`+0x16d`) and stops
  (`HudWeapon_ShowInfoOff`). vehicleHud.showInfo (`+0xfe`) stays inert.
- **vehicleHud.useVehicleCameraRotation** (template `+0x108`, block
  `+0xc0`, getter slot 0xdc): the map node (`0x00793b60`, at `0x00794f03`)
  turns the object's icon by its first Camera child's yaw (`0x005c6430` →
  `0x005c63b0` with class 0x9472, `0x00998670`) less the map's rotation
  (`+0x80c`). Shipped on the sentry gun, the sentry drone and the drop pod.
  The rewrite turns a vehicle's icon by the seat yaw bundle that carries
  the camera (`menu::cameraRotationBundle`, `GameWorld::seatYaw`).
  The map node's list is the game's (`DAT_00a1c170` slot `0x1a4`) of the
  root objects with a PlayerControlObject (interface `0xc4c5`), so the
  map also takes what isn't a vehicle body here: the deployed sentry gun
  (`eu_sentrygun`, mini_sentry, vehicleType 3), the drones and the drop
  pods (`GameWorld::mapObjects`, added to the local HudWorld's
  vehicleList; a joined client's vehicleList already lists every
  PlayerControlObject ghost). The sentry drone's icon turns with its gun
  bundle (`unl_drone_sentry_guns`, its camera's parent), the heading the
  rewrite turns (`Drone::gunYaw`); the deployed gun doesn't turn in the
  rewrite, so its icon keeps the object's yaw. The pods set no
  miniMapIcon, only usePlayerIcon: their rider is the player's icon.

- **The blinks** (the blinker `0x00778040`, vtable `0x009b264c`, ticked
  with the frame's time by `0x00778080`; `menu::HudBlink`): 0x0079e5a0
  makes four with its variables (`0x0079fa9f`..`0x0079fb89`):
  PlayerHealthBlink (`+0x2ae`) on PlayerHealth (`+0x1cc`),
  VehicleArmorBlink (`+0x2b9`) on VehicleArmor (`+0x1d8`),
  PlayerStaminaBlink (`+0x2aa`) on PlayerStamina (`+0x1d0`) and
  VehicleStaminaBlink (`+0x2ac`) on VehicleStamina (`+0x1d4`), each with
  threshold 0.3, floor 0, periods 0.7 / 0.15, scaled. Below the threshold
  (the threshold not 0, the value not negative) the timer runs; past the
  period ((0.7 − 0.15) / 0.3 × value + 0.15) the flag toggles, or goes off
  at or below the floor, and the timer restarts; above it a lit flag goes
  out once the timer passes the period. The weapon HUD's constructor
  (`0x007bee10`, at `0x007bf20a`..`0x007bf393`) makes eight more, ticked
  by its frame (`0x007c40c0` → `0x00778420`) after the update:
  PrimaryAmmoBlink (`+0x15e`) on PrimaryAmmo (`+0xb4`) and
  SecondaryAmmoBlink (`+0x16a`) on SecondaryAmmo (`+0xc4`), 0.3 / 0 /
  0.7 / 0.15; PrimaryClipBlink (`+0x165`) on PrimaryClips (`+0x178`, the
  spare magazines) 1.5 / 0 / 0.3 / 0.15 and SecondaryClipBlink (`+0x172`)
  on SecondaryClips (`+0x1a4`) 0.7 / 0 / 0.3 / 0.15; FlareBlink (`+0x1de`)
  on FlaresReloadTime (`+0x1e0`) 0.98 / 0 / 0.7 / 0.15; TVBlink
  (`+0x15c`) with no value, toggling every 0.7 s; and the heat's two of
  the twin class (`0x007782f0`, vtable `0x009b2654`, tick `0x00778330`,
  which watches the value above the threshold and holds the flag off at
  or above the floor): PrimaryHeatBlink (`+0x15f`) on PrimaryHeatValue
  (`+0xf8`) and SecondaryHeatBlink (`+0x16b`) on SecondaryHeatValue
  (`+0xf4`), 0.7 / 1 / 0.3 / 0.15. The update (`0x007c1f10`) clears the
  ammunition's flag and sets its value to 1 without a magazine, clears
  the clips' and sets −1 without clips, leaves the ammunition's value
  as it was during a reload; the hidden HUD (`0x007c40c0`'s other
  branch) zeroes the ammunition values and the ammunition and clip
  flags and doesn't tick. Rewritten in `menu::WeaponHud` (`HudBlink`'s
  `Watch::above` and `tickFree`); FlareBlink isn't (the rewrite has no
  FlaresReloadTime: `0x007be490`'s flare launcher).
- **The other seats' turrets** (`0x007a2b50` → `0x007a1e00` →
  `0x007a07c0`; GunnerAngle `+0x20c`, SecondaryGunnerAngle `+0xb0`, used
  by the tank, APC and mech drivers' HUDs and the gunships'): with the
  local player in a vehicle, every PlayerControlObject of the root's list
  (its slot `0x64`) that isn't a soldier (interface `0xc4d7`) or his own
  seat is searched depth first for the first RotationalBundle (class
  `0x947d`) whose maxSpeed (`0x006147c0`) turns on the yaw alone; with the
  controlled object's showOneSecondaryGunnerAngle (block `+0xc1`, the
  APCs) only the first such seat, found or not. Of the bundles found, the
  first since entering is kept (`+0xa8`) and a second different one
  (`+0xac`); `0x007a1ee0` clears both as the controlled object becomes the
  soldier again. With one, GunnerAngle = clamp(−r, ±π) (r the bundle's
  rotation, slot `0x188`, degrees × π / 180); with two, the second gives
  SecondaryGunnerAngle = clamp(−(r + 1.5708)) and the first GunnerAngle =
  clamp(r − 1.5708) (the exe adds π / 2 to the degrees before turning them
  to radians). The rewrite keeps the HUD's angles in degrees (its picture
  rotations and compasses), the bundles by seat (`GameWorld::seatYaw`: the
  seat's yaw bundle's own rotation; a seat's yaw bundle is the look's
  RotationalBundle, which for the shipped turrets is the yaw-only one),
  in seat order (`menu::OtherSeat`, `VehicleHud::gunnerBundle`).
- **displaySelectionOnEnter** (block `+0xbd`): entering a seat
  (`0x007a3920`, from the enter event at `0x007a3cb0` for the local
  player) with it opens the item list for 2 s (`+0x20` = 2.0, menu state
  0xb) before `0x0079bdf0` packs it: the artillery guns as_ag / us_ag
  (main.cpp). The vehicle HUD's `+0xb4` that also stops it is written by
  the seat dots (`0x007a28e0`, called just before): for each occupied
  seat, 1 when its occupant's controlled object (player slot 0x4c) is a
  Parachute (class 0xc5a8) whose template's isPod (`+0x4cc`) is 0, else
  0, so the last occupied seat decides; `0x007a3180` clears it off a
  vehicle. No shipped parachute sets displaySelectionOnEnter
  (`menu::displaySelectionOnEnter`).
- **standardHelpEnabled** (block `+0xbb`, 1 by default): the help
  manager's exit message 0x48 (`0x00648948`: in a vehicle that isn't a
  LadderContainer) and enter message 0x47 (`0x00648872`: the controlled
  object, on foot the soldier) need the controlled object's flag; the
  static guns, the parachute, the bipods and the overhead camera set 0
  (`menu::standardHelpEnabled`, `HelpPopups::Context::standardHelp`).
- **useVehicleCommRose** (block `+0xbe`, 1): the radio key (`0x0075be30`)
  opens RadioVehicle (state 6) when the controlled object isn't the
  soldier, that rose is enabled (its slot `0x1c`, `+5`, 1 from
  `0x007b88e0`) and the flag is set; else Radio (state 5). The parachute,
  LadderContainer and the bipods set 0 (`menu::usesVehicleCommRose`).

- **MechFootAnimationValue** (`+0x244`, 0 from `0x007a24c0`):
  `0x007a0940`, for each PlayerControlObject (class `0xc4c2`) of the
  root's list with an animation system (slot `0x180`), asks the system's
  slot 0x40 (`0x008ba560`, last argument 1): the instance nearest the
  back of its playing list (the top) whose `+0x46` is set, the flag
  Forward / Side / Up / Movement / SlopeTriggers (`0x008c3a70`,
  `0x008c3b00`, `0x008c3bb0`, `0x008c46d0`, `0x008c4f00`) set on queueing
  a looping bundle (`+0x31`), gives the bundle's length × its rate and
  its time × its rate (|rate| × length and |rate| × (length − time) for a
  rate below 0; −1 and −1 without one). Under 0.3 s the value is 0, else
  sin(2π × min(time / length, 1)) + 1: 0..2 over the mechs' step
  (`anim::AnimationState::walkCycle`, `GameWorld::walkCycle`,
  `menu::mechFootValue`; a joined client's from its ghost's system).

(The map's spotted vehicles and the silos' reload and
background icons are above, under the map's vehicles, miniMapInfo and
Spotted.)

### Name tags

The 3D name tags and object icons (friendly names, health bars, control
point icons over the world) are not HUD nodes: RendDX9.dll's
NametagManager (`dice.hfe.geom.NametagManager`, vtable `0x101d6c80`, its
frame `0x100f3490`) keeps them and its NametagRenderer draws them
(`0x1016c1e0` the bars, `0x10168890`.. the icon passes, `Shaders/Nametag`,
the font `Fonts/BF1942.font`); BF2142.exe only looks the manager up
(`0x0043ab00`) and hands it object tags (slot `0x30`, `0x100f40d0`, from
the templates' Nametag component, `0x0063b760`). `src/Main/Nametags`
rewrites them as HUD quads under the HUD. The manager reads the player
manager and the objects, which a client fills from the server: a joined
game's tags take the server's players, control points, requests and the
ghosts' armour (`Nametags::setWorld` with the RemoteHudWorld; the round
answers the sight lines and the seats):

- **Players** (`0x100f0e60`, `0x100f0310`): a tag per other player at its
  soldier's head (0.6 m along its up over its origin, more with distance:
  `+ min(d × 0.6 × 0.05, 3)`) or over its vehicle (`0.35 × height +
  0.45`, nametags.vehicleNametagOffsetFactor / Offset), with "  [n/m]" for
  a vehicle's occupants. Friends: full to 80 m, gone at 120
  (maxFriendlyDistance), out to 500 m while aimed at (faded in over 0.7 s,
  out over 1.5 s); down, they fade over 0.6 s (deathFadeOutTime), or 14 s
  (manDownFadeOutTime) for a local medic. Enemies only while aimed at,
  after a delay of their distance's share of 300 m (the player cull
  distance) and gone past 285 m; never while down. Someone in the local
  player's vehicle has none. Colours by ColorIndex: 1 enemy, 2 team, 3
  squad (squad members stay on screen at the edge of a circle of 0.65,
  glueToEdge, with "[d m]"), 4 a call.
- **Aimed at** (`0x100f0d30`): the crosshair's target, a ray 300 m along
  the view every 0.5 s (`0x100ef5b0`; every occupant of a vehicle it meets,
  `0x100f2ec0`), or, looked at every 0.25 s, the tag's point within the
  0.99999 cone and in sight. The rewrite's ray meets soldiers as 0.6 m
  spheres and vehicles as 2.5 m ones and asks `GameWorld::lineOfSight`.
- **The bar** (`ICArmorBar`: `bar_base` under `bar_filler`, filled from
  texel 1 to 45 of 64, `createBar ICArmorBar 1 45`): a hurt friend's
  health under half for a local medic (the Assault kit), a damaged
  vehicle's armour for an engineer.
- **Object bars** (the same pass, RendDX9 `0x1016c1e0`, tag kind 3): an
  object of the player's team or of none (tag `+0x74` against slot 0xf8)
  whose template sets `Nametag.showArmor` (flag 0x4000000, template
  `+0x33` bit 4) or `Nametag.showSupply` (0x8000000, bit 8) joins it. At
  `0x1016c64f` a repairing kit (the Ability's second byte) or showArmor
  sends it to the armour branch, which draws only for a state (`+0xc8`)
  another path set (none for these, so the sentries' and drones' showArmor
  shows no bar here); a support kit without showSupply takes the ammo
  branch; showSupply shows the SupplyObject child's (class 0x9c47)
  storage, `+0x194` over sharedStorageSize `+0x2bc`, at any level (the
  0.5 test at `0x1016c7a5` doesn't apply), its state 2 / 4 / 3 by
  healSpeed `+0x2a8` / refillAmmoSpeed `+0x2ac` (the bar icons' pass,
  `nametag_barIcons`): the hubs and the MiniMed. The rewrite:
  `nametags::objectTagBar`, `GameWorld::supplyStorage`
  (`Nametags_ObjectSupplyBar`); a joined client has no storage to show.
  The object tag's other way in (`0x1016c52e`): with tag `+0xc4` and flag
  0x800000 (`0x1016c555`) straight to those branches, and with 0x10000000
  as well (`0x1016c59c`) to the object's owner (interface 0x94c1, slot
  0x50: a living player of another team), whose control object's armour
  would fill the bar (state 2 on foot, 1 in a vehicle). Nothing sets
  either flag: the tag's flags are the Nametag component's `+0x34`
  (through the block's `+0x24`, `0x100f3ed0` / `0x100f40d0`), whose
  setters (`0x0063ac70`..`0x0063af70`) and constructor (`0x0063b760`)
  give only the named bits, and RendDX9's other writers of the tag's
  `+0xb8` add other bits. So that path is dead and showArmor draws no bar
  anywhere (settled).
- **Control points** (object tags, `0x100f1330`, `0x100ef960`): the
  templates' `Nametag.*` (showItem, 3dMapIconOffset 0/5/0 on the shipped
  points, showDistance, teamSpecific, maxDistance / maxEnemyDistance 1200
  by default), the icon `Menu/Nametag/<Neutral|Pac|EU>/miniMap_CP` 32 × 32
  with "[d m]" under it, alpha `1 − d / max`.
- The distance shown changes only by more than 0 / 2 / 5 / 9 m below 25 /
  250 / 400 m / beyond (`0x100f0be0`).
- **The object tag's refresh** (`0x100f40d0`, each push of an object's
  runtime Nametag, vtable `0x00989450`, to the manager's slot 0x30). The
  tag info hands a block (slot 0x38, `0x00658590`: the template
  component's `+0x10`..: the offset, type, colour, healthActivationLevel
  `+0x14`, useBoundingRadius `+0x18`, maxDistance / maxEnemyDistance,
  the flags `+0x24`) and its icons (slot 0x44(i), `0x006585a0`:
  3dMapIcon, component `+0x38`, for 0; secondary3dMapIcon, `+0x3c`, the
  component's getter slot 0x38, for 1; each plus the object's own offset
  `+0x10` / `+0x14`, set by slot 0x40). With healthActivationLevel under
  100 the first armour up from the object whose percent is at or below
  it sets flag 0x1000000 and the tag takes icon 1 (the Titans: 49 / 50 to
  53 / 54 at 60 %). With useBoundingRadius (block `+0x18`, the
  component's `+0x28`, getter slot 0x100; 1 from the constructor
  `0x0063b760`) the tag's height (`+0x30`) is raised by the object's
  radius (object slot 0x8c). 35 of the shipped show3dIcon templates set
  it 0; the sentry gun, the missile silos (offset 0/−3/0), the spawn
  beacon, the supply hubs and the MiniMed keep it. Rewritten:
  `nametags::objectTagIcon` / `objectTagPoint` (the icon chosen at each
  drop of the armour, the radius `GameWorld::objectRadius`, the
  collision radius slot 0x90 gives, which is slot 0x8c's for an object
  with a collision mesh and bundled geometry). The blink a change of icon
  starts (`+0x68` = 4, `+0x6c`) isn't.

ColorArray for player and object tags (types 0 and 3) is the table at
`0x102112f8` the NametagManager's constructor fills (`0x100f24c0`):
white, red (0.87, 0.094, 0.094), blue (0.254, 0.552, 0.89), green (74,
227, 37 / 255), yellow (1, 1, 0). The soldier's origin is 1 m over its
feet (the built-in Soldier_CollisionMesh, `0x006e4880`: the feet at −1).
The vehicle's "height" is its root's render object's radius (`0x100c26a0`
the root, `+0x44` slot `0x44`: RendDX9 `0x100c7000`, the shown
geometry's box radius about its centre, as for the order markers;
`Nametags::setMeshLods`) at the LOD the instance shows: RendDX9's pick
for a drawn BundledMesh (`0x100c3390`: the camera's distance over the
view's zoom less LOD 0's radius against the switch distances times the
global scale and the geometry quality) sets `+0x274` and, through slot
`0x6c` (`0x100c3260`), the box `+0x268` (`lodRenderRadius`). The order
markers' height takes LOD 0: it is read as the marker is made, before it
is drawn. Not determined: the bar's
place.

The icons come from `Menu/Nametag/nametags.con`, which the HUD manager's
set-up (`0x0075cfa0`) runs after HudSetupMain.con: `nametags.createIcon
<NametagItemIDs>` (`0x10079004`) picks an id by name (the enum
`0x10070e1a` prints: ICRank 0 with its 44 ranks, ICRevive 0x2c, ICMedic,
ICRepair, ICAmmo, the vehicle ones 0x30-0x33, the bars 0x34-0x36,
ICSquadOrder 0x3d and ICCommanderOrder 0x43 of six frames, ICTarget 0x4e,
ICVeteran 0x4f, ICObject 0x50 of 41 frames, the request orders
0x79-0x80, the Titans 0x81-0x88, the silos 0x8c-0x91, the selection
backgrounds 0x92-0x94, ICObjectCore 0x96, the consoles 0x97-0x9a, the
networkables 0xa0-0xa5); `nametags.setTexture <n> <texture> x y w h`
(`0x100790e4` → the manager `0x100ee9a0`) gives an icon `n` frames along
the texture (`0x1016b790`: frame k is the w × h texels at x + k w, so id
+ k), and a bar (`createBar`, mode +0x4cc 1) its fill (0) and base (1).
`nametags::IconRegistry` keeps them. The objects' 3D icons
(`Nametag.show3dIcon`): the icon 0x50 + `Nametag.3dMapIcon` (so 70 is
ICObjectCore, 71-74 the consoles, 49/50 the two Titans, 60-64 the silos;
lower numbers are the Objects atlas) at the object and its
`3dMapIconOffset`, faded to `maxDistance` (`maxEnemyDistance` for the
enemy's), `showInside` / `showOutside` by the camera inside a Titan,
`teamSpecific` / `inverseTeamSpecific` as the points', in ColorArray by
`useTeamColor`. The Nametag component's flags (component `+0x30`, the
tag's `+0xb8`; the write-back lists them): showItem 1, showIcon 2,
showName 4, showDistance 8, show3dIcon 0x10, glueToEdge 0x20,
teamSpecific 0x200, inverseTeamSpecific 0x400, showIconOnTracker 0x4000,
showInside 0x40000, showOutside 0x80000, selectable 0x100000,
useTeamColor 0x200000, useAliveArmor 0x1000000, showArmor 0x4000000,
showSupply 0x8000000; a player's tag starts
with 7 and `0x100f3de0` adds 0x500201. The rewrite reads them once per
template (`Nametags::TagTemplate`) and looks for tagged objects once a
second.

- **Ranks and veterans** (`0x100f0840`): the tag's `+0x50` is ICRank +
  the stats' rank (player slot `0x1a8` `+0x20`), `+0x54` ICVeteran 0x4f
  when the player's slot `0x3ac` (`+0x402`) says so, which only the
  online profile's "Ent-3" entitlement sets (`0x0045c8a0`, `0x00513e70`):
  never offline. The renderer (`0x1016b100`) copies both into the tag's
  16-pixel text row before the name (each advancing by its width, then 2
  pixels; the row centred), white, or the squad's colour for a squad
  member; not when glued to the edge.
- **The players' icons** (the selectable pass `0x1016a950`, same team,
  selectable, the first occupant of a vehicle `0x100f33c0`): `+0x60`
  (`0x100f0310`) ICObject + 10 for a soldier or vehicle, + 25 for the
  commander, + 25 + the squad for a squad leader (the Objects atlas'
  marker, star and numbered circles), in the tag's colour, at the icon
  point (`0x100efb90(0)`: 0.6 m under a soldier's origin, times 30 / d
  past 30 m; a vehicle's origin). Squad members glued to the edge
  (flags 0x4020) show only the icon there (showIconOnTracker), no text,
  with the location arrow (`0x10168d90`, Menu/Nametag/loactionArrow.dds,
  outwards at 1.05 the edge, alpha 0.5).
- **The radio calls** (`0x100f19c0`, events 0x33-0x37): a call within
  maxCallDistance (150 m) that the local kit can answer (the HUD manager's
  slot `0xac` `+0x74` slot `0x38`: heal, repair, ammunition; here the
  kitType Assault, Engineer, Support) puts ICMedic 0x2d, ICAmmo 0x2f,
  ICRepair 0x2e (12 s, `0x101f6740`) or ICRevive 0x2c (30 s) on the
  caller's tag (`+0x64`, flags 0x26808: glued, "[d m]  name" under 300
  m), crossfaded with the tag's icon and its text towards yellow by (1 -
  min(d / 150, 1) / 2) x the blink 0.5 - 0.5 cos(2 pi t)
  (`0x100f3490`); the local player's own call starts a 12 s timer
  (`0x10211290` / 98 / a0) during which those who can answer show that
  icon (`0x100f0310`). Here the calls come from Radio.callFor* and the
  "medic" / "need_ammo" / "need_repair" messages the local player hears (a
  man-down caller's "medic" is the revive call).
- **The selection** (`0x100f16c0`): the selectable tag nearest the screen
  centre within 0.08 is selected (a sound, 2/0x58); a selected object's
  icon sits on its selected3dMapIcon (0x50 +, ICObjectFlagBackground 0x93
  without one; `0x100f3ed0`) in ColorArray's yellow (ColorIndex3 4).
  Glued objects off screen show only with showIconOnTracker; useAliveArmor
  hides an object's icon once its armour is gone (the Titans' consoles).
- **Inside a Titan**: the object drawer's slot 0x40, as the renderer
  finds it (`LevelSources::cameraInTitanOut`).

- **A vehicle's own icon** (`0x100f0310`: aboard a vehicle, not a squad
  leader or the commander): the "unidentified manager" is the
  NametagManager itself (ECX on entry), its slot 0x74 (`0x100ee590`) on
  the vehicle root template's 0xc4c4 interface: by setVehicleType (slot
  0x34, template +0x3d8, 0x1b by default from the template's constructor
  `0x005cd9e0`; the names `0x004d..`'s VTHeavyTank 0 .. VTInfantry 0x1a)
  heavy and light tanks 0x5f, VTApc / VTNoVehicleType / VTArmoredCar /
  VTTankHunter 0x5d, VTScoutCar 0x5c, the aircraft 0x61, VTAAGun 0x64,
  VTStationaryMG 0x65, ships, the submarine and boats 0x60, VTATGun 0x66,
  VTAA 0x5e, VTHelicopterAttack 0x62, VTHelicopterTransport 0x63; VTLcvp,
  VTSniper, VTInfantry 0x5a; any other by vehicleCategory (slot 0x24:
  VCLand 0x5b, VCSea 0x60, VCAir 0x61, VCHelicopter 0x62), 0x5a when the
  vehicle draws its occupant (usePlayerIcon, the HUD data's +0xb8)
  (`nametags::vehicleIconId`, read once per template).
- **The poses** (`0x100efb90`, the soldier's slot 0x3c: 1 standing, 2
  lying, 3 crouched, as the animation's `0x008b9840` has 2 for prone): the
  text 0.6 / 0.3 / 0.7 m over the origin plus min(d x that x 0.05, 3), 1 m
  for any other (swimming); the icon 0.6 / 1.2 / 1.2 m under it (none for
  the others), times 30 / d past 30 m. The origin stays 1 m over the feet.
- **The fog on enemies** (`0x100f09b0` from `0x100f0e60`): the enemy's
  alpha is capped by fog x the cull range's last third at d / 0.95, the fog
  factor clamp(max(r3, d r1 + r3) - (d r0 + r2)^3, 0, 1) on the fog
  object's FogRange (+0xb8, `0x100355c0`: r0 = 1 / (e - s), r1 = -base /
  (e - s), r2 = -s / (e - s), r3 = e / (e - s)); the CRT pow's exponent
  isn't visible in the decompilation and is taken as calcFog's cube. The
  level's renderer.fogStartEndAndBase feeds it (`Nametags::setFog`; the
  water's under the sea and the view distance's scale aren't).
- **Orders** (TTOrder: the exe's order object `0x005b8b20` → manager slot
  0x2c `0x100f4620`, or 0x28 `0x100f4730` on an object): ICSquadOrder
  0x3d for the squad leader's, ICCommanderOrder 0x43 for the commander's,
  0x39 / 0x3f + the order's map kind (MapMove 4 .. MapRepair 7; a
  comm-rose order is taken as its map kind), at the point 1.5 m up, white,
  "[d m]" under it, glued to the edge (flags 0x4079), faded out to 1200 m
  (DAT_101f67b4); the local player's squad's (commander's and leader's).
- **Requests** (TTRequest: SquadManager `0x004c5720` → slot 0x24
  `0x100f44d0`, only to the local commander): kind 0 the orbital
  bombardment's ICObjectOrbitalBombardmentRequestOrder 0x7a, 1 the orbital
  strike's 0x79, 2 the UAV's 0x7b, 3 the supplies' 0x7c (selected 0x7e /
  0x7d / 0x7f / 0x80), selectable (`nametags::requestIconId`). The squad
  leaders' requests come from SquadLeader.sendRequest (`0x007708d4` →
  `0x007d6d20`) into the squad manager's store (`0x004c5720`), see
  "Squad requests, asset feedback and the commander screen's panel".

The spectator's rules: see "Spectators" (the cameras). The HUD's object marker
nodes (`createObjectMarkerNode`) are the AA and gunship lock-on markers;
see "HUD nodes: transform lists, effects, markers and the map menus".

### Map and spawn screen

`createMapNode` builds the map. Its sizes come from the scripts:
`setMiniPos 245/-291` and `setMiniSize 146/146` for the minimap,
`setMaxiPos -122/-271` and `setMaxiSize 512/512` for the big map, with
positions from the screen's centre. The map texture is the level's
`Hud/Minimap/ingameMap.dds`, covering the primary terrain with north up.

The engine switches the map between two states:

- **Playing:** `MapShow` and `MapMinSize`, the minimap.
- **Dead:** `MapFullSize`, `MapFullSizeAndSpawnShow` and `SpawnShow`, the
  spawn screen. The in-game HUD stays up while dead.

The markers:

- control points, by owner (`Ingame/Flags/Icons/Minimap/<team>/miniMap_CP.tga`);
- on the spawn screen, the spawn icons of the points the team holds with
  spawn points (`Ingame/Minimap/Icons/spawn_(Un)Selected.dds`), and of
  the team's mobile spawn points: the vehicles carrying a SpawnPoint
  (APCs, the AT and IFV spawn vehicles; `GameWorld::spawnVehicles`), at
  the vehicle and moving with it. The original's spawn map (`0x0078e830`)
  walks every spawn group the spawn manager offers the team, a vehicle's
  among them, with the same icons (+0x9f0 unselected, +0xa00 the selected
  group at +0xa48; the squad and inactive variants +0x9f8/+0xa08 and
  index 0), 32 px; clicking a vehicle's picks it
  (`GameWorld::setSpawnVehicle`, spawned into its free seat);
- teammates;
- the player's heading arrow.

While dead, the mouse becomes a pointer, and clicking a spawn icon picks
where the player spawns once the spawn time is up
(`GameWorld::setSpawnChoice`). HUD buttons run their console commands (`setButtonNodeConCmd`: event 0
is the press, 1 the pointer entering, 2 leaving, 3 the release) when
clicked. The commands include `hudManager.setDone`, `hudItems.setBool`,
`scoreboard.setToggleShow` and `spawnManager.setPlayerKit`.

A kit is chosen by the team's kit index (`gameLogic.setKit team index
kit soldier`: Recon, Assault, Anti-Vehicle, Support). The soldier spawns
with its kit's soldier template and the kit's primary weapon: its
`GenericFireArm` child with `itemIndex` 3 (1 is the knife, 2 the sidearm).
Bots take the kits in turn.

The map is BF2142.exe's `Bf2MenuMapNode` (render `0x00795620`). The
node is the minimap's or the big map's rectangle; the map texture is the
node's size times 2.3 to the power of a zoom level (`0x0077b7b0`), divided
by the shown area's share of the map, placed with the player at the
node's centre and pushed back to keep the shown area covering the node,
then cut to it. The level eases (1 - e^(-6 dt) a frame) to its target by
the zoom index (1 at start): minimap 0.5/1.5/2.5 on foot, 0/1/2 in a
vehicle, times 1/2/2.3 inside a Titan; the big map 0. The shown area is
the combat area's bounds in the big map's pixels, 20 pixels wider a side,
made square and kept on the map (`0x0078b490`); without one, the whole
map. Markers keep their pixel size at every zoom (`0x0077c610`: the
rectangle is floored, turned by the marker's yaw, cut to the node). The
exe's own sizes and tints (set where its markers are made): control
points 32 px, soldiers 15 or 16 px, squad leaders 32 px, the commander
16 px (`0x0077d9f0`, `0x0077dbf0`); players are tinted by side from the
table at `0x00b3be30` (no team (1, 1, 1), either team (0.7, 0.7, 0.7)).
Which markers to show and their sizes come from the game
(`HudManager::setMapMarkers`).

The soldier carries every `GenericFireArm` of the kit by slot, and keys
1–9 take the slot's weapon in hand. Each keeps its own magazine; the held
object, the muzzle effect and the weapon's animation system change with
it. Gadgets work through abilities (`ammo.replenishingType`: RTHeal or
RTAmmo, `abilityRadius`, `abilityStrength`, `abilityMaterial`). The medic
and ammo hubs are thrown out as their stationary projectile objects, one
per owner and gadget, and treat the team within their radius. The repair
tool (`onlyActiveWhileFiring`) works round the soldier's hands while the
trigger is held; a gadget without that flag (the hubs) works there while
it is in hand (the ReplenishingAmmoComp's tick, `0x005d8740`). The material table's `damageMod` doubles as the
ability's factor per target: the medic material 73 is 1 on soldiers'
materials and 0 elsewhere, and the repair material 84 has factors on
vehicles' materials.

The component's update (object vtable `0x00970b10` slot 6, `0x005d8ac0`;
template constructor `0x005d7f50`: abilityDrain `0x68` (a tick's at
`0x6c`), abilityStrength `0x70` (a tick's, × 0.033333, at `0x74`),
abilityMaterial `0x7c`, abilityRadius `0x80`, replenishingType `0x84`,
onlyActiveWhileFiring `0x88`) rescans its targets every second while it
has none and every two seconds while it has some (`*0x00a6db70` 1,
`*0x00a6db68` 0.5 a second): a sphere of abilityRadius round the holder
(`0x005d8740`), or with onlyActiveWhileFiring a ray of it along the
holder's forward (`0x005d84a0`); held targets are treated in between even
out of reach. The ray (the repair tool's) starts at the holder's camera
(slot `0x60`) and runs abilityRadius along its forward (slot `0x78`'s third
row) through the object manager's ray (`DAT_00a85220` slot `0x68`, the
holder left out); the first object it meets is the target when it passes
the filter (`0x005d7d40`). A bot whose ray meets nothing takes its AI's
target instead (the AI interface `DAT_00b4bc0c` slot 8). The rewrite casts
from the eyes along the aim (`applyAbility`'s `rayEnd`, `firstHit`); its
bots fall back on the sphere. (Until 2026-11 the rewrite used a 2.5 m
sphere a metre ahead of the hands measured to the vehicles' centres, so a
tank could only be mended from inside its hull.) Only the holder's team or team 0 for RTHeal and RTAmmo,
only enemies for RTTeam (`0x005d7d40`). Each tick each target gets the
tick's strength × the cell (`0x005d7a40`):

- **RTHeal** (gameLogic slot `0x108`: the server's `0x004bc410`, which asks
  `0x004cc380` and then the armour's slot `0x48`, `0x00655a00`): that many
  per cent of its maximum hit points, when it can be repaired, is alive
  and not full. "Can be repaired" is the armour template's
  `armor.canBeRepaired` (`+0x14c`, 1 by default; constructor `0x00630040`,
  setters `0x006304e0` / `0x00630500` through the executors `0x0054b1c9` /
  `0x0054b2ee`) and, for a wreck, `armor.canBeRepairedWhenWreck` (`+0x14d`,
  0 by default); `0x004cc380`'s check (the target filter `0x005d7d40`, the
  seated kit's first pass `0x00599f30`) tests hit points over 0, the
  armour (`0x00655a00`) its wreck flag `+0x15`, and the latter never mends
  a Titan's own armour (`0x00561d90`). Shipped 0: the Titans' cores, core
  doors, shield generators and force fields and the Titan hulls; 1 when
  wrecked: the Titans' gun bundles, the commander's assets and the bridge
  piece. A wreck mended over 0 works again (`0x00654120`). Every heal
  goes this way: tools, hubs, crates and pads, the seated kit
  (`GameWorld::repairable`);
- **RTAmmo** (slot `0x10c` → `0x004cf7b0`): min(100, it) per cent of a
  magazine for each weapon (`0x005f5110`, the fraction kept a second).

The strength is also multiplied by the holder's player's
`ability.increasedRepairAbility` when above 0 (`0x005d7a40`: player slot
`0x2a0` → `+0x30c`, `+0x48`; copied from an unlock's Ability component
by `0x005706b0`, e.g. 1.5 for UnlockEU_AssaultMedic1).

The battery is the soldier's (`+0x338`, read and drawn through component
`0xc4d7` slots `0x90`/`0x98`, `0x0064aad0`/`0x00586310`), 0 to 1, −1
without a kit. A new kit's is empty (kit `+0x1bc`, 0 from `0x00562a80`);
the soldier takes it with the kit (`0x0058b680`) and hands it back when
dropping it (`0x00589890`). Each soldier tick adds the kit's
`abilityRestoreRate` / 30 (kit `+0x31c`, setter `0x0056cd90`), up to 1
(`0x0058d350`). Nothing is treated unless the battery holds a tick's
`abilityDrain` (template `+0x6c` = drain / 30, `0x005d7ae0`), and each
target treated takes that much when it is there (`0x005d81b0`). A hub's
battery is its owner's soldier's: owner seated or dead, none. RTTeam
(slot `0x110`) is used by no ammo in the game's data and is not
rewritten. A thrown hub (`unl_hub_*_stationary`) carries a `SupplyObject`
child (`Unl_Hub_Medic_Supply`: radius 5, healSpeed 4, sharedStorageSize
300; `Unl_Hub_Ammo_Supply`: radius 6, refillAmmoSpeed 8, workOnVehicles,
sharedStorageSize 500; both destroyWhenEmptyStorage) and works as the
supply crates do (see [Commander](#commander)), not by the gadget's
ability.

Projectiles with a detonation component (`DefaultDetonationComp`,
template `0x953b`) explode where they hit. Its constructor (`0x005e9df0`)
sets the defaults: `explosionMaterial` −1, `explosionForce` 150,
`explosionYMod` 1, `explosionRadius` 10 (so C4, which sets none, reaches
10 m), `explosionDamage` 500. The detonation (`0x005e9300`) hands the
blast to the server game logic (vtable `0x009294e8`): slot `0xe8`
(`0x004ba7a0` → `0x005a9090`) for a blast, slot `0xec` (`0x004ba830` →
`0x005a7ab0`) for an EMP (`isEMPWeapon`, `+0x5f`). With material −1 both do
nothing (the car horns' detonations); `endEffectTemplate` plays either way.
Rewritten in `GameWorld::explode`, `blastShare` and `empBlast`;
`GameWorld::detonate` sets one off at a point.

- **Distance:** to the object's position (a soldier's physics origin, a
  metre over its feet; a vehicle's centre), the height difference times
  `explosionYMod`.
- **Falloff** (`0x005a61a0`): 1 within a fifth of the radius
  (`0x00a6aab4`), then linear to 0 at the radius.
- **Soldiers' share** (`0x005a7530`): the head (bone 47) is worth 0.5,
  bone 11 0.35 and bone 3 0.15 (`0x00a01750`), each when a ray from the
  blast reaches it, or one from a point min(0.02 × radius, 0.5) m beside the
  blast (below, left, right, then above; each point used only when the
  blast sees it). A directional charge reaches only soldiers inside
  `explosionConeAngle` (`0x005a6370`). A bone out of sight counts half
  when the object the last blocked ray met (`0x006f2d20`'s out, kept
  across the rays and bones; it or the first parent with armour, `+0x48`)
  is destroyed by what the blasts have dealt it so far: `0x005a8900`
  records each object's damage (after the material cell and `0x005b7290`)
  in a list that `0x005a8d00` applies and swaps each frame (`0x00a6aadc`,
  `0x00a6abcc`, index `0x00a6aacc`), and its hit points (armour slot
  `0x3c`) are at most a recorded amount. The objects are handled before
  the soldiers (`0x005a9090` puts soldiers, `0x9493`, aside), so a blast
  that blows a vehicle away also reaches the soldier behind it (the
  rewrite keeps the one blast's list).
- **Damage** (`0x005a8900`): `explosionDamage` × falloff × share × the cell
  of `explosionMaterial` against the target's material; 0.1 or less is
  dropped.
- **Push** (`0x005a66e0`): `explosionForce` × falloff × share × the target
  armour's `explosionForceMod` (default 1; soldiers 25), at most its
  `explosionForceMax` (default 10; soldiers 1000), for a soldier times
  0.8 + 0.005 × (rand % 100) and with its speed counting against the
  maximum. It points along the soldier's axis nearest the line from the
  blast plus that line made a unit with 5 added upwards (`0x00a6aac0`).
  `0x005ee4d0` keeps it for 0.5 s for the ragdoll, times `rd_expForceMod`.
- **Other objects** (`0x005a9090`): a ray from the blast to the object
  (`DAT_00a85220` slot `0x68`); something else first (or the object
  without armour) halves the blast, and stops it when the object's radius
  (slot `0x90`: its geometry's and its children's) is under a fifth of
  the blast's (`*0x00a6ab24` = 5). The object's radius (`0x006f6b90`):
  its collision mesh instance's (slot `0x74`, `0x006dedb0` on the
  instance's geometry: the first sub-geometry with a LOD, its LOD of the
  lowest collision type, that LOD's radius `+0xc0`; the state `+0x14` is
  not read) plus slot `0x94` (0), or, farther, a child's: its offset's
  length (slot `0xdc`) plus its own radius (a child's instance is the
  geometry its `collisionPart` names). `Body::objectRadius`.
- **The push on objects** (`0x005a66e0`): roots with a node that are not
  major actors (slot `0x1c4`), the blast's own object excepted (its
  armour, `param_6`). Without armour the mod is 10000 / max(mass, 100) and
  the most 500; a wreck uses `wreckExplosionForceMod` / `Max` (`+0x124`,
  `+0x128`, defaults 1 and 100). The rays pass the blast's own object
  (the rewrite's reading of `0x006f2d20`'s object argument: a vehicle's or
  wreck's blast starts inside its hull).
- **The wreck's own blast** (`0x00654120`): its armour at or below
  −wreckHitPoints with `armor.wreckExplosionDamage` (`+0x118`, 0 by
  default) above 0, slot `0xe8` at the object with
  `wreckExplosionRadius` (`+0x114`), `wreckExplosionMaterial` (`+0x11c`),
  `wreckExplosionForce` (`+0x120`), yMod 1, the armour's own object left
  out, the giver (`+0x24`) as attacker, no instigator and no hit object
  (`stepVehicleDamage`; the rewrite has no giver for it).
- **Where a hit round goes off** (`0x005e9300`): off the face along its
  normal by `detonation-collface-offset` (0.07) + `-speedmod` (0.05) ×
  min(|v·n| / `-speedmod-max` (500), 1). Deeper under water than
  `maxDepthForExplosion` (`+0x48`, 2) nothing happens (the node's slot
  `0x144`); `preventDetonationFromDestroyedParent` (`+0x7d`) skips a round
  whose armoured parent is destroyed; `useMMOnEndEffect` (`+0x5e`) plays the
  material pair's effect (game logic slot `0x114`) within 10 ticks of the
  hit; the end effect's up axis is the face's normal with
  `useCollisionNormal` (`+0x69`, 1), else the round's forward. Rewritten:
  the offset (`detonationPoint`), the depth test against the water level
  (`GameWorld::detonateHit`; the rewrite's rounds reach the bottom, so it
  is the bottom's depth) and the end effect's up (`0x005e8f50`); not
  useMMOnEndEffect (the rewrite plays the material pair's effect on every
  hit already) nor preventDetonationFromDestroyedParent. The direction is the object's axis
  nearest the line plus the line (y only when strictly nearest). It wakes
  the node and goes in through slot `0xa4` at (blast − object) /
  max(distance, 1) from the object, itself over max(distance, 1); a
  soldier's node (`0x00993aa0` slot `0xa4` → `0x7c`) takes it as
  acceleration, a tenth of it under water (the node's `+0x5c` over 0, set
  by the ground pass `0x006c28c0`). `game::blastPush`.
- **Read by nothing in BF2142.exe** (the DefaultDetonationComp's
  constructor `0x005e9df0`, its write-back `0x005e97b0`):
  `detonation.detonateOnWaterCollision` (executor `0x004f3fb8`, byte
  `+0x68`, 1 by default; 34 calls in the shipped scripts) and
  `detonation.detectionRadius` (executor `0x004f35b0` through the
  component's slots `0x2c` / `0x30`, float `+0x58`, 1.5 by default; the
  write-back's own default test at `0x005e9b56` is 2; 62 calls). Each is
  read only by the write-back; the float getter `0x006c5fe0` (`+0x58`) is
  shared by many vtables, and none of its callers is the detonation's. So
  a round under water goes off as on land (the depth test above is
  `maxDepthForExplosion`'s); the rewrite reads neither field.
- **The torque pair** (`0x005a66e0`'s `bVar5`): when the projectile has a
  detonation component (`0xc54d`, the object's slot `0x50`; the
  Default/ReplenishDetonationComp at `+0x10`, `0x005e91b0`) whose slot
  `0x4c` (`0x005e89e0`: the template's `+0x44`, `explosionDamage`) is below
  0, the force is 1 × 20 × `explosionForce` × share (no falloff, no mod;
  the tenth in water, the maximum, the soldier's random factor and speed
  as above), along the nearest axis alone (the line is not added,
  `0x0043dbd0` skipped). After the wake, instead of the spread push it
  goes in as three slot `0xa4` calls, unspread: with a the object's x axis
  (matrix row 0) turned to the blast (negated, `0x00562dd0`, when the line
  runs along +x) and f = force / 2.9 (`*0x00a6aa94`) × max(the box's width
  across x, 2) (slot `0x9c` → `0x006f7b10`, the box `0x006f7360` from the
  mesh's slot `0x78`, `0x006deeb0`: every part's and LOD's boxes; its
  `+0x24`, `0x00561d30`; `*0x00a6aa98`): (0, f, 0) at a, (0, −0.5 f, 0) at
  −a (`*0x00a6aa8c`) and a × f × −0.5 at the centre (`*0x00a6aa90`,
  `0x006ac600`'s zero). No shipped detonation has a negative
  `explosionDamage`. `game::blastTwist`.
- The lag-compensated positions (`*0x00a6ab48`, node slot `0x178`):
  on the server (`DAT_00a06884`, set from game logic slot `0x144` by
  `0x006fac60`) a hit is tested against where the target was the
  shooter's latency ago (`0x006b4ee0`): `lagComp` override
  (`*0x00a83e48`, −1: off) when above 0; for a remote client (player slot
  `0x60`) its ping × 0.5 (`*0x00a83e3c`) / 1000 plus 0.05 s
  (`*0x00a83e40`) or, with `*0x00a83e2c` set, its interpolation (slot
  `0x194`, ms); for a local one `0x006b4e70`: an input value (index 8,
  `0x00696db0` → `*0x00a83e4c`) with `*0x00a83e30` set; at most 0.3 s
  (`*0x00a83e44`). It only matters for remote clients' shots; the rewrite
  has no server for remote clients (its local game is the local player and
  bots), so nothing is rewound.

Thrown weapons: projectiles with `physicsType` RotationalPoint or Mesh
(grenades, mines, C4; rounds and missiles are Points) bounce. The
template makes the node and response by physicsType (`0x005f6ba0`,
`0x005f6a60`); RotationalPoint's response (`0x006c0cb0`, vtable
`0x00993018`) finds the deepest ground contact (`0x006c0f90`: the
heightmap's height, normal and material under the node's centre of
collision, or the water) and object contacts (`0x006c1220`) and solves
them (`0x006c0d00`): pushed out by the depth, the velocity's part along
the normal reversed times the mean of the two materials' elasticity
(slot `0x80`), the part along the surface times 1 − their friction (slot
`0x88`, at most 1); nothing on a water material. A frag grenade
(Grenade_hand: friction 0.25, elasticity 0.5) keeps 0.25 of its speed
into grass and 0.475 of its slide. There is no rest speed: only the spin
stops, under |v|² 0.1. The rewrite's projectiles lie still (for the
mines' triggers) under that on a face turned up, and Mesh projectiles,
rigid bodies in the engine (ResponsePhysics), bounce the same way here;
the terrain's material is the level's material map's (see Terrain
materials). They go off when
their time to live runs out (frag grenades: 2.8 s, 140 damage over 9 m),
not on impact.

**Deviation** (the deviation components: `SimpleDeviationComp`, template
`0x005df040`, object `0x005defc0`; the shared base `0x005f5750` also
serves `SoldierDeviationComp`). The template keeps `setFireDev a b c` (the
build-up's maximum `+0x10`, a round's addition `+0x08`, an update's
decay `+0x0c`), `minDev` `+0x14`, `subProjectileDev` `+0x18`. A firing
(`0x005c3cb0`) makes `batchSize` projectiles, the first the main round
and the rest sub-projectiles; for each the component updates once a tick
(`0x005dedb0`: the build-up decays; the deviation is minDev plus it, 0
while zoomed) and applies (`0x005f5540`): with a deviation over 0.01, two
normal(0, 1) numbers from a table of 1024 (filled once by `0x005b28d0`,
Marsaglia's polar method on the engine's shared generator, at the first
component's construction; read at Game slot `0x68` + the round's index)
times the deviation (`subProjectileDev` for a sub, kept; the main round's
adds the last sub's), each × 0.01 × the firearm's velocity (`0x005c1ac0`),
added to the projectile's velocity along its up and right axes. Every
round adds to the build-up, to its maximum. So deviation 1 is 0.57°, one
standard deviation on each axis; 45 is 24°. The rewrite applies it to
the strikes' shells and the sentry drone's rounds with its own generator
(the table's contents depend on the shared generator's state at the time,
which the rewrite can't reproduce). The build-up (`DeviationBuildUp`):
`deviation.setFireDev` is a method of three numbers (template `0x005f5360`:
`+0x10` the most, `+0x8` added a round, `+0xc` the decay a tick), with
`minDev` (`+0x14`) the floor; a round adds (`0x005f5540`), each tick off
the trigger decays toward the floor (`0x005dedb0`).

**Batches** (`fire.batchSize`, the fire template's `+0x48`, 1 by default;
property `0x004e2c5c` / `0x004e2d1a`). FireComp's fire (`0x005f31d0`)
makes that many projectiles (`0x005f2bb0` each, at the same velocity, each
counting toward the tracer interval and taking the next barrel), and the
firing's end (`0x005c3cb0`) strays every one of them through the
deviation component (above): the first is the main round, the rest
sub-projectiles by `subProjectileDev`. The recoil, the fire sound and the
firing's messages go with the main round only, and the magazine loses one
round. The shipped batches: the shotguns' 12 pellets (`*_shotgun`,
`subProjectileDev` 1.4), the EU AV's 4 wire-guided rockets (`eu_av`:
`subProjectileDev` 8, `maxProjectilesInWorld` 8, 125 damage each against
the PAC AV's single 500), the heavy IFV's main gun's 20, and the
commander's orbital strikes (`Commander.cpp`). The rewrite's soldier fire
(`GameWorld::fire`) and seat fire (`fireSeatWeapon`) loop over the batch
(`GameWorld::batchDeviation`); a guided seat round lets the gun's earlier
firings go, not its batch-mates. (Until 2026-11 both fired one round: a
shotgun one pellet, the EU AV a quarter of its damage.)

**Soldier deviation** (hand-held firearms' `SoldierDeviationComp`, class
`0x94e1`; the object's update `0x005de980` each tick with the holder's
input; `game::SoldierDeviation`). The template adds `setTurnDev max pitch
yaw decay` (`0x005de3c0`: `+0x2c`, `+0x20`, `+0x24`, `+0x28`), `setSpeedDev
max throttle strafe decay` (`0x005de3e0`: `+0x3c`, `+0x30`, `+0x34`,
`+0x38`), `setMiscDev max add decay` (`0x005de400`: `+0x48`, `+0x40`,
`+0x44`), `devModStand/Crouch/Lie` (`+0x4c`..`+0x54`) and `devModZoom` /
`minDevModZoom` (`+0x58`, `+0x5c`), all modifiers 1 by default. The
input's bits pick the parts: PIYaw (strafe, bit 0) and PIThrottle (bit
3) the speed's (a fixed step each while above 0.01, held at its max,
decaying without), PIMouseLookX / Y (bits 4, 5) the turn's (their size
times the factors less the decay); the misc part grows while its flag
holds (the rewrite: in the air; eu_ar_rifle's `7 7 0.14` puts a jump at
the maximum). The deviation = (minDev × minDevModZoom + misc + turn +
speed + the firing's build-up) × devModZoom × the stance's (zoom
modifiers 1 when not zoomed). Rounds stray by it as above, and the
crosshair (`0x007be770`) spreads by it. Its `+0x44` extra is a bot's AI
deviation (below, Bots: Deviation), added while the holder is an AI
(its slot `0x1a0` → `0x6c(0)` → `0x68`). Unlike the simple component's,
the soldier component's build-up stops at 0 on the side it builds from
when it decays off the trigger (`0x005de980`: below 0 for a positive
round's addition, above 0 for a negative one): the machine guns'
`setFireDev -1 -0.09 -0.009` steadies them as they fire (to −1) and comes
back up to 0, no further (`DeviationBuildUp::updateSoldier`; the rewrite
used to let it climb by 0.009 a tick for ever, tens of degrees after a
minute's rest).

**Muzzle speed** (`ObjectTemplate.velocity`, the firearm template's
`+0x2f0`, property `0x004e115f`): 600 m/s unless set (the GenericFireArm
template's constructor `0x005c2800`). The SMGs (as_smg, eu_smg), the
handguns, as_at_r_gun_barrel and the recon drone's gun set none
(`FireArmSettings::velocity`; it used to default to 0, the rounds
dropping at the shooter's feet).

**Gun sway** (`DefaultGunSwayComp`, class `0x94f6`, object `0x005e0640`,
update `0x005e0da0`; `game::GunSway`): it moves the aim by nudging the
holder's look inputs, PIMouseLookY on the pitch (`0x005e09a0`) and
PIMouseLookX left-right (`0x005e0ba0`). With `gunSwayUseZoom` only while
zoomed. Each axis, every `UpdateRate` seconds, takes a step of `Max /
Steps` less its smoothing: `Factor × ZoomModifier × step × dt × the
stability × ±1` goes on the input when the player's own is smaller; the
swing turns at `Max` + an extra (`RandomMin..RandomMax`, drawn at the
ends), and with `DirModifier` / `DirThreshold`'s draw keeps on to
2 × (Max + extra) before starting over (the left-right pass writes the
pitch's keep-on flag, as `0x005e0ba0` does). The smoothing (`0x005dfc20`:
`SmoothFactor`, `SmoothMax`, `SmoothThreshold`) slows the steps near the
ends. Holding the sprint key (PISprint) while zoomed with the scope
stabilizer (an unlock's `ability.hasScopeStabilizerAbility`) steadies it
(`0x005e0750`): the stability falls to 0 over `stabilityTime` and back
over `stabilityRecoverTime`, held at most `stabilityDuration`
(`stabilityDurationRecoverTime` to recover).

**Dog tags.** `dogTagRewardTemplate` / `dogTagExchangeTemplate` (Kit
`+0x34c` / `+0x368`) are read by nothing. The kit build (`0x00570ab0`)
applies a kit's `isDogtagReplacement` containers (`+0x2e2`: the knife
unlock and its `replaceItem knife`) for a player whose totalDogtagCount
(player `+0x104`, slots `0x398` / `0x39c`, `pmgr_p_set`; carried to
clients in the kit-selection event `0x0050beb0`) is 50 or more
(`*0x00a67b68`), unlocked or not (`GameWorld::setDogtagCount`, `fillKit`).
A knife kill's reward is the ranked stats scripts' (not shipped):
`host.sgl_sendGameLogicEvent(player, 19, victim)` posts
ECGameLogicGLDogTag, which a client (`0x004cbea0`) shows as HUD event
0x28 (the "dogtag" sound and `HUD_DOG_TAG_MESSAGE` for 5 s, `0x0074f0d0`)
and counts per victim; not rewritten.

**Kit abilities in a vehicle** (the player's update `0x00599f30`, each
tick from `0x0059bd80` while the soldier sits in a vehicle). The kit's
own Ability component (`ability.hasHealingAbility` on the assault kits,
`hasRepairingAbility` on the anti-vehicle kits, `hasAmmoAbility` on the
support kits; the kit object's `+0x74`, slot `0x38`'s three bytes) works
round the vehicle: the object manager's sphere (`DAT_00a85220` slot
`0x44`) of `abilityInVehicleRadius` (Kit `+0x328`: 7, 8 for the
engineers), at `abilityInVehicleStrength` (`+0x324`: 0.35, 0.075, 0.4)
per cent a tick of material `abilityInVehicleMaterial` (`+0x320`: 73,
84, 91). Healing treats the team's soldiers, the seated ones too (game
logic slot `0x108`); repairing (with neither of the others) the vehicles
of the team or of none, the engineer's own among them (slot `0x108`);
ammo refills the team's soldiers (slot `0x10c`). `GameWorld::
stepVehicleAbility` through `applyAbility` without the battery. Left: the
first sphere's pass over the nearby vehicles and, when the player's
slot `0x2a0` object has `+0x48` above 0, its message (`0x005910c0` with
`0x400` and the material). `abilityInVehicleStrengthModifier` (executor
`0x004ff6df` → the template's interface at `+0x298`, slot 0x164
`0x0059dbc0`: template `+0x4b0`, 1 by default; getter slot 0x168
`0x0059dbd0`; saved by `0x005caff0`) has no reader: nothing reads
`+0x4b0` and no call of slot 0x168 goes through that interface. Nothing to
rewrite.

**Unlock abilities.** `ability.setMaterialDamageMod <material> <mod>`
(`0x0054eadc` → the Ability's slot `0x94`) scales the damage a projectile
of that material does to the soldier (the assault's armour unlock: 0.75
for twenty bullet materials); `ability.addExtraAmmoItem <item> <mags>
<rounds> <flag>` (`0x0054ebed`) adds magazines and rounds to an item of
the kit (`as_handgun 3 0 0`, `unl_grenade_frag 0 1 1`; the list's
consumer and the flag aren't traced, the rewrite adds to nrOfMags and
magSize). The Ability template (class `0xc4b2`, vtable `0x00981e68`)
keeps `sprintRechargeModifier` at `+0x5c` (slot `0xb4`),
`sprintUseModifier` `+0x60` (`0xc4`), `beaconSpawnTimeMod` `+0x64`
(`0xbc`) and `setOverheatMod <weapon> <mod>`'s pairs (`0x0054e8b0` →
slot `0x8c`, `0x00631740`, the list `+0x34`). Applying an unlock
(`0x005706b0`) copies each modifier that isn't 1 into the player's ability
block (player slot `0x2a0`, `+0x30c`: `+0x4c` recharge, `+0x50` use,
`+0x54` beacon) and appends the pairs. The soldier's stamina
(`0x0058b680` → `0x00645790`) takes the use modifier as its drain factor
and the recharge one as its recovery factor; a player's respawn wait
(`0x004bb220`: slot `0x108` × sv.spawnTime × 30 ticks) is its squad
leader's beacon modifier when its chosen spawn is the squad's beacon
(`0x005913c0`), else 1; the batch fire (`0x005c3cb0`) adds the last
matching pair's modifier × `heatAddWhenFire` per round (the
active camouflage's 0.72). The kit's `sprintStaminaDissipationFactor`
(`+0x304`, `0x004f879a`) is read by nothing. `GameWorld::fillKit`,
`withExtraAmmo`.

**Blast shake** (`0x005a6e70`, `GameWorld::cameraShake`). Its callers:
the server's game logic slot `0xe8` (`0x004ba7a0` → `0x005a9090`, only
for a material other than −1), the client's (`0x004cc4c0`), a gun's round
with recoilForce above 5 (`0x005ddfc0`) and an EffectBundle starting with
`cameraShake` (`0x0061a1c0`: radius `cameraShakeRadius` `+0x460`, damage
and force both `cameraShakeForce` `+0x464`; the heavy mechs' footsteps,
10 and 90). An EMP (`0x005a7ab0`) doesn't call it. The detonation's
arguments (`0x005e9300`, read off its pushes): the position, radius
(slot `0x3c`), material (edx, slot `0x38`), damage (slot `0x4c`), force
(slot `0x48`), the projectile's `+0x184` slot `0x30` (the handle at
`+0x1c0`; the rewrite reads it as the shooter), the projectile and the
object it hit. It first raises the ambient triggers' event 8; then the
players in the hit object's PlayerControlObject (interface `0xc4c5`, its
slot `0x64` list, those with slot `0x60`) get min(force / 20, 1) ×
min(damage / 150, 1) × 4 through player slot `0x21c` (`0x00592010`:
`+0x1d8`, the player networkable's hit strength, two records `+0x1dc`;
`GameWorld::takeSentShake`). The local player (PlayerManager slot `0x30`,
not a commander on its screen: slots `0x128` / `0xcc`) with a control
object: amount = min(damage / 150, 1) (`*0x00a6ab74` 150) × min(force /
20, 1) (`*0x00a6abc8` 20) × 4 (`*0x00a6ab4c`) × (1, or 0.1 without the
instigator, `*0x00a6ab84`) × (1 on foot or for the own object, else 0.2,
`*0x00a6ab00`) × (1 on or inside the own object, else max(0, 1 − d /
(3 × radius))); "own" is the hit object's root being the control object or
the blast inside a vehicle's box (`0x005a60a0`, inclusive). Above 0 it
goes to the camera's hit shake. And with a material other than −1, a
soldier on foot (class `0x9493`) within 0.6 × the radius (`*0x00a6ab7c`)
gets the game logic's event 0xd (`DAT_00a7d06c` slot `0x10`, the local
player from `DAT_00b43878` slot `0x78`): the tinnitus.

**Lock-on weapons** (the target components: `MultiFireArmTargetComp` on
the AA and AT launchers, the walkers' and gunships' guided guns; template
`0xc50c`: `target.targetSystem` `+0x80`, `maxDistance` `+0x78`,
`lockAngle` `+0x88` (45 by default), `lockDelay` `+0x8c` (round(× 30)
ticks at `+0x90`), `loseLockDelay` `+0x94` (0.2, ticks `+0x98`)). The
default component (runtime `0x005e1a70`, interface vtable `0x009733a8`)
updates in slot 6 (`0x005e1b30`) for TSHeatSeeking and TSLaserGuided
while the weapon is one of its holder's three in use: the candidate
(game logic slot `0x1c8`, `0x004cf290`) is the nearest registered target
object of the round's `seek.targetType` (not the system's), alive, not
under the shooter's root and not in a root occupied by his team (an empty
vehicle of either side counts), within min(maxDistance, the round's
`seek.maxDistLock`) and lockAngle of the direction (the camera's with
`target.useCameraDirectionToTarget` `+0x7d`, else the weapon's), in
sight; with the candidate the target, a loss in progress ends; unlocked,
the target becomes the candidate at once and its clock restarts; locked
and another (or none), after more than loseLockDelay ticks the candidate
replaces it unlocked; locked once the tick passes the target's start +
lockDelay ticks. The shot (`0x005e1ee0`) gives the round the target only
when locked. The heat and laser rounds (SeekClosestTargetComp, template
`0x9540`, ctor `0x005ec300`: maxAngleLock 45°, maxDistLock 9999,
distLoseLock 0, `seek.reLockTime` `+0x28` / ticks `+0x2c`) home from
`seek.trackingDelay` on (`0x005ec260`): a destroyed target dropped, the
nearest candidate from the round along its heading (none: with
distLoseLock, asked again out to it and the target kept only if found);
with reLockTime 0, nothing found, the relock flag clear or the target
alive it takes the candidate at once, else only once the same one has
lasted more than reLockTime ticks, clearing the flag the shot set
(`0x005b2e70`, `0x005ebea0`); DefaultFollowComp turns it
(`GameWorld::steerClosest`; 9999 on the AA missiles and static_aa: an
unlocked shot never acquires). Wire guidance (LPTargetComp, the 11
TSWireGuided weapons, ctor `0x005e2100`; `0x005e2e20` → `0x005e27a0`
every tick): the steering point is o + f × (max(0, (m − o)·f) +
`target.wireGuidedLookAheadDistance` (`+0xb4`, 20)) from the shooter's
camera o and forward f, m the missile; guidance goes beyond
`target.maxDistance` or with the line o–m cut, unless
`dontLooseGuidanceOnObstruction` (`+0xb8`); `disableGuidanceOnReload`
(`+0xb1`, as_av / eu_av) lets the missile go unguided at the reload's
start (`0x005c0f40` → slot `0x48`, `0x005e23b0`). The component guides
one round, its last (`+0x1c`, slot `0xbc`, which `0x005e2e20` steers): a
new round of the gun takes the guidance over and an earlier one flies on
unguided (`GameWorld::stepGunner`). With a projectile camera the camera
is the round's own (see **The projectile camera**). `targetObjectTemplate`
(`+0x88`, the object the guidance moves): the rewrite keeps the point. The
HUD's object markers (`Bf2ObjectMarkerNode`) show the state.

- **Mines:** a mine fires when someone faster than
  `triggerVictimMinSpeed` (3.6 m/s: walking past is safe) comes within its
  `triggerRadius`, inside `triggerAngle` of its facing (the radius
  trigger's test `0x005e8aa0`). Its blast reaches only
  `explosionConeAngle` of that facing. Who sets it off is its
  `detonation.triggerType` (`+0x64`, RadiusTriggerType): MTYNone (the
  default) nobody, MTYPersonnel soldiers, MTYVehicle anything but soldiers
  (the EMP and motion mines; a vehicle within the radius of its bounds),
  MTYPco both (the anti-personnel mine). Its owner's side is spared when
  the one crossing it is a bot (player slot `0x68`, `+0xd4`), or when the
  server's `sv.friendlyFireWithMines` (settings `+0x288`, copied to
  `DAT_00a3fcc0 +0x58` by `0x00430e20`; on by default) is off and the mine
  has `detonation.allowFriendlyFireDetonation` (`+0x7c`; the three mines
  have it); a human teammate sets it off otherwise. A vehicle's player is
  its driver; a mine whose owner has gone spares nobody. The trigger runs
  every `weapon-detonationTriggerFreq` (0.25 s, `0x008e7260`) of the
  detonation component's update (`0x005e9f60`), in flight too: everyone
  with a control object within `triggerRadius` (a sphere query) is
  tested, and the test's shape (`game::radiusTriggerShape`) depends on
  `triggerAngle` (`+0x78`, 0 by default):
  - 0 or less (the EMP and motion mines): soldiers pass as they are; any
    other object passes when the point `min(distance, triggerRadius)`
    from the mine towards its origin lies in its box (slot `0x9c`, in
    its frame, `0x005a60a0`). An object touching nothing (its physics
    node's `+0x249`: set at each step, cleared by a contact, slot
    `0x1b8`) only counts with `detonation.radiusDetonateWithAirVehicles`
    (`+0x5c`), which the three shipped vehicle mines all set. The
    rewrite counts its wheels' ground contact as contacts.
  - above 0 (the anti-personnel mine's 30, the static AA flak's 360): in
    the mine's frame the object's origin must be ahead and within tan(angle)
    × z of the axis across and up, less half its box's width and height:
    a pyramid. At 360 that leaves a line ahead as wide as the box, the
    flak's proximity fuse along its flight.
  - then nothing in the way to the origin (`0x006f2530`; a soldier tried
    again to his body, bone 2), and a speed (the whole velocity) of at
    least `triggerVictimMinSpeed`.
  A soldier's box is his collision mesh's LOD 1 (slot `0x54(1)`): every
  soldier names the built-in Soldier_CollisionMesh, which `0x006e4880`
  builds without a file (LOD 1 a copy of LOD 0, `0x006e1ea0`: x and z
  ±0.4 m, y −1..0.8 m about the physics origin), so 0.8 m wide and 1.8 m
  high. The mine's frame is its matrix (slot `0x7c`): once stuck (the
  anti-personnel mine sticks to faces within 45°), up along the face's
  normal with its x axis kept (`0x005e83d0`, `game::stuckFrame`); lying,
  its facing; in flight, its heading.
- **C4:** it has neither a trigger nor a fuse to speak of (9999 s), so its
  owner sets it off with alternate fire (the right mouse button). It has
  no radius of its own: the detonation's default, 10 m.

Vehicles take damage through their armour settings:

- **EMP:** an EMP blast (`detonation.isEMPWeapon`: the EMP grenade, mine
  and launchers, the commander's EMP strike) hurts nobody (`0x005a7ab0`).
  Every armoured object within the radius takes EMP damage `explosionDamage`
  × (1 − distance / radius) (`0x005a6500`; with `armor.empDamageIgnoreRadius`
  × `empDamageIgnoreRadiusModifier`, default 0.1; 0.1 or less is dropped).
  The armour (vtable `0x00988cb8`, slot `0x148` = `0x00652980`) adds it in
  steps: level = min(`empDamageNumStep`, ceil(level + damage /
  `empDamageStepSize`)), and the level falls by one every `empLevelTime`
  seconds (`0x00652910`; defaults at the armor template's `0x180`-`0x188`:
  5 s, 120, 3 steps); slot `0x14c` (`0x00652a00`) gives it rounded up. The
  EMP grenade's default 500 at its centre fills every step. The
  PlayerControlObject's input filter (`0x005ca2e0`) scales the driver's
  throttle, yaw, pitch and roll by 1 − level / `empDamageNumStep` (0, 1/3
  and 2/3 at levels 3, 2 and 1 with 3 steps), mouse look left alone; a
  seat whose own armour is a child's (not the root's) scales mouse look
  too. With `autoControllerTemplateName` (template `+0x298` slot `0x110`)
  it cuts every input above level 1. With `scaleInputOnCriticalDamage`,
  below the armour's `criticalDamage` the inputs are scaled by
  `criticalDamageScaleModifier`. The level falls continuously, at
  1 / `empLevelTime` a second. Firearm components never read the EMP
  level: the filter (`0x005ca2e0`) scales the driver's inputs only, and a
  gunner's fire (PIFire, input 8) and look are touched only on a seat
  with its own child armour. So gunners keep firing; an auto-controlled
  object (the sentry drone) neither turns nor fires above level 1. Only
  ActiveDefense ammo (`0x005d9560`) and camouflage (`0x005d9030`,
  `0x005d8ec0`) drain faster, × (level + 1).
- **Active defence (ADS):** `ads_land` (ammo.protectionRadius
  6: the APCs, tanks, heavy mechs) and `ads_air` (10: the gunships, the AT
  walkers), GenericFireArms on PIFlareFire at 12 rounds a minute, one
  round, a 12 s reload without a player, ActiveDefenseAmmoComp with
  ammo.detonateMaterial 2142 (template `+0x68`, executor `0x004e7720`)
  and protectionRadius (`+0x6c`, `0x004e75e5`). While the weapon's fire
  state is 4 (`0x005c14d0`: one round's interval, 5 s) the component's
  update (`0x005d97f0`) sets the shield {material, min(protectionRadius,
  the root's slot 0x90 − 0.1)} on the vehicle's root (slot 0x118; cleared
  with 0 otherwise; "ads-draw-sphere" draws it). A projectile whose
  template has activeDefenseEnabled (`+0x336`; 25 shipped: the AA, AV and
  TV-guided missiles and some guns' rounds) meeting an object with a
  shield (slot 0x11c) that isn't its firer's root (`0x006c07a0`) is tested
  as a segment from its last position against the sphere about the root
  (`0x006bf220`: entering from outside, the entry point and inward
  normal); on entry it is flagged (`+0x268`) and the contact recorded as
  its collision at that point with material 2142 (`0x006c0430`), so it
  detonates on the shield and never reaches the hull. The ammo's
  can-fire test (`0x005d9560`) defers to the vehicle's slot 0x14c; EMP
  drains it × (level + 1). Rewritten: the PIFlareFire group's weapon
  (a seat's weapons, under Seats) fires on PIFlareFire (X), not while the
  EMP level is up; its round raises `Body::shieldRadius` for one round's
  interval (`GameWorld::raiseShield`; the root's radius is its collision
  points' farthest); a projectile with activeDefenseEnabled entering the
  sphere from outside is hit there with the shield's material (2142:
  damageMod 0, e_ActiveDef, the force-field sounds), goes off there and
  doesn't penetrate (`stepProjectiles`). The bots never fire it (the ads
  have no aiTemplate).
- **Critical damage:** below `armor.criticalDamage` a vehicle burns down at
  `hpLostWhileCriticalDamage` a second (FAV: 18 below 151, out in 5.6 s from
  100).
- **Water and rolling:** in water deeper than `armor.waterLevel` over its
  centre for longer than `waterDamageDelay`, a vehicle loses
  `hpLostWhileInWater` a second (`hpLostWhileInDeepWater` past
  `deepWaterLevel`). Upside down, it loses `hpLostWhileUpSideDown`.
- **Destruction:** a destroyed vehicle explodes with `armor.explosion*`
  (FAV: 300 over 6 m), kills everyone aboard, and stays as a wreck for
  `timeToStayAsWreck`. Its spawner then puts out a new one.
- **Abandoned vehicles:** the spawn (`0x005aeb80`) hands a spawned
  PlayerControlObject root (interface `0xc4c5`) its spawner (slot `0xc0`,
  `+0x264`), the spawner's `timeToLive` (slot `0xa4`: `+0x25c` and the
  countdown `+0x258`; 60 by default, 30 to 999 in the levels) and the time
  (slot `0xb8`). On the server a check (`0x005c8ba0`, event `0x1d`) runs
  half a second on and then: in use (a seat taken) again in 5 s; within
  the spawner's `distance` of it, again in 5 s with the countdown full; a
  living soldier on foot within 3 × its `armor.explosionRadius`, again in
  5 s; otherwise every half second the countdown loses 0.5 and, once out,
  the vehicle 0.5 × the spawner's `+0x2f0` (50, which nothing sets) hit
  points (0.5 without the spawner) through the game logic's damage,
  until it is destroyed. `GameWorld::stepAbandoned`.
- **holdObject** (`0x005af230`'s end; operation_clean_sweep and the_hell):
  the spawner holds its last spawn at the spot (its matrix and
  `spawnOffset`; the node's motion stopped, slot `0x148`) until its first
  Engine (`0x005ad420`) turns at 0.1 or more (`+0x25c`); without an Engine
  or wrecked it lets go at once; letting go puts the node to sleep.
- **The spawn spot's test** (`0x005aeb80`'s first half): the template's
  collision mesh (`0x005ad4d0`: the collision manager's, slot `0x28`, by
  the template's slot `0x90` name) at the spawner's matrix moved by
  `spawnOffset` (unturned) is tested against the PlayerControlObjects
  (interface `0xc4c5`) the scene finds within 10 m (`DAT_00a85220` slot
  `0x44`) of the spot, less those a global list holds (`0x005628f0` /
  `0x00561d90`: the Titan sync manager, `ECPhysicsETitanSync`,
  `0x00561c00`, with the two teams' Titans at `+8` / `+0xc`, in `gpm_ti`
  alone; `GameWorld::testSpawnSpot` skips them, see [Titans](#titans-gpm_ti)). The spot is first dropped
  (`0x005ad8b0`): along the spawner's up axis from the template's
  vehicle-LOD box top (slot `0x54(1)`: max y) to its bottom (min y), the
  scene's ray (slot `0x68`, `0x00700b80`) through objects whose flags
  (`+0x14`) have `0x1000100` and not 8 (`0x006f4aa0`; 8 marks the mobile
  ones, set with their node by `0x005f6ba0` / `0x00621b50`): a hit on a
  static object puts the box's bottom on it; else a bottom under the
  terrain (`DAT_00a83e58` slot `0x6c`) comes up onto it. Only the test
  moves: the spawn is at the spawner's spot. One overlaps (`0x006f2e90`) when it isn't being deleted, its
  response is a mesh one (`0xc42d`, `0xc430`, `0xc431`) and
  `0x006f2760` finds, for any vertex of the template's vehicle LOD (type
  1; slots `0x28`, `0x3c`, `0x40`) turned by the matrix, the segment from
  the spot to it crossing the object's soldier LOD (its slot `0xc4(2)`;
  the mesh instance's slot 22, `0x006e5920` → `0x006de850`, both sides of
  the faces). A template with MechLegs (`0x9482`) also probes three
  segments down (world y) by its object's box bottom (the
  PlayerControlObject template's `+0x4c4`, set by `0x005cd4f0` when one is
  made: slot `0x98(0)`'s min y, `0x006f7050`: its mesh instance's box and
  its children's at their offsets) from the spot and 1.7 m either side
  along the spawner's x axis (`0x006f28e0`: the mesh instance's slot 22,
  soldier LOD), when that is not 0. An existing walker is also tested
  through its legs' objects (`0x006f2e90`'s loop over the responses, slot
  `0x5c`), which the rewrite doesn't have as bodies: its hull alone. An overlapping object in use (the interface's slot `0x18`,
  `0x005c87b0`: `+0x14`) stops the spawn; otherwise the overlapping ones
  are counted as a try (`+0x204`) up to five, and on the sixth they are
  removed (the object manager's slot `0xa4`) unless a soldier (`0xc4d7`) is
  within 7 m of the spawner. Every one of these returns −1: the update
  tries again in a second (`0x005af230`). A spawn clears the count.
  `GameWorld::testSpawnSpot`, `dropSpawnSpot`, `ObjectSpawner::SpotTest`
  (the drop's ray asks the static objects' projectile LOD).

Deployables: a gadget whose projectile has mesh physics and armour, and
neither explodes nor holds a beacon (`portable_shield`: 600 hit points),
is set down a metre ahead, one per owner and gadget. Its mesh then blocks
rounds like any body's, and shot to pieces it is gone.

**`fire.maxProjectilesInWorld`** (the fire template's `+0x74`, 0 by
default in the base constructor `0x005f2ad0`, executor `0x004e33d8`). The
runtime fire component (`0x005f28a0`; template `+0x98`, firearm `+0x0c`)
keeps a list of weak handles to the rounds it made (`+0x14`..`+0x1c`). Its
projectile creation (`0x005f2bb0`), unless the round is a client's own
predicted one (`0x005f1440`), with a limit above 0 drops the list's dead
entries, then deletes the oldest (the game's slot `0xa4` → `0x004a5f90` →
the object manager's delete `0x006fdd90`: no detonation) while the count
is at the limit, and adds the new round: the firearm never refuses to
fire. The list belongs to the firearm instance: a new kit's firearms start
empty, and the old ones' rounds go keepProjectiles seconds after their
firearm (`0x005f1cc0`). Shipped: Unl_c4, Unl_Mine_EMP, Unl_Mine_Motion,
Beacon 5; Unl_Mine_AntiPersonnel, unl_sonar 2; Unl_Deployer_Sentrygun,
Bp1_Decoy, Bp1_sonar, the drone detonators, Unl_Hub_Ammo, Unl_Hub_Medic,
Unl_Port_Shield 1; eu_aa, eu_av 8. `fire.destroyProjectilesOnDestroy`
(`+0x80`) has no reader besides its setter `0x004e34f2` (the template's
13 slots don't read it) and no template sets it. Rewritten:
`GameWorld::limitInWorld` (the hubs, the shield, the drones and the beacon
keep their own one-per-owner paths).

**Weapon and armour flags, from their readers.**
- `fire.fireStartDelay` (the fire template's RandomDistribution at `+0x08`,
  its value `+0x0c`): SingleFireComp / SpawnObjectFireComp's fire slot 36
  (`0x005d4d80`) and ExplosivesFireComp's (`0x005e6bc0`), on a fresh press
  (`+0x6c`) at a burst's first round with a value other than 0, start the
  wait (`+0x60`; `0x005f1650`: round(30 × max(0, sample)) ticks, its seed
  the owner's `+0x214` or the time + 0xcfb) and fire nothing; the update
  (`0x005f18b0`) lets the round go once past; a release (`0x005f1630`)
  drops it. MultiFireComp's slot 36 (`0x005d6e10`) never starts it.
  EU_AAcannon_Firearm_Barrel 0.6, the AT miniguns 0.5, US_AG_Cannon_fireArm
  0.227 (the heavy mech's minigun's 0.5 is a MultiFireComp's). `FireArm::fire`.
- `fire.maximumVehicleTiltForFire` (`+0x7c`): every fire component's press
  (base `0x005f1370` through slot 74, Multi `0x005d5d50`, LP `0x005e3d20`,
  Thrown `0x005e4d80`) asks `0x005f1780`: 0 passes, else acos(the root
  object's up.y) in degrees must be under it; a double-click launcher's
  second click isn't tested. The pod launchers 30, the air transports'
  70. `tiltAllowsFire`, `GameWorld::launchPod`.
- `target.disableFireWhenActiveMissile` (LPTargetComp `+0xb0`, constructor
  `0x005e2100`): its press slot 13 (`0x005e2430`) refuses while the guided
  round (`+0x54`) lives; a reload with disableGuidanceOnReload (`+0xb1`,
  `0x005e23b0`) lets it go. as_ag_GuidedMissileWeapon,
  us_ag_TAD_GuidedMissile_firearm, as_hov_light_Gunner_missile_launcher.
  `GameWorld::activeMissile`.
- `fire.useDistanceCounter` / `distanceStep` / `minimumDistance`
  (SingleFireComp `+0xa8` / `+0xac` / `+0xb0`, constructor `0x005d5790`;
  the rifles' rocket launchers, 2 and 20): the input handler `0x005d5440`
  with a zoom component turns the range mode (`+0x178`) on when zoomed in,
  the distance (`+0x17c`) the view ray's rounded (`0x005d4f70`, 999 m at
  most), and off zoomed out; PIPrevItem / PINextItem step it by
  distanceStep, never under minimumDistance (without a zoom component
  PIAltFire toggles the mode: none ships). On fire (`0x005d4d80`) a
  GenericProjectile gets the distance (`+0x26c`, flag `0x800`) when on and
  at least 1; its update's end (`0x005b3e60`) sets it off that far from
  its start. `GameWorld::stepBurstRange`, `stepBurstDistance` (the
  mouse wheel's c_PINextItem / c_PIPrevItem, `SoldierInput::itemStep`, a
  step a tick on the server's input as on ours), `stepProjectiles`.
- `collision.bouncing` (the collision template's `+0xd`): the projectile's
  slot 51 (`0x005b5390`, after a hit that doesn't go through, from
  `0x005a39d0`) gives the ricochet component the first say, then keeps a
  bouncing round, else sets it off (event `0x1f`, `0x005b62a0`). The EMP
  grenade (unset) and the smoke grenade (0) go off where they land.
  `ProjectileSettings::bounces` (it was the physics type).
  `collision.hasCollisionEffect`
  (`+0xc`) has getters (`0x005e7840`, `0x005b3000`) and no caller found;
  `fire.projectileStartRotation` (ThrownFireComp `+0xb4`..`+0xbc`) only
  turns the thrown object's matrix (`0x005e5720`), not its velocity (see
  **The rounds' own look**: `throwFrame`).
- **Sticky projectiles** (StickyCollisionComp, component `0xc54b`; its
  template's constructor `0x005e8820`; 11 shipped: C4, both sonars, the
  decoy, the AP and EMP mines, the explosive shotgun round, both hubs, the
  shield and the beacon). `collision.maxStickAngle` (`+0x10`, executor
  `0x004f27f1`) is kept as the cosine of the angle clamped to ±180
  (`0x005e8030`; default −1, any face); `stickToTerrain` `+0x14`,
  `stickToStaticObjects` `+0x15`, `stickToVehicles` `+0x16` are 1 by
  default (0 shipped on the mines, decoy, hubs, shield and beacon). The
  response (`0x005e83d0`), on a contact the ordinary collision handler
  (game logic slot `0xf8`) took: an object answering PlayerControlObject's
  interface (`0xc4c5`) whose template isn't exactly a PCO (`0xc4c2`: so a
  soldier, a parachute, a drone) is bounced off; once stuck (`+0x14`) it
  answers nothing; a normal whose y is under the cosine bounces. Otherwise
  it is placed at the contact, its up turned to the normal, and on an
  object whose root isn't a control point (`0x94a5`) its matrix kept
  relative to the hit part's RotationalBundle (`0x006f2d70(.., 0x947d)`,
  the handle at `+0x10`, the relative matrix at `+0x18`). Then: the
  surface's material (manager slot `0x30`) unknown or with water physics
  (material slot `0x68`, `+0x2d`) bounces; stickToTerrain on the terrain
  (`0x00561d90` with the terrain singleton `0x005628f0`) sticks; without
  stickToVehicles a root answering `0xc4c5` bounces; without
  stickToTerrain on no object, or without stickToStaticObjects on one,
  bounces; else it sticks (`+0x14` = 1). Placed (`0x005e81a0`), the server
  sends everyone the StickyProjectile event (0x20: built `0x0050f850`,
  written `0x0050f460`, read `0x0050f720`): the round's ghost (16 bits),
  the nearest ghosted ancestor of the hit part's root (16, 0 none;
  `0x0050f3b0`) and with one the networkable index under it (8,
  `0x0050f340`) and the RotationalBundle index along the way down (8,
  `0x006f1ff0`), the thrower's player id (8, 0xff none), and a 3x4
  matrix as four rows written +0x2c, +0x0c, +0x1c, +0x3c: its place in the
  bundle's frame with a parent, its world matrix without; a joining client
  gets one for each round with a parent (ServerConnection `0x0057dda0`).
  The client (`0x0050f5d0`) stops its physics and places it (`0x005b3080`
  in the bundle, `0x005b30a0` in the world), and the thrower's own client
  hands it to his firearm (0x94c0 slot 0x16c). The rewrite
  (`HostedGame::stickyEvent`, `net::StickyProjectileInfo`,
  `RemoteWorld::stuckProjectile`, `GameWorld::stickRemoteProjectile`):
  the vehicle's root ghost, part 0, bundle 0 (its rounds ride the whole
  vehicle), up along the face's normal, facing as thrown; the client's
  round ignores the ghost's updates from then and rides the client's
  object of that ghost (`rideStuck` on the object's place without a body);
  the thrower's firearm list isn't kept on a client (the server sets C4
  off). The rewrite
  (`GameWorld::stickProjectile`, `rideStuck`; `Projectile::stuck`,
  `stuckTo`, `stuckNormal`): a stuck round lies at the contact and rides
  the vehicle's body (the whole vehicle: the rewrite doesn't pick the
  turret's bundle); the vehicle gone, it falls again (the engine's case
  isn't traced). A round only lying on a vehicle (not stuck: the mines
  have stickToVehicles 0) falls again once the vehicle moves from under
  it (`Projectile::lyingOn`: the rewrite's rounds are points, not the
  engine's ResponsePhysics bodies resting in contact with the hull). The
  engine's place along the normal (a constant `*0x00a6fe94`, or the
  geometry's lowest y, plus a dot product) is 0.01 m here. Placed hubs,
  beacons and shields aren't thrown in the rewrite (set down a metre
  ahead), so their stick flags have nothing to act on.
- **Radar sources** (the Ability component, template class `0xc4b2`,
  constructor `0x00631790`: showPlayers `+0x13` 1, showVehicles `+0x14`
  1, radialRadar `+0x15` 1, radarRadius `+0x18` 0, hasZoomUpgradeAbility
  `+0x54` 0; read through the runtime component `0x00656640`'s block,

  (`0x00656550` → `0x00a79ff8`; out by `0x006565e0`) when created: no
  arming, rest or age test. Nothing else reads the radar fields: no server
  scan and nothing networked. Each client's minimap (`0x0078f680`, every
  5th frame `0x00789f30`) keeps those of the local player's team (the
  shooter's root's team) within max(view distance, 500) m of his control
  object (`0x00789a10`), draws them (`0x0078f060`) and tests enemies
  against the ring (`0x007926c0` from `0x00792980` soldiers on foot, alive,
  not man-down, with showPlayers; `0x00793b60` vehicles with a living
  occupant, with showVehicles; none with alwaysShowOnMinimap or without
  canBeSpotted): within the radius across the ground and, radial, the
  sweep within 0.1 rad of the bearing, else the growing ring
  (radius × sweep / 2π) within 2.5 m (`0x00791660`); a hit is a blip
  (`0x00790d60`) and HUD_Uav_target. The sweep turns 4 rad/s (`0x00788600`).
  Shipped: unl_sonar 100 m, rings, vehicles only (showPlayers 0);
  Bp1_sonar and the radar grenade 40 m, soldiers only; the recon drone's
  rounds 65 m with both 0 (a ring without blips; its reveals are the

  The rewrite: `ProjectileSettings::radarRadius` and its flags,

  yaw bundle's; the pitch is the look's own).

Squad leader drones: the recon and sentry drones' detonators
(`Unl_Drone_Recon_Detonator`, `Unl_Drone_Sentry_Detonator`, slot 8) fire a
`PlayerControlObject` (`unl_drone_recon`, `unl_drone_sentry`: 120 hit
points, `takesEmpDamage`) that carries a `ForceObject` child. The drone
starts at the detonator's `fire.projectileStartPosition` (1/1.75/1 from the
feet) and leaves at its `velocity` (5 m/s). Each owner has one drone
(`maxProjectilesInWorld` 1), and the detonator's `ParentTargetComp` makes
the owner the drone's target. The detonators have `ammo.nrOfMags -1`,
which means magazines without end.

The ForceObject template (class `0x9489`, created by `0x0053fd17`,
constructor `0x0062d4f0`, properties registered from `0x00547519`, saved
by `0x0062add0`) creates a runtime object of `0x1f0` bytes (`0x0062d4c0`,
constructor `0x0062cd10`). Its tick (`0x0062c920`, then `0x0062b750`)
works like this:

- The target is lost (the owner is dead or gone): with
  `destroyWhenTargetLost` (template `0x295`) the drone is destroyed.
- Across the ground, the goal is the point `positionToleranceXZ`
  (`0x2a0`, 1.5 m) short of the target. When the drone is that near
  already, the goal is where it is. In height, the goal is the target's
  height, taken again only while the target is more than
  `minHeightAdjustDistance` (`0x2ac`, 0.7 m) off across the ground (kept
  at `0x1a8`).
