- **BBPHeliFire3d** (0x1007f9d0 / 0x1007f180): to the target (margin 25)
  until within 30 m, then attack runs: away to 150 m (margin 40) and back
  (margin 50); on the way back, 20 m to maxRange ahead (dot over 0.5) with
  the line clear, HeliAimAt (0x100e5590: margin 40; too steep, fly on
  150 m; lined up within 10° turning under 0.1 rad/s, the nose follows the
  aim with a feed-forward) and the trigger every 60 / round((1 − (1 −
  skill) 0.8) round(1.5 rpm)) s. The runs only inside the combat area:
  the plan's If (0x100d29f0) on 0x100dd3e0 (type 9; its 150 at +8 is
  never read), which asks IAITerrain slot 0x1c (BF2142.exe 0x008a0380 →
  the combat area manager's 0x004ca5d0: the areas that apply to the
  player, 0x004d9d50 — its team or none on either side, binding its
  controlled object's vehicleCategory — inside a plain one and in no
  cut-out; with none, the heightmap's bounds), else HeliMoveToObject at
  the target, margin 25 (`GameWorld::insideCombatArea`). HeliAimAt's aim
  is the ballistic lead (below) from the gun along the hull, the hull's
  motion inherited (an indirect weapon: precision 0.75, none inherited,
  the direction laid flat), else straight at the target (the aim's slot
  8); the trigger's condition is the on-target test (0x1007ec50 builds it
  with the AI weapon's allowedDeviation and its fire mode).
- **BBFire3d** (behaviour vtable 0x10116d40 slot 9, 0x1007e1b0; the score
  0x1007d6c0; `BotManager::fire3dUrgency`): over the known targets, each
  `facing × reach × 0.5 × temperature × motion × freshness × strength ×
  recency` (the factors in Bots.cpp: the vehicle's best weapon strength,
  1.5 − 0.5 clamp(t/30) after the target hurt the bot, 1/(0.05 t + 1) once
  lost, the target's motion against the bot's (none for an air target
  over 5 m up without anti-air guns), 20 a vehicle and 1 a soldier × 0.75
  outside the order's area, 1 − d/(3 maxRange), or for an air target
  1 − d/(1.5 maxRange) with the temperature doubled by anti-air guns,
  max(0.5, 1 + facing)); the target kept unless another scores 1.2 times
  more; urgency fuzzy(2 best) × weight. A target whose units (the
  vehicle's root and seats, 0x100a8cb0's walk) sum battle strengths (the
  Unit part's +8, capability scaled) against the bot's own type (its
  Physical's slot 0x40) of 1 or less scores × 0.01 (against the bot's
  +0x24, 0x100d2b30, which is 1 for every bot, 0x1009ac30): a gunship's
  soldiers with rifles (battle strength 0 against Helicopter) count for
  little (`fire3dUnitScale`). An enemy aircraft whose bot pilot targets
  this bot (slot 0x74 against 0xa8) is passed over. When the current
  target isn't among the memory's items, a second loop weighs the manned
  enemy units the side knows within 75 m (600 m for an ITAir bot: the
  information environment's slot 0x18, 0x100caab0 with −1, filtered by
  0x100ca960 and 0x100d3530) at a freshness of 1; the one chosen enters
  the bot's memory as known from others. The "20 s a failed target is
  passed over" (+0x30) never happens: the map's only accessor
  (0x1007df70; BBFire's 0x10075ec0 the same) makes a missing stamp at
  −10000 and nothing writes one; every 60 s dead entries are purged.
  Left out: the Unit's capability flags (0x100cf5c0/a0, bot vt+0x180).
- **BBChangeLandingCraft** (vtable 0x10116970, AIDLL 0x1006f460; the transport
  helicopters' pilots and their ParatrooperFixed passengers;
  `BotManager::landingCraftUrgency`): the vehicle's seats weighed as
  BBChange weighs them (0x100d3e70) × 1 for the bot's own when it drives or
  the driver's seat is taken (else 0.25), × 1.5 for a passenger looking at
  an ITAir root's driver's seat, × 0.25 for the others; a free driver's
  seat of a Mobile root + 100. Near the order (the order's spot within
  15 m, 50 m in an enemy area: 0x100bf800 with 225/2500) a driven
  transport says bail_out (0x100a7860: type 0, the AI's channel 7) and one
  with nobody at the controls (0x1006f3c0) lets its passengers out within
  10 m (40 m), urgency 4. Otherwise a better seat: fuzzy(best / current /
  2) × 4, × 6 within 15 s of taking the seat, 0 for a seat another bot
  reserved (0x1006f320). Not followed: the ground transports' way out (no
  shipped ground vehicle runs it). Decoded as far as: a root that isn't
  ITAir takes it when its Physical part's slot 0x64 holds and slot 0x5c
  gives a point, its Mobile speed (slot 0x24) is under 2 and the bot
  stands within 4 m of the Mobile's +0x10 point (0x1006f460); those
  adaptor slots weren't traced into BF2142.exe.
- **The ballistic lead** (`src/AI/Ballistics`, `ai::LeadSolver`; the
  solver record 0x100f9fd0, set up by 0x100fa060, solved by 0x100fa6f0):
  every aim that leads (the turret and soldier aim at an object 0x100d9a60,
  HeliAimAt's 0x100dcf10, the aim at a position 0x100dd6a0) solves for the
  launch angle in the vertical plane through where the target will be.
  The round: the muzzle speed (the AI weapon template's +0x28, the
  firearm's velocity), the drag (+0x14: the projectile's drag over its
  mass × π/100 for a Point or RotationalPoint, 0.3 for a Mesh with any)
  and the gravity (IAIPhysics slot 4 × the projectile's gravityModifier,
  +0x2c), all filled by 0x00892be0 through 0x0088a8c0; indirect (+0,
  weaponTemplate.indirect) asks for the high arc. The first guess of the
  flight time is the distance over the closing speed (the muzzle speed plus
  the shooter's motion less the target's along the line; under 1 m/s no
  solution). The search starts from the last solve's angle (the record
  keeps it, 666 at first: straight at the target), the high arc from
  3π/8 and pulled halfway to 1.508 rad each solve with the step reversed;
  each of round(8 p + 2) iterations (p 0.5 at the aims: 6) computes the
  flight time to the target's distance (with drag, 0x100fa100, in the AI
  clock's 1/30 s steps, quadratic over 200 m/s), the round's height there
  (0x100fa200) and the target's new place at that time, and moves the
  angle by its step towards the target; once the target is bracketed the
  step halves each time. A search that never brackets doubles the step
  (up to 0.017 rad upwards) for the next solve, and with a step of a
  degree or more succeeds without a new direction (0x1008e940 then aims
  along its zeroed local; the rewrite keeps the straight line). Over 60 s
  of flight it starts again straight at the first guess; over 100 s, an
  angle past ±2.98 rad, a speed along the ground under 0.1 m/s or a
  non-finite point: no solution. The record's +0x68..+0x6a, which would
  pin the time or drop the point, are never set.
- **The on-target test** (0x100dcab0 / 0x100dcb00, vtable 0x1011b048;
  `ai::OnTargetTest`): with a solution, the gun's forward within
  atan(0.0125 d) of its direction, and a round fired now along the gun
  (0x100fbad0 → 0x100fa680) within d of the solution's impact point at its
  flight time, d the AI weapon's allowedDeviation (slot 0x94 → 0x008926f0,
  the template's +0x44, 0.5 by default; the plain fire statement 0x1007fec0
  passes its own). A weapon that isn't automatic (slot 0x104 → 0x00892650:
  the fire mode isn't 2) waits for the closest approach: while the miss
  shrinks it holds; the test after it grows holds when the best was
  within d.
- **Measured** (flat ground, `Vehicles_BotPilotsFlyToAPointAndHover`):
  the gunships fly 156 m to a point 25 m up and stop on it within 1 m; the
  transports reach it (1.5 m) from 22 m/s and wander round it within 35 m
  (they brake only within 20 m). In a round (minsk_coop gpm_coop 32, 31
  bots, 300 s) a PAC bot flew as_ag 2.2 km: 10 s on its pad, a climb to 25
  m over the ground, the flight to its order, hovering, attack runs.

### Seat values (0x100d3e70) and Change

A seat's value is health × (k × weapons + move), k 2 for a vehicle seat
with an Armament plug-in, else 1:

- **Refused (0):** a seat another bot reserved (+0x2c/+0x30); with
  `other`, one whose driver's seat is taken; a vehicle whose Unit team is
  not 0 or the bot's; below 0.3 health (AIMain +0xdc; × 0.3 for the
  vehicle the bot drives); the root seat of a non-ITAir vehicle a human
  of the bot's team got out of under 7 s ago (the unit component, vtable
  0x009d6af0, vt+0x60/+0x64 per team, −1000 at first, 0x008a1d70; set by
  the exit event 0x00894860 for players that aren't bots, player vt+0x68);
  more than 8 m over the terrain (not in the rewrite).
- **Weapons** (0x100d3b80): for each of the seat's guns (on foot the
  kit's), its strength against each object the bot knows (by its
  CombatStrengthType), plus at a vehicle seat with Mobile its eight
  strengths summed; then, not for the bot's own soldier and not 0, +4 for
  light armour, naval, helicopters and planes, +10 for heavy armour (+2
  and +5 with `setHasExposedSoldier`).
- **Move** (0x100d39a0) × 0.3, with a Mobile plug-in on the root: its
  maxSpeed × 0.5 × 1.5 at the root's seat; at another, × 5 behind a
  driver of the bot's squad, × 1 of its group, 0 without a driver.
- × 1.15 for the seat the bot reserved itself.
- **Transport** (0x100d3730, 0x1005d840): `orderClose` (the order's
  spot within its area), `transportClose` (the bot's or the vehicle's
  second position), and `threatened` (sensing +0x7c, 0x100ebdd0). Close:
  no move value; close and not in the area: no weapons either. The root
  seat stays close only when the order's spot is outside a capturable
  control point (area flag bit 16; capturable = not
  `unableToChangeTeam`, IAIGame vt+0x24 0x00895d90) or when threatened
  and unarmed.

Change (0x1006c520): the vehicles within 75 m (IAIInformationEnvironment
0x100ca9e0; one without Mobile within 75/√2 m), on the vehicle mesh, each
seat at its value × max(0, min(0.5, (R² − 0.8 d²) / R²) + 0.5), × 5 for a
soldier under a quarter of its health within 20 m. On foot the current
value is 1.2 × the soldier's own; in a vehicle 2 × the seat's (250 at the
driver's seat with others aboard), and the way out is the soldier's own
value, or 10000 for a wreck or a vehicle more than 4 m off the vehicle
mesh (0x100880e0), a test 0x1006c520 runs only for a bot object that
isn't ITAir (its flags' bit 1): a pilot stays in the air. A seat another
bot reserved is worth nothing to others, but not to the bot sitting in it
(the rewrite's reading: a passenger heading for the vehicle would
otherwise turn its driver out). The other seats' factor (0x1006b910): 1 with the
driver's seat taken; else, for a Mobile root that isn't ITNaval, 0.77 for
ITGround and 0.5 for ITAir. The AI flags are the template's
`aiTemplate.addType` bits (BF2142.exe 0x0088fbd0, 0x00882ff1): ITUnit 0,
ITAir 1, ITHelicopter 2, ITGround 3, ITNaval 4, ITControlpoint 5,
ITTransportation 6, ITMobile 7, ITStructure 8, ITSoldier 9 (also set
through 0x0088d070), ITObstructedView 10, ITNoTemperature 11, ITHasWreck
12, ITObstacle 13, ITHasCarHorn 14; ITBiological sets none.

In a vehicle the driver's current value is 2 × its seat's (250 with
others aboard); a passenger starts from the driver's seat as another's.
Unless it drives an ITAir root, the root's other seats follow × that
factor (1 for a passenger with the driver's seat taken), the passenger's
own seat as its current value (× 2); then the way out (see above). A seat
of the same vehicle is reached by pressing its select key
(`aiTemplatePlugIn.setSelectKey PIPositionSelectN`, 0x100aa5f0; the plan
0x1006dac0) and waiting to sit in it; seats are reserved one by one. Not
rewritten earlier as "the type-0/1 order multipliers": those are the radio
lists (the comm's +0xc, per type; read at their first message from a
human alive and not down). bail_out (0): in a vehicle the way out ×
modifier × 100 (`aiComm.addAIRadioMessage`'s modifier column, the
message's +8; 10 shipped), 10000 in an ITAir object, and no other
vehicle is weighed. get_in (1), on foot: a vehicle of the bot's team that
a sender rides (0x1006c080) × the modifier; when the first sender rides
the vehicle the bot already heads for, only that one counts, × 5. From a
vehicle the other vehicles are weighed as on foot (the own one left out)
unless the way out is already best, a bail_out is held, the bot's object
is ITAir or it is off the mesh; a driver of a Mobile root (and a soldier)
takes one with `setUseNoPathfindingToGetToObject` (Unit +0x15, the
bipods), one without Mobile, or one whose infantry-map spot lies within
the two radii; a passenger any. The choice of another vehicle gets out
and walks there.

**Getting in** (the plan 0x1006dac0, a soldier at a seat of a vehicle
with a Mobile part, without `setUseNoPathfindingToGetToObject`): While
(0x100d19c0) the seat isn't taken (NOT 0x100d4190, test 0x100d41c0: the
seat's Unit, 0x100aa530), a Parallel that ends with its first child
(0x100cde50 with 0; 0x10119a64's run 0x100cdca0) of MoveToObjectFinding
(0x100cff90) at the vehicle with no distance kept and Trigger (0x100d3110)
of PIUse (input 10, mask 0x400) whose start condition is ObjectDistance
(0x100d4480, run 0x100d4620: 3-D from the seat's object to the bot's)
within the vehicle's radius (its physical part's vt+0x28, the root's for
a seat without one) + the bot's + 1 m. The move's goal is the vehicle's
spot on the bot's map (its step 0x100d07a0 reads the root's Mobile record
through 0x100a4510), which the bot never reaches: it walks on into the
hull, pressing use, and the game's use key (BF2142.exe 0x004bb570 → the
entry search 0x005a98e0) lets it in once it stands within an entry
point's 3 m. The bot walks on while it presses: a bot that stopped at the
press distance stood outside every entry point. (The rewrite pressed
within 2.5 m of the origin across, which the hull's side keeps soldiers
from: bots stood about 3 m from it, pushing. The rewrite's choice on foot
is a vehicle, any seat: the root's object and radius.) The plan's other
statements (the req_pickup radio, the wait to be seated 0x100d4d30, the
target without a Mobile part walked to by MoveToFinding at the chosen
spot) are as before.

### Action plans

A BBP pattern builds its plan from statements (Parallel, Serial, PlanEnd,
If, Wait, While and the leaves: MoveTo, MoveToObject, AimAt, Trigger,
TriggerContinously, Sense, SoldierPose, ChangeWeapon, PlaceC4...; the
BAPStatementType names 0x1005b000, the conditions LookDeviation,
ObjectDistance, WeaponReadyToFire... 0x10058ab0), and the bot's
interpreter runs the leaves with the implementations its equipment type
lists (`aiSettings.addInterpreterEntry <equipment> <statement>`,
0x10029e10; the implementations by name, registered by the AI object's
constructor 0x1002a400: TankMoveTo, CarMoveTo, MechMoveTo,
FloatingTankMoveTo, InfanteryMoveTo, HeliMoveTo..., the sensing patterns
Turret, MouseFreeLook, Soldier, Null). The rewrite doesn't build statement
objects: each pattern is code running the same statements in the same
order (BotManager::fire, flee, assist...), and the leaves are its
functions (ai::driveControl, aim, the path follower). The interpreter's
table is read (`BotSettings::moveInterpreter`: the MoveTo statement an
equipment type lists picks its driver). Rewriting the patterns as trees
for an interpreter would change no behaviour (the trees are fixed per
pattern; no script builds plans) and was not done. The plan printers
(0x10059000 the statement names, 0x100a4aa0, BotPlans.cpp's 0x100c65e0
for `ai.writeBotPlans`) are debug output.

### AIDLL's console and scripted bots (src/Game/BotsScript.cpp)

AIDLL registers 282 console commands from its static initialisers
(0x10100000..): each is an object whose constructor names it, its class
(the `FUN_100fde20` calls: AutoControllerTemplate, AI, aiSettings,
AIBotManager, aiStrategy, AIStrategicArea, AILandingZone, AIPathFinding,
AIDebug, AIRandom; the console's names are case-insensitive) and its
argument types, with a parser per argument (slots 24..) and an execute
slot (23). The weapon, kit and AI templates (`weaponTemplate.*`,
`kitTemplate.*`, `aiTemplate*`, `aiPathfinding.setActiveMap`,
`aiPathfinding.map.*`) are BF2142.exe's, not these.

- **The settings object** (AISettings, constructor 0x10051aa0; the
  interface IAISettings, vtbl 0x101148c8, and IAISettingsModifier, vtbl
  0x10114828, of one object, registered by AIDLL 0x100c4910): the
  `aiSettings.*` setters write it through the modifier slots
  (maxBots +8 by slot 0 0x1008b9d0, auto controllers +0xc 0x1004f410,
  maxBotsIncludeHumans +0x37 0x1004f420, ignoreCommanderDistance +0x38
  (30) 0x1004f430, the behaviour count +0x10 0x1004f3d0 (and
  DAT_10139520, 0x10096940), the view distance +0x1c 0x1004f460, the
  stats view distance +0x20 (300) 0x1005ccd0, the information grid +0x2c
  (32) 0x1004f4d0, the sides +0x30 0x1004f4f0, the skill 0x10051d10, the
  SAI's gate +0x28 (35 s) 0x100d7ec0, respawn +0x34 0x1003c2c0, the
  vehicle records 0x10051050 and cluster mappings 0x10050030, autoSpawn
  +0x36 0x1004f660, the man-down equipment +0x40 0x1004f690, the menu
  override +0x184 0x1004f6b0, the side's personality 0x100509d0) and the
  game reads them through the interface (maxBots 0x1004f380 and with the
  auto controllers 0x1004f390, 0x1004f3a0, 0x1004f3b0, 0x1004f3c0,
  0x1004f450, 0x1004f4e0, 0x1004fc00, 0x1004fc20, 0x1004ffa0). The
  rewrite's `BotSettings` holds them; the scheduling and skill are used,
  the rest is kept.
- **Bot names** (`aiSettings.addBotName <first> <last>`, 0x10050720):
  "first last" goes into the list by a random key, U[0, 0.4) for the
  first six names and U[0, 1) after, so those six tend to lead. The game
  names a bot it adds without a name (BF2142.exe's AI player factory
  0x0089e7a0 → IAISettings slot 0xc4, 0x10050a20): the head, which goes to
  the back. `bf2142 --bots` names its bots so (BotNames.ai's 100 names).
  The keys' U[0, 1) is a fixed sequence here.
- **Scheduling** (`aiBotManager.*`, the bot manager's second vtable
  0x101196b0): the thresholds (+0x6c, +0x74, absolute: 0x100c5cf0,
  AIDLL 0x100c5d10) and interleave (+0x60, +0x64: 0x100c5d30) feed the think
  queue (see Scheduling; 0x100c95f0 takes max(0, planned − planned
  waiting) + unplanned unplanned bots); the sensing and system quotients
  (0x100c5d50, 0x100c5da0) are shares of the real-time budget, kept.
- **Auto controllers** (`autoControllerTemplate.*`, the template
  0x100a8ed0 of 0x3c bytes, made by 0x10034320): sendFireWarning +0,
  operatesAlone +1, scanningSpeed +4 (0.03), accuracy +8 (0.5), fov +0xc
  (20°; the sensing agent 0x100ed700 makes an auto controller's frustum
  (0x100feea0) of it in degrees, its reach viewDistance / cos(fov / 2)), viewDistance
  +0x10 (30), useSiren +0x14, reactionTime +0x18, targetLostTimeout
  +0x1c, neverAttackDeployer +0x20, reportEnemiesToTeam +0x21,
  allowTakeOver +0x22, maxTrackingInput +0x24 (4), checkLineOfFire +0x28,
  discoverCloakedEnemiesDistance +0x2c, flipOutAtHealth +0x30,
  scanningInputScale +0x34 (1), reloadOnTeamChange +0x38,
  onlyAttackNetworkBattlefieldObjects +0x39, simpleFirePlan +0x3a. The
  sentry drone and the silos (GameWorld, Titans) use the shipped
  UAVDrone and CP_CANNON values, which `BotSettings::autoController`
  holds. AutoControllers.ai's `scanningSpeedWhenFlippingOut` is no
  command.
- **Not commands:** the shipped AIDefault.ai's `aiSettings.setAutoSpawnBots`
  (AIDLL's is `aiSettings.autoSpawnBots`), so autoSpawn stays off.
- **Scripted bots** (`ai.*`): `botMoveTo <radius> <x/y/z> <bot>`
  (0x100284a0), `botFlyTo <bot> <radius> <height> <unused> <x/y/z>`
  (0x100285a0, ITAir only), `botSetWaypoints_Patrol <bot> <radius>
  <count> <p1> [<p2> <p3>]` (0x10028680) and `botSetWaypoints_Patrol3d`
  (0x10028790) give the bot (the bot manager's slot 7, 0x100c6c80, by
  player id) a goal object (vt+0x38; see Goals below) that its MoveTo, or a
  pilot's GotoWaypoint3d, follows in place of the SAI's orders. In the
  rewrite a goal lasts until it is done (a waypoint goal reached) or the
  bot dies; the original's next SAI order would replace it.
  `deactivateBot` (AIMain's slot 5, 0x10055f80: out of the SAI and the
  bot manager) and `updateBot` (0x10026f30, the bot's vt+0x24) act on
  the running `BotManager` (`attach`). `addBot <name> <team> ...`
  (0x10005bc0) adds a bot player; `addUnspawnedBot` (0x10028d70) does
  nothing and answers −1. `ai.init` (0x10004dc0) marks the level's AI.
- **Goals** (src/AI/Goals; the vtables' slot 1 urgency, slot 2 the head,
  slot 3 the kind): waypoints (kind 1, vtbl 0x1011747c, constructor
  0x1008ae90: reach `radius`, done within max(ceil(radius), bot radius +
  1), 0x1008aaa0), patrol (kind 2, 0x10117520, 0x1008b560: reach at least
  5; urgency 1, the head to the back within the reach horizontally,
  0x1008b6c0), fly (kind 6, 0x101174b8, 0x1008b450: horizontal and
  vertical reaches; with several points the head is passed within both
  or once the bot is farther from it than at the last look, 0x1008b230),
  patrol 3d (kind 7, 0x10117560, 0x1008b7d0: urgency 1, the head to the
  back within the reach and when |y − head.x| < 10, 0x1008b920: the
  original compares the bot's height with the point's x, kept). Slot 4
  (0x1008a9a0, 0x1008a9b0) suspends a goal.
- **Strategic areas** of their own (`aiStrategicArea.create <name>
  <x/z> <x/z> <height> <temperature>`, juneau and Strike_at_Karkand_Coop
  use them): kept with their box and per-side takeable flags (`setTakeable
  <side> <0|1>`, +399 + side, 0x1001ab30) and the SAI's status rule for
  them (0x1005f210 with +0x164 −1: with units there, the side's own alone
  make it Owned when it is takeable for the side, the enemy's alone make
  it Hostile when takeable for the enemy, else the status stays;
  `ai::boxAreaStatus`, `Bots_BoxAreaStatusRule`). The status, counted over
  the units the side knows in the box, feeds the neighbours' flags; the
  SAI still orders units only to control point areas, and the starting
  status is taken as neutral (the area's constructor wasn't traced).

### Squads (src/Game/BotsSquad.cpp, src/AI/Formation)

AIDLL's squad object (0x110 bytes, 0x100c4080; reset 0x100c1700,
destructor 0x100c38f0) is the game's squad seen by the AI: its members
(0x70-byte member objects, 0x100bf550), the game's leader among them
(0x100c34d0), its spot (the leader's, 0x100c32b0), the order and a
formation. The squad manager (0x1008a720) makes nine a side up front
(IAIGame slot 0x50, BF2142.exe 0x00895850: 10); each AIMain frame
(0x1008a910) updates one squad of one side, the sides taking turns: a
squad every 18 frames.

- **Orders** (state +0x98: 0 none, 1 taken, 2 under way; kind +0x38: 0
  attack, 1 defend, 2 move, 4 none). The game's order event (0x10089480;
  here a change of `BotManager::squadOrder`) reaches 0x100c1eb0: a
  commander's order (the SAI's are) is taken only by a squad with none,
  and without a human commander only while no member stands within 30 m
  (+0x50 900) of the old order's spot in an area the side doesn't hold
  (0x100c1e50 / 0x100bf780): state 1 for 10 s. A squad leader's own order
  hands the formation's lead to a human leader (0x100f52d0). The leader
  (or the member asking) accepts it in its member update (0x100c21b0):
  without a human commander an attack on a held area is dropped; an area
  whose radius (+ `aiSettings.setIgnoreCommanderDistance`, IAISettings
  slot 0x10, 30) holds the spot and isn't the side's takes the area's
  position (the area lookup 0x100349b0: the most radius / max(1, d²),
  slot 0x68); else a spot within 30 m on the mesh (0x100c14a0: the spot,
  then 8 tries ±30 m); none: the bot says negative (7) to the commander
  (channel 4, 2 s) and the order goes. Accepted: a bot leader says
  roger_that (6, channel 4, 2.5 s) to a human commander and
  attack_position (16) / defend (15) / move (17) to the squad (channel 3,
  2 s); the game's order is accepted for it (IBFSquad 0x28; 0x2c
  refuses), and the bot leader orders its squad in the game: IBFSquad
  0x1c / 0x24 / 0x20 by kind (BF2142.exe's adaptor, vtable 0x009d65a0:
  0x008968d0 / 0x00896910 / 0x008968f0 → 0x00896830 → the squad
  manager's slot 0x48, SquadLeader.sendOrder) a map attack (5), defend
  (6) or move (4) at the order's spot: the squad leader's order marker
  its members' HUD shows. Every member re-goals.
- **The SAI's orders stay in AIDLL**: AIDLL never calls IBFCommander's
  order slots (3..5, 0x008971c0 / 0x008971e0 / 0x00897200 → the squad
  manager's slot 0x4c, the commander's order), so without a human
  commander no commander order exists in the game and no player sees one
  (`BotManager::Side::orders`, read with the human commander's through
  `BotManager::squadOrder`). A human member of a bot-led squad sees its
  leader's order; a human leader sees none. A squad leader's own order
  reaches the squad as the event with its flag 0 (0x10089480 reading
  the game's leader order, slot 0x50).
- **Ending:** an attack ends once the side holds the area; a defence of a
  held area while the enemy holds an area whose point can change hands
  (0x1009c660 over IAIGame slot 0x24, 0x00895d90). The SAI letting go of
  an area (0x100893c0, on reassignment and strategy changes) drops its
  squads' orders unless a member is near the spot; a human commander
  leaving drops every order of the side (0x1009bcd0 → 0x10089440). A new
  leader drops the order unless a human commands and the leader is a bot.
- **Formation** (+0x7c, 0x100f67d0): six slots (IAIGame slot 0x54,
  0x008c0360), slot 0 the leader's. A member is in it (0x100bf950) while
  alive, up and on foot, but not within 30 m of the spot of an order under
  way (it heads for the order then). Slots are taken in order (0x100f5760)
  and given up with the last moving into the hole (0x100f64a0: the
  leader's hole takes the bot nearest the order's spot, whose own hole the
  last used slot fills in turn, and the trail starts again, 0x100f6020;
  the earlier rewrite left that second hole, so a member respawning took
  slot 0 at its spawn and drew the squad back to its base). A move copies
  the used flag, member, trail point and lag (+0, +4, +0x14, +0x18, +0x1c)
  and never the parent (+0x20); the offset (+8..+0x10) only into the
  leader's hole and the second move, so a hole past slot 0 keeps its own
  place until the next layout (the earlier rewrite copied the whole slot,
  and a leader's hole took its donor's parent and with it a side offset).
  The member moved in is re-goaled (0x100bf4e0(0): +0x35 0, +0x4e 1). A
  member leaving re-hands them in member order (0x100f57f0). The shape (+0x14, 0x100f58c0)
  is 0 always (only the constructor and the update's third tick write it):
  a line abreast, slots 1 / 2 right and left of slot 0, 3 / 4 off them, 5
  off 3, each 3 (r + r') from its parent (0x100f53a0; the wedge and
  echelons 0x100f54c0 / 0x100f55f0 are unused), turned to the leader's
  walk (+0x34, 0x100f51f0, over 0.5 m/s; 0x100f5c70: x' = z side + x
  ahead, z' = -x side + z ahead). A slot off the mesh or on cost class 4
  (0x100c0ff0) takes a trail point (0x100f4d30: dropped every 6 m the
  leader goes; 0x100f5950, 0x100f6c10), else the order's spot or slot 0's
  member. Slots are swapped to the nearest placed member (0x100f69a0 over
  0x100f63b0; member and lag swapped by 0x100f4eb0, nobody re-goaled).
  Slot 0 and the game's leader (0x100f60a0): without a human's order
  (+0x58) a leader in a slot past 0 swaps into it unless 50 m or more from
  the spot and not released (+0x59), the leader and the member moved out
  re-goaled; under a human's order the leader in slot 0 swaps with the
  last used slot (a member leads; it stays put once past 0); a leader
  with no slot gets slot 0 for a member of its kind (bot or human) when a
  member of the other kind holds it. Each swap clears both lags and starts
  the trail again (0x100f6020; the earlier rewrite skipped the whole step
  under a human's order and re-goaled the wrong member). Every sixth
  update the offsets are laid out again with the members' radii (the
  soldier's AI radius 1.149 m: 6.89 m between neighbours, slots 1..5 at
  +6.9, -6.9, +13.8, -13.8, +20.7 m across the walk). No shipped .ai file
  (AI/*.ai, the levels' ai/ folders) sets anything of the formation's.
- **Lagging** (0x100f4f30): a human member past slot 0 whose slot time
  (member +0x20, read through 0x1004f4e0: the squared distance to its slot
  over its top speed, 5 for a soldier; 0x100c0890 writes it for every
  member with a slot, humans too) lies in (150, 1500) — about 27..87 m
  off — and who stands farther from the order's spot than the squad's
  spot lags for 10 + 10 U s (+0x18, +0x1c): the formation isn't together
  (+0x28) and the leader walks at its own speed. Once over, the slot stays
  timed and doesn't lag again until a test clears it (a bot, the human
  leader a human leads by, a member not placed, out of the band or no
  longer behind). Bots never lag. (`BotManager::updateFormation`.)
- **A member's map:** the squad's goals are drawn and tested on the map
  of the object the bot controls (the reachability test 0x100c1300 asks
  its Mobile part's map, 0x100a4330), so a member that took or left a
  driver's seat isn't left with the other map's goal: the rewrite's
  `updateGoal` kept a member's goal while its squad had no order under
  way, and an infantry goal off the vehicle mesh fails every path request
  (0x100966c0); Suez's PAC tanks stood at their spawn for the round.
- **Members** (0x100c0bb0): every 9 s a goal unchanged since the last look
  is given again when the bot's goal reads reached (urgency below 0.5) or
  it stands still over 4 m from it. In the formation the leader goes to
  the order (0x100c0130, the SAI goal path of `updateGoal`) at the squad's
  speed (the slowest member's x 0.9, 0x100f5120, read by InfanteryMoveTo's
  throttle 0x100e6060; only with an order under way and the formation
  together: otherwise the leader walks at its own speed, and it never
  waits for anyone), the others to their slot by a waypoint goal (reach
  0, area 60, 0x100bff90) when re-goaled (+0x4e) or at every look while
  +0x4d is set. +0x4d is the bot's Idle plan: the Idle statement
  (vtable 0x1011a2f8, made by BBPIdleInfantery 0x1006a500, BBPIdle3d
  0x1006ab50 and BBPIdle2d 0x1006b2f0) sets it through the bot's vt+0x134
  as it is made (0x100d2830, setter 0x100bf450) and clears it as it goes
  (0x100d28a0); a new member starts with it clear (0x100bf550) and the
  round's reset sets it (0x100bf640). A member that reached its slot
  point (the goal's reach is the bot's radius + 1, 2.15 m) idles, and
  idling it is handed the slot again at each look, so it follows the slot
  as the squad moves; one still walking keeps its goal until the 9 s
  look. (The earlier rewrite read +0x4d as set once by the reset and
  never cleared: the members present at the first squad update were
  handed their slot at every look for the whole round, the others only on
  re-goals.) Out of it a member heads for the order (0x100c0a90).
  Nothing else moves a member off its slot: the formation is kept whether
  or not the leader walks (+0x3c, 0x100f4c70, has no reader), in combat
  and on sighting an enemy; only the order's 30 m and leaving foot or
  life (0x100bf950), an event through 0x1004dfe0 (→ 0x100bf410, the slot
  given up) or leaving the squad (0x100c3630 / 0x100c36d0) takes a
  member out. `BotManager::formationGoal`. The slot goal is only MoveTo's: Fire's
  urgency (0x10075fb0, 50 with a known enemy that scores) reads neither
  the squad nor the hold (vt+0x128 / 0x12c), so a member fights what it
  sees wherever its slot is. Measured on Cerbere_Landing gpm_sp 16 (six
  seeds), members on foot that saw an enemy ran Fire 408 of 418 s
  (others 1,233 of 1,261 s); they see one about half as often (8 % of
  their time against 17 %), as they walk behind slot 0. Without the
  formation (every member heading for the order) the bots' kills rise
  from 11.5 to 19.4 a round over 50 seeds, and the leader at full speed
  instead of the squad's changes nothing (11.9). With the +0x4d and
  slot-move fixes (30 seeds, 300 s): 11.9 → 13.3 kills a round
  (minsk_coop gpm_coop 32: 2.2 → 3.0, within noise). With AIDLL's own twister, the commander's
  answers, slot 8's 4/3 and no flank spots (20 seeds, 300 s): 12.7 →
  13.1 kills a round (sd 2.8 / 3.0), within noise.
- **Mode** (0x100c4010 / 0x100c1940): bounding with two or more of the
  squad's bots fighting a soldier within 90 m (0x100c3af0, every 4 s:
  halves in turn, a bot facing its target over 40 m off holds); flanking
  for a commander's order 50..173 m off into an area the enemy holds
  (0x100c3390: once, 65 %, the area's two flank spots reachable would mark
  it and re-goal the leader). The hold (bot +400, vt+0x128) is read only
  by the look-around (0x100d7840 via vt+0x12c: a held bot looks along its
  walk). The flank spots are never found: 0x1005e820 takes the pair
  nearest the squad's spot from the area's list (+0x1c4 / +0x1c8, 0x20-byte
  nodes of two points), which nothing in 1.51 fills (written only by the
  area's constructors 0x1005ffe0 / 0x10062e10 and destructor, copied by
  0x1005f0d0 / 0x10061240, read by 0x1005e820 and the debug printer
  0x1002eff0). So the 65 % draw is made, +0xc0 stays clear and no leader
  is re-goaled; nothing reads +0xc8 either.
- **Danger list** (+0x14, pruned by 0x100c1b60: gone, timed out or moved
  5 m, re-goaling everyone): no writer was found among AIDLL's functions,
  so it stays empty. The repair marker (+0xd4, 0x100c0fa0, 60 s; the
  bridge repair) has no broken bridges to serve.
- **Radio:** req_new_order (14, channel 4, 1 s, every 20 s) from a bot
  leader near the spot of an attack or move with a human commander
  (0x100c30f0); a human leader's "followme" (12) answered roger_that by
  the first bot (channel 3) and the formation released; a bot leader under
  a human commander answers commend (18) thankyou (8), rebuke (19) and
  followorders (20) sorry (9), divide (21) negative (7), channel 4
  (0x100c2ee0).
- **Strike spots** (the squad manager's two records, +0x28 + 0x48 side):
  a commander's strike for a side (the AI commander's artillery,
  0x1009c050 → 0x10088040; a human commander's orbital strike or
  artillery through IAIEventCourier slot 0x5c, 0x1004e690, from
  BF2142.exe 0x007d7d80 / 0x007d88d0 as the tool is used; the rewrite
  takes each strike new in `GameWorld::strikes`) marks its spot at the
  terrain's height, the time, and how long the other side takes to learn
  of it, (U + 1) × 12.5 s; it forgets both sides' escape points. A spot
  goes 25 s on (+0xc0, 0x10088f20, first in the manager's update), and
  every member of every squad is given its goal again (0x100c1ca0). A bot
  member alive and up (0x100bfa70) within 40 m (+0xb8) of its side's
  spot, or of the other side's once that one's delay is over (0x100880e0),
  leaves it before anything else in its update (0x100bfcb0): from the
  spot through the bot at 45 m, a point on its map, five tries, the way
  turned about the vertical each time from the first by an angle a (0 at
  first) going 3a + 0.6 + 0.2U when a ≤ 0 and −a − 0.6 − 0.2U otherwise
  (0x100a82c0); none found, the point an earlier member of its side found
  for its kind (soldier or vehicle, 0x10088240), else it stays. It gets a
  waypoint goal there (0x1008aff0: reach 0, area 60), and +0x35 / +0x4f
  hold it until it is out of every spot; a point it searched out is kept
  for its side (0x10088310). `BotManager::noteStrike`, `escapeStrike`.
  (The earlier passes took 0x100bfcb0 for a vehicle pick: it is this.)
- **Population** (AIMain): see Respawn, kit and the bots' population.

### Look-around (src/Game/BotsLook.cpp)

The sensing agent (bot +0xdc, 0x100d7210; reset 0x100d6b90) decides where
a soldier looks when no plan aims; its update (0x100d7840) runs after the
main plan (0x1009a4c0). Any plan's aim (MouseTurretLookAt 0x1008e6e0,
MouseTurretAimAt 0x1008e940 → 0x100d51c0) pauses it for 2 s; each walk
step (InfanteryMoveTo → 0x1008f8e0) hands it the walk's way and clears
the pause's stamp.

- Eight world sectors (+z, +x, -z, -x, then +x+z, +x-z, -x-z, -x+z) with
  weights (+0x3c): faced ones (within ~10°, 0.9848) go to 0 at each
  sensing pass (0x100d6d60); at each choice those within 20° of the walk
  grow 0.05 (0.25 when the walk turned off the chosen look), the others
  0.0125 (0x100d6630).
- Stimuli into their cardinal and diagonal sectors, × the side's
  certainty: memory items (0x100d7400: not yet seen 0.3 heard + 0.25 the
  fire plan's target; seen first-hand 0.5; second-hand 0.25 targeted or
  heard) and the rounds that passed it (0x100d7590: an enemy's 0.7, 0.5
  after 5 s, at the shooter, forcing one re-decision; a friend's 0.5 at
  the impact). The heaviest sector wins with its stimuli's mean point;
  none above 0: a random one, round(U × 7) (0x100d60f0).
- The look lasts (0x100d5ad0): with no walk yet U(1.5, 2) s; walking,
  U(7, 10) s along the walk, U(1.5, 2) s aside; standing U(3, 4) s. Prone
  it looks about only when forced; a bot the squad holds (vt+0x12c) looks
  along its walk. A plan whose sector isn't chosen again is replaced
  (0x100d6300). The look (0x100d5ca0): a sector's way at the current
  pitch, or the stimulus's point; before the first walk step the
  GotoWaypoint plans' Turn (0x100d0fc0 → 0x100d58b0, weight 0.5) at the
  goal may win.
- The Soldier pattern's steering (0x100cd3b0) turns the walk into
  throttle and strafe against the look: clamp(sign(c)·√|c|) of its
  forward and side components (`BotManager::steer`). The sprint branch of
  0x100cd3b0 and the MouseFreeLook pattern (unused by the shipped sets)
  aren't rewritten.
- **Turret** (vtable 0x10117660; AIBehaviours.ai gives it to Tank, Mech,
  Fixed, ArmedCar and ParatrooperFixed): the same look statement (offset
  0x1008c120, at an object 0x1008c220) for the seat's controlled object
  when that has its ControlInfo (its AI part's +0x38), with no steering:
  the gun turns, by the seat's MouseTurretLookAt as a soldier's look does.
  The statement carries 5° (+0x1c, DAT_10127df0 × 5) where the Soldier's
  carries 0; the controller 0x100e5820 takes it as its fifth argument and
  never reads it. The faced sectors are the gun's. A turret's sectors are
  held to its yaw limits (0x100d5440 over the ControlInfo's BF2142.exe
  slots 0x4c / 0x54 / 0x60, not traced); the rewrite lets every sector
  through (the shipped tanks' and AA guns' turrets turn all round).
  `BotManager::turretLooks`.
- **Null** (vtable 0x101175b4, FloatingTank and ManDown): its plans
  (0x1008b9f0) are a statement that does nothing (0x100d1fe0(0, 1, 0)):
  no look of its own, as before.
- The 2d path look (0x100d2500, BBPGotoWaypoint2d when the seat's
  ControlInfo slot 0x38 holds, 0x100cf660; stand-in: a driver whose look
  turns the gun): along the path, the follower's point 20 m ahead, level.

### Respawn, kit and the bots' population

- **Respawn** (SAI step 4 0x100a1a80 → 0x100f0590, after the death hook
  0x100a1270; the game's timer decides when, the SAI where and with
  what; `BotManager::chooseRespawn`): 20 % of the time the last spawn
  point is kept while usable; else the chooser (0x100eff20): unless (U ≤
  0.3 and the leader is a bot), with the leader alive and up, the usable
  spawn point nearest the squad's spot on the mesh; else a roulette over
  the usable points by their area: max(1, (1 + 0.033 E) T − 0.1 D), T the
  area's temperature for the side, E the basicTemp of empty vehicles
  within 50 m, D the area's distance to the squad's spot. The kit
  (0x100f04a0): floor(U × 4), the four kits alike. Its unlocks
  (0x100efce0): for each of four unlock values, the most any human alive
  holds for that kit (the player's vt+0x98 of the kit and its vt+0x68(i),
  i = 0..3), + 1, at most 4; with no humans 1 each. The value compared is
  the human's owned mask for the branch (the adaptor's slot 38 → player
  slot 0x2ac, `0x005977e0`: the bits of the levels owned for the kit's
  unlockIndex, `+0x2c4`), so a human owning levels 0 and 1 (3) gives the
  bots 4. They go with the kit through the bot's player: vt+0xb0 is
  BF2142.exe's AI player adaptor (vtable `0x009d7650`, forwarding to the
  player at `+4`), whose slot 40 (`0x008a5b90`, kit, l0..l3) clears the
  kit's chosen unlocks (player slot 0x2c4, `0x005995f0`); a squad leader
  (player slot 0x150) with l3 > 0 has one UB_SquadLeader container of
  levels below l3 at random chosen (player slot 0x294, `0x00599630`: the
  chosen masks `+0x2cc`) and owned (slot 0x2b0, `0x00597850`: the owned
  masks `+0x2b4`); UB_Player level 0 is owned (its frag grenade applies
  by replaceWithoutEquip); with l0 > 0 the UB_First containers of levels
  below l0 and the UB_Second ones below l1 (each level's first of the
  branch, `0x0056fb20`) are pooled, an anti-air one (its firearm's AI
  weapon template's isAntiAirWeapon, `+0x71`, through the adaptor's slot
  39, `0x008a57b0`: the AV kit's eu_aa / as_aa) kept aside, two of the
  pool taken at random (floor((n − 0.001) U)), then the anti-air one on a
  coin toss when the AI's object environment answers slot 0x98(1) for an
  object (checked once, `0x00b4cb7d`; here: an air or helicopter vehicle
  on the map), which ends the choice. l2 isn't read. Slot 39 also leaves
  out a container whose first item has no item interface (`0xc49a`) or
  no aiTemplate (template `+0x1a0`; the abilities, HUD upgrades, mines,
  sonars and shields), and sends to a second pool one whose item's
  itemIndex (the item interface's slot 0x14, GenericFireArm's
  `0x00440dc0`, the template's `+0x2e0`) is the kit template's `+0x2c8`
  (3, set by the Kit constructor `0x00570080` and by no property: the
  primary's slot). Those are the primaries: the HAR, LAR, carbine, HMG,
  shotgun, AV rifle and advanced sniper rifle. When the anti-air one isn't
  taken, one of that pool at floor((n + 0.999) U) is, none when that comes
  out n (about half the time with one). Rewritten: `GameWorld::chooseBotUnlocks`,
  called by the respawn's kit choice (`BotManager::chooseRespawn`), the
  AI weapons' `weaponTemplate.isAntiAirWeapon` (`WeaponAi::antiAir`). The
  rewrite's choice is the point's control point
  (`GameWorld::setSpawnChoice`); the bots no longer spawn on their leader
  (the original's bots don't).
- **Bots outside squads** (steps 10 / 11, 0x100a0420 / 0x100a09c0): in
  turn to attack or to defend by the strategy's Aggression (all attack
  with no area held, all defend with every area held), A / (A + D) of the
  rounded strategic strengths kept to the share (`ai::assignsAttack`). In
  the shipped game every bot is in a squad, so this is bookkeeping (its
  release flags feed 0x100a21a0 / 0x100a2630 branches not decoded); the
  rewrite's bot outside squads takes its role's areas first. The release
  flags: step 11 sets +0x23d (attackers over their share × 1.2, unless
  the last bot dealt went to defence) and +0x23c (defenders over theirs ×
  1.2 when it did), both with +0x23e; step 10 (cleared +0x23e first)
  then releases every loner of the over-full kind from its areas
  (0x1009f740, setting +0x23e again). 0x100a21a0 (attacks) with +0x23c
  set and nothing released, and 0x100a2630 (defences) with +0x23d, sum
  the loners their chosen areas still need (0x10063060 / 0x10063080) and,
  with none, skip the pass that hands the areas out. With no loners
  (the shipped game) both tallies stay 0 and the flags clear, so none of
  this runs; the rewrite deals its loners afresh at each SAI update, which
  is what the releases correct for.
- **Population** (AIMain, vtable 0x10114d30): a new bot is refused once
  the active bots reach `aiSettings.setMaxNBots` (slot 30, 0x100581a0;
  `BotManager::refused`). A human joining (slot 7, 0x10056110) is
  counted (+0x100; a bot's join only counts, +0xfc); with
  maxBotsIncludeHumans (IAISettings slot 3, +0x37), bots about and the
  server's maximum (DAT_10139454 slot 4: here sv.maxPlayers,
  `BotManager::setServerMaxPlayers`) under humans + bots, one bot goes
  (IAIGameEffector slots 0x24 / 0x14): the last one in the player list of
  the team with more players, team 2 on a tie, the other team's when that
  one has none. A human leaving (slot 8, 0x10056d10) leaves its squad
  (0x10089860) and, with maxBotsIncludeHumans and bots + humans under the
  maximum, the fill (slot 20, 0x10056680) adds setMaxNBots less the humans
  less the bots, through the AI player factory (slot 0x18; here `addBot`
  on the side with fewer players), when autoSpawnBots (IAISettings slot
  40, +0x36) and the game's slot 0x5c hold. `aiSettings.autoSpawnBots` is
  a command (0x10011420); the shipped AIDefault.ai says
  `setAutoSpawnBots`, which isn't, so the fill doesn't run in the shipped
  game. `BotManager::population`.
- **Revives and team kills** (the bot manager's slots 15, 16 and 24,
  vtable 0x10119738, reached through IAIEventCourier 0x1004e620 /
  0x1004e130 / 0x1004e3e0 from BF2142.exe's AI event listener 0x00894860,
  category 3): event 6 is man down (0x100c5ea0: the bot's down flag
  +0x178, its path follower reset 0x100962a0); event 7 is the soldier's
  revive (the soldier's event 0x19, 0x00587b90, with the soldier and its
  player): 0x100c5f00 clears the flag, thinks at once, resets the path
  follower (0x10095120) and queues "thankyou" (8) on channel 6 in 1 s;
  the SAI's slot 15 (0x100a0f40) gives the squad member its goal again
  and redoes its area record (0x1009fdc0). Event 0xb is a team kill
  (0x005b7680: killer and victim of one team, the killer not the victim):
  0x100c60c0 has a killer bot that isn't scripted (vt+0x27c) say "sorry"
  (9) on channel 6 at once. The rewrite sees a bot come back from man down
  and a bot's teamKills grow.

### Mines on the navigation mesh (src/AI/MineZones, BotsMines.cpp)

IAIMineManager (vtable 0x101145f0): BF2142.exe registers every mine of
both teams (the AI event adaptor 0x0089f8d0 / 0x0089fdd0 → slot 0x14
0x100496f0; the rewrite takes the trigger-armed rounds) and takes it off
as it goes (slot 0x10 0x1004b880). Every 0.5 s (slot 3, 0x1004b640) a
resting mine gets its zone (0x1004ae90): a soldier mine a 7.5 m cone,
22.5° either side of its facing, flooded over the infantry mesh
(0x100b9200: on x/z, a vertex inside or an edge crossing, nothing 2 m
above or below); a vehicle mine (MTYVehicle: EMP, motion) a 9 m circle
(0x100b94d0) on the vehicle mesh and another on the infantry mesh. The
start polygon: under the mine, else along the facing a metre at a time,
or 15 random tries round it. The marks (0x10048230) count per polygon
(A for a zone's own mesh, B for the circle's second): a polygon's first
mark only makes its record; a later one finding that counter at 0 sets
its cost class to 7 (×1000, the pathfinder's slot 0x5c). So only
infantry polygons under both a cone and a circle turn 7 in the shipped
game, and nothing puts the class back when the mines go (the original
keeps no copy). Kept as the binary does it.

### Smaller behaviours

- **BBPIdle2d** (0x1006b2f0): the driver answers the passenger it waits
  for (BBIdle's 0x1006b1f0) when that one asked for a pickup
  (req_pickup 2, unanswered) within 40 m (a bot only while a seat is free):
  roger_that (6) on channel 6, 1 s.
- **The get-in plan** (0x1006dac0): walking to a vehicle whose driver's
  seat is taken (0x100d4190) and holding no get_in: req_pickup (2) to the
  driver, channel 6, once. Seated (0x100d4a90): out of the root's seat
  with a driver and no other seat reserved, gogogo (11); else, when
  someone aboard holds a get_in from it, thankyou (8): channel 7, 1 s.
- **Guided aim point** (0x100da710): the target's point; a soldier target
  over 1 m/s whose distance less the round's speed is under the round's
  distance is aimed lower by its pose (1.21 / 0.73 / 0.1 m); a wire-guided
  round 20 m past the target aims 10 m under it, else beyond 0.5 m of the
  target's distance at the point led by the target's x/z motion over the
  time to it at the closing speed, under 2.5 s. The aim leads no more.
- **The pilot's weapon** (0x100dd4a0): of the pilot seat's weapons, the
  strongest against the target's CombatStrengthType (above 0), the one in
  use counting twice.
- **The take-off wait** (0x100d1cb0, 10 s): it ends early with no soldier
  within 75 m (a human always counts, a bot while a seat is free).
- **Revive** (0x10082f10, 0x100dda20): within 1.6 m of the body the bot
  crouches; crouched, one press of the trigger, then its release.

- **Scheduling:** the CPU budgets are real time (see Scheduling: they
  depend on the machine's speed, so they can't be reproduced; every slice
  runs to its count, the SAI once a second). That holds for the path

  `0x100c6ee0` gives the bots waiting for a path (`+0xd9`, `+0x150`)

  tenth of the frame's budget, hands 0.9 of what is left to the
